coverage_notes:
I read ledger-walls.txt and both gpu-shading slices in full, and grepped ledger-compact, ledger-open, git log and url-flags.md for every candidate.

**Code read for this dimension:**
- **Terrain:** the assembled terrain fragment shader (dumped with a node probe through terrain.js `_terrainGlslForTest`, 3,032 lines) and far_terrain.js.
- **Materials:** materials.js POM, CSM, depth-bias and light-clamp patches; light_loops.js; static_atlas.js statPom; terrain_grass material.
- **Sky:** sky_glow.js, sky_dome.js sky-chain anchor, atmosphere_sky.js SkyMaterial, the takram AerialPerspective `mainImage`.
- **Clouds:** the vendored takram clouds build and src (qualityPresets, CloudsPass, ShadowPass, CloudsEffect.update, the march loops), plus cloud_volume.js and cloud_overlay.js.
- **Post chain:** atmosphere_pipeline.js pass list and split chain, layered_haze.js, ssao.js, fx_distort, fx_decal and fx_glow effects.
- **Other:** ibl_environment.js water cube.

**Main tool:** I fetched ANGLE's OutputHLSL.cpp and ASTMetadataHLSL.cpp to confirm how D3D11 translates gradient sampling inside loops: it adds FLATTEN to an `if` holding a gradient loop and samples at LOD0 inside discontinuous loops. Then I scanned every GLSL template in scene3d and vendor for implicit-gradient samples inside loops. The terrain is clean (gradUv uses textureGrad), statPom is clean, the SSAO and fx_distort loops only read mip-less depth, and the cloud march self-terminates under FLATTEN. The legacy POM patch is the one real hit.

**Checked and dropped:**
- **Precision (highp vs mediump):** ANGLE D3D11 compiles everything as fp32, so there is no gain on the 1070.
- **Sky drawn before the world:** SkyMaterial is a full-screen quad drawn ahead of the world pass. No pixel-identical reorder exists without splitting world transparents (additive sky glows would break), so I dropped it.
- **Other gl_FragDepth writers:** every one is log-depth guarded except sky_glow and the tiny punch/seal aperture passes.
- **Half-res SSAO depth:** not pixel-identical, because SSAO nearest-samples full-res depth at arbitrary offsets.
- **Clouds:** temporal upscale is already on; the remaining cloud knobs are quality trades.
- **Open lead #45 (water cube):** verified small, 128²×6 faces at 1 Hz.
- **Draw-count and statics-merge ideas:** skipped; walls 29/89/107/108 cover them.

**Walls that shaped the search:** wall 105 (CPU-bound frame) is superseded by the 10-19 picture (fill-bound at ultra). Walls 11 and 183 (clone drops onBeforeCompile) are reused as evidence for finding 2. Wall 101: nothing here was measured on the GPU, so every ms figure is derived or assumed.

**Limits:** no browser, build or full gate was run. The only execution was a light node probe to dump the terrain GLSL, plus python static scans in the scratchpad.

This dimension now looks largely mined. What remains is finding 1's dependency on lead #7 and pass and cadence amortisation.

findings.title: Legacy POM loops are compiled by ANGLE D3D11 as FLATTENed ifs with mip-0 height samples, so the march runs at every distance on the 1070
findings.evidence:
materials.js:1747-1763: `_pomPerturbedUv` samples `texture2D(uPomMap, …)` (implicit gradient) before, inside (1753) and after a `for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++)` loop. The loop exits through `if (i >= steps) break; if (currentLayerDepth >= currentHeight) break;` (1749).

materials.js:1781-1784: `_pomShadow` has the same shape (`for i<16`, `if (i >= sSteps) break`, `texture2D` in the body).

Call sites are inside runtime ifs:
- materials.js:1823 `if (_pomLod > 0.001) {` and 1834 `if (_pomGrazeW > 0.001) {` → 1836 `_pomPerturbedUv(...)`
- materials.js:1880 `if (_pomLodG > 0.001) {` → 1882-1883 hit-depth sample plus `_pomShadow(...)`

ANGLE source (google/angle main, fetched this session):
- OutputHLSL::visitIfElse: `// D3D errors when there is a gradient operation in a loop in an unflattened if. if (mShaderType == GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER && mCurrentFunctionMetadata->hasGradientLoop(node)) out << "FLATTEN ";`
- texture calls get `bool lod0 = (mInsideDiscontinuousLoop || mOutputLod0Function) && mShaderType == GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER`.
- ASTMetadataHLSL: `texture`/`texture2D` are gradient builtins. A call to a function with `mHasGradientLoopInCallGraph` marks the enclosing if (and its parents) as `mIfsContainingGradientLoop`. A `break` not directly in the loop body makes the loop discontinuous.

Result on the owner's ANGLE→D3D11 1070:
- (a) All three ifs are flattened. The march (nSteps up to 64 at grazing, quality.js:540 pomStepsPrimary 24) and the self-shadow (12, quality.js:541) execute for every fragment of every POM material, including beyond the 5-10 m fade (POM_UNIFORM_DEFAULTS lodNear/lodFar, materials.js:1597-1613) where `_pomAmt == 0` discards the result.
- (b) The in-loop samples become SampleLevel(…,0) on a mipmapped height map (adapter.js surfacePixelsToHeightTexture: LinearMipmapLinear, generateMipmaps). Distant fragments thrash the cache, and within 10 m the march compares mip-0 detail against a base sample taken at the proper mip.

statPom already avoids this by sampling through textureGrad with `_statUvGx/_statUvGy = dFdx/dFdy(vMapUv)` (static_atlas.js:635, 703).

Who reaches it today: entity parts (entities.js:5420 `materialCache.getCached(did, …)`), shared scene3d.materialCache with pomEnabled at mid+ (index.js:2167, statics.js:885), and non-atlased statics (statics.js:3126/3194/3971).

Invisible on the laptop (SwiftShader is not D3D).
findings.proposal:
Mirror statPom's convention in `_installPomShaderPatch`:
1. Add globals `vec2 _pomGx, _pomGy;`.
2. Set them unconditionally at the top of the patched <map_fragment> (`_pomGx = dFdx(vMapUv); _pomGy = dFdy(vMapUv);`), next to the already-unconditional getTangentFrame.
3. Replace all six `texture2D(uPomMap, X)` with `textureGrad(uPomMap, X, _pomGx, _pomGy)`.

With no implicit-gradient op left in a loop, ANGLE emits neither FLATTEN nor LOD0. The 10 m fade and graze gates become real dynamic branches, and the height reads use the base-UV mip, which is what GL backends approximate and the same rule statPom and terrainGradUv already ship.

Flag `?pomGrad` (proposed default ON after the eye check; `=off` restores the current text byte-for-byte). Bump nothing else; the program key changes with the source.

Optional follow-on: a one-shot D3D audit, `__diag.hlslAudit()`, that greps every live program's translated HLSL for FLATTEN and `lod0`, so this class is caught automatically.
findings.expected_gain:
Unmeasured.

Derived from code: on D3D every POM-material fragment beyond 10 m currently pays 1 + up to 64 + 1 + 1 + up to 12 height fetches (loop ones at mip 0) plus about 40 ALU. After the fix it pays a dynamic branch, and only fragments within 10 m pay at all.

Assumed: about 0.1-1 ms GPU in NPC-dense towns at ultra 1440p, since only entity parts and singleton statics carry the legacy patch today. It becomes multi-ms if lead #7 is fixed first (see gpu-shading-2).

It also removes a D3D-only mip-0 shimmer in the 5-10 m POM band.

findings.title: Open lead #7 confirmed on default flags: baked EnvCell walls, cell statics and building floors lose the POM patch; re-installing it must wait for gpu-shading-1
findings.evidence:
- **EnvCell walls:** cells.js:791-795 `cellMaterialFor` returns `mc.getCachedCellBaked(...)` when the cell is baked. vertexBake is ON when absent (materials.js:887-903, `return { enabled: true, suppressDirect: true }`). materials.js:4110-4122 does `v = base.clone(); … applyBakedVertexLightPatch(v, …)`.
- **Why the patch is lost:** three r184 `Material.copy` (node_modules/three/src/materials/Material.js:901-977) copies fields and `userData = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` but not `onBeforeCompile`. The baked patch then chains onto the prototype hook (materials.js:917 `_chainBeforeCompile`), so the POM patch installed on the base (materials.js:5296-5305) is gone, while `userData.pomEnabled` survives into the program key. `_CLONE_LOST_PATCH_FLAGS` (materials.js:3214-3218) already admits this.
- **Cell statics:** these use `getCachedStaticBias` (cells.js:2131-2134; CELL_STATIC_BIAS default on, cells.js:150-156) → materials.js:4158-4170, the same clone pattern.
- **Building floors:** `getCachedFloorBias` (buildings.js:897, materials.js:4078-4090), the same clone pattern.
- **Intent vs reality:** quality.js:324-331 says POM went on at mid precisely so 'EnvCell interiors … EVERY dungeon wall' are not flat. On default URLs no baked dungeon wall or cell prop runs any POM. They are also not atlas members, so statPom never covers them.
findings.proposal:
Re-install the POM patch on the three clone families, like makeOwnedVariant already re-installs CSM and light clamp: call `_installPomShaderPatch(v, heightTexForMaterial(v))` when the base had `pomEnabled`, after `_inheritHeightTex`.

Ship only after gpu-shading-1 lands. With today's texture2D-in-loop patch, ANGLE D3D11 would FLATTEN the march, so every dungeon wall at every distance would pay up to ~80 mip-0 height fetches per fragment.

Flag `?cellPom` (default per owner eye test; `=off` keeps today's flat walls).

Without it, the cost on dungeons is assumed to be several ms at 1440p (derived from the flattened per-fragment fetch count over full-screen walls).

findings.title: Sky-glow sheets write gl_FragDepth = far, which disables early-Z/Z-cull for nine kilometre-wide transparent quads every outdoor frame
findings.evidence:
sky_glow.js:180-191 SKY_GLOW_FRAGMENT_BODY ends with `#ifdef USE_REVERSED_DEPTH_BUFFER gl_FragDepth = 0.0; #else gl_FragDepth = 1.0; #endif`. applySkyGlowMaterial (sky_glow.js:222-232) sets `transparent`, `depthWrite=false`, `depthTest=true`, LessEqual (three flips it to GreaterEqual under reversed-Z).

The moon SkyObject's three Swarm emitters are nine ~2 km additive quads (sky_glow.js:5-16; sky_dome.js:557-566 anchor). They are patched on the instanced bucket (particle_manager.js:2958 `applySkyGlowMaterial(mat)`) with `im.frustumCulled = false` (2968), and stay in the MSAA world pass (`skyChain` is left behind the clouds).

A shader depth write disables early depth test and hierarchical Z for the draw. So every covered pixel is rasterised and shaded and only then rejected against terrain, buildings and trees, even though the result survives only where depth is still the clear value.

With reversed-Z the far value is the constant 0, so the same depth can be produced by the rasterizer (ZERO_TO_ONE clip control, shader_logdepth.js:148-149), with no fragment write. After the reversed-Z flip, every other default-path gl_FragDepth writer is log-depth guarded (terrain, far_terrain, materials depth biases moved to the vertex stage at materials.js:760-857). sky_glow is the remaining large-area one.
findings.proposal:
In `patchSkyGlowShader`, under `#ifdef USE_REVERSED_DEPTH_BUFFER`:
- inject `gl_Position.z = 0.0;` after `#include <fog_vertex>`, the last vertex chunk;
- drop the fragment `gl_FragDepth = 0.0` (keep `gl_FragDepth = 1.0` for the log/conventional path).

Bump SKY_GLOW_PROGRAM_KEY to `hbSkyGlow2`.

The depth test then compares the same constant 0 against the same buffer, so the same samples pass. Occluded pixels are rejected by early-Z and Z-cull before shading or blending. Clipping only differs for geometry between the eye plane and the 0.1 m near plane, which is off-screen for sheets 450-700 m out.

Flag `?skyGlowEarlyZ` default ON (`=off` restores the fragment write).
findings.expected_gain:
Unmeasured.

Derived: today every pixel the nine sheets cover is shaded and depth-tested late at 4× MSAA, whatever is in front. After the change, occluded tiles are culled before shading.

Assumed: 0.1-0.5 ms GPU outdoors at ultra, scaling with how much of the screen the sheets cover (large when the camera pitches up) and with town clutter in the upper frame.
findings.novelty_check:
- ledger, slices, walls for `skyGlow|sky glow|FragDepth|early-z`: only reversedZ, terrainLast and the log-depth walls 84/207. The 10-19 reversedZ work removed log-depth writes but not this explicit far-depth write.
- git log `skyglow|sky glow|fragdepth`: nothing.
- url-flags has `skyGlow` (strength/legacy) but no depth-path option.
findings.verify_how:
- **Node:** patch a stub MeshBasic shader with the reversed define and assert there is no `gl_FragDepth` in the fragment and `gl_Position.z = 0.0` is in the vertex.
- **GPU smoke (orchestrator):** extend the existing harness/glsl_smoke reversed_z smoke to render a far-depth sheet behind an opaque quad and compare pixels between arms; expect identical.
- **1070:** GPU timer around the world pass with `?skyGlowEarlyZ=off` vs default, camera pitched up over Holtburg.

findings.title: Cloud shadow march can run every 2nd/3rd frame at the same resolution, because its temporal resolve only takes 5% of each new march
findings.evidence:
CloudsEffect.update (build index.js:3371 `this.shadowMaps.update(`, then 3441-3443) recomputes the cascades and marches the shadow every frame: `shadowPass.update(renderer, this.frame, deltaTime); cloudsPass.shadowBuffer = shadowPass.outputBuffer; cloudsPass.update(...)`.

ShadowPass.update (src/ShadowPass.ts:124-139) renders 3 cascades × 512² (qualityPresets.ts high: cascadeCount 3, mapSize 512, maxIterationCount 50) and then the temporal resolve. `temporalPass = true` is the default (build:2819).

holtburger sets the shadow resolve to `temporalAlpha = 0.05` (cloud_volume.js:175-177), so each frame's fresh march contributes 5% to a roughly 20-frame exponential history. The resolve reprojects history with the cascade matrices stored at the last run (`copyReprojection`/`swapBuffers`), and cascades are texel-snapped (CascadedShadowMaps.ts:240-244).

Terrain reads the same frozen-able matrices (cloud_volume.js:516-534 copies `this.material.uniforms.shadowMatrices` and `cloudsPass.shadowBuffer`).

Cost share, derived from the 10-17 arm in the ledger (1024→512 shadow saved about 3.5 ms of clouds+AP): the 512² pass is roughly 1.0-1.2 ms of the ~4.3-4.6 ms clouds budget.
findings.expected_gain: Derived: about 0.5 ms GPU at N=2 (half of a ~1.0-1.2 ms pass, including its variance-clip resolve) and about 0.7 ms at N=3, at high/ultra outdoors. The image keeps the same steady state; the shadow time constant goes from ~20 to ~40 frames (≈0.4 s more lag on drifting cloud shadows).
findings.novelty_check:
Advances ledger-open line 235 / gpu-shading-open #67 ('3 x 512² shadow cascades marched every frame … cloudShadowRes default unchanged … needs 1070 look+GPU arm'). Earlier proposals were all quality knobs (cloudShadowRes 256, cloudResScale 0.5, cloudQuality).

What I add: a same-resolution, same-quality amortisation, grounded in the resolve's α=0.05, plus a concrete zero-vendor-edit hook, the STBN-counter detail and the cost-share derivation.

No cadence flag exists (url-flags cloud* rows) and nothing in git log (`cadence|shadowPass|cloud shadow`).
findings.verify_how:
Node: a stub-effect test that N=2 calls shadowMaps.update and shadowPass.update on alternate frames with a consecutive own-frame counter, and N=1 is a pass-through.

1070 only (SwiftShader samples 3D textures as 0): GPU timer around CloudsEffect.update at a fixed pose with `?cloudShadowEvery=1/2/3`. Eye test: cloud shadows sweeping over Holtburg fields while running and during a fast 360° camera spin, plus a storm DayGroup.

findings.title: Split post chain at high/ultra runs two avoidable full-screen RGBA16F passes (NanScrub #1 and LayeredHaze); fold both into the atmosphere EffectPass
findings.proposal:
Behind `?postFuse` (default ON, `=off` byte-identical):
- **(a) Haze:** wrap the haze math in a pmndrs Effect with attributes NONE and its own tDepth/uInvProj/uCamWorld/fog/strength uniforms, refreshed in `update()` with the same isSkyBlocked → strength 0 rule. Append it to atmosEffects after ssaoComposite and build `fxPass = new PostChainTargetPass(camera, particlesOverCloudsPass, ...atmosEffects, hazeEffect)`. Drop PostChainHazePass. EffectPass sorts by attributes descending (postprocessing build/index.js:15551), so a NONE effect appended last keeps today's AP → AO → haze order.
- **(b) Scrub:** on the split chain only, put the existing makeNanScrub() effect first in atmosEffects with EffectAttribute.DEPTH so it stays first among the DEPTH group, and stop adding the standalone scrub EffectPass. Keep it on the unsplit chain, where bloom lives in fxPass.
- **(c) Optional:** the late scrub could likewise move into bloom's LuminanceMaterial plus the first post effect.
findings.expected_gain: Derived: 3.69 Mpx × ~16-20 B per pass ≈ 60-75 MB of traffic. That is roughly 0.15-0.3 ms per removed pass on a 1070 at 1440p, so about 0.3-0.6 ms GPU for two (≈0.15-0.3 ms at 1080p), plus two fewer render submissions of main-thread and CrGpuMain overhead per frame.
findings.novelty_check:
- ledger, slices, walls for `scrub|fuse|merge pass|full-screen pass|post quad`: only the NanScrub correctness rows (wall 93, SKY-5) and msaaWorldOnly (post quads made single-sample). No pass-count reduction.
- git log: 4dc55751 and 2f5c64a6 add the scrub; nothing merges it.
- url-flags has no `postFuse`.

Caveat: identical up to one dropped fp16 rounding of the intermediate. Differences can only appear at non-finite or negative source texels inside an active heat-haze/fxDistort UV-warp footprint (filter-then-scrub vs scrub-then-filter). The NaN source itself is fixed (8b537b32).
findings.verify_how:
- **Node:** build the pipeline with split-chain opts and assert the composer pass list loses the standalone scrub EffectPass and the PostChainHazePass, and the atmos pass is a PostChainTargetPass whose effect order ends [..., ssaoComposite, haze].
- **GPU smoke (orchestrator, harness/glsl_smoke):** `?postFuse=off` vs default readback of T and of the final frame on a fixed scene; expect a max delta within one fp16 ulp.
- **1070:** frame GPU time A/B at Holtburg at ultra.

findings.title: Terrain fragment shader compiles ~170 lines of off-by-default family blocks behind uniforms; gate them with #defines like HB_TERRAIN_TRAIL_MAP
findings.evidence:
Assembled terrain FS (node dump via `_terrainGlslForTest`): 1,386 non-comment code lines. Uniform-gated blocks:
- uSnowPrintEnabled (frag lines 1359, 2743)
- uMudPrintEnabled (1408, 2755)
- uIceRefractEnabled (2021)
- uCrackGlowEnabled (2532)
- uMudWetEnabled (2782, 2920)
- uSnowSparkleEnabled (2822)
- uIceEnabled (2864)
- uSandSparkleEnabled (2978)

Together they total about 173 code lines (≈12%), including hash/noise and env-cube taps, plus their family weights (snowW/sandW/dirtW/iceW/volcW) computed for every pixel.

Their enables are session-constant strict `=== "on"` opt-ins that ship OFF on every tier (terrain.js:4939-4985 `sandSparkleEnabled: terrainSandEnabled() && terrainSandSparkleEnabled()`, etc.; uniforms seeded once at terrain.js:6561-6669). A uniform can't be dead-code-eliminated, so FXC keeps these blocks, their temporaries and their sampler bindings in the program that draws the 6.1 ms terrain.

Precedent: HB_TERRAIN_TRAIL_MAP and HB_TERRAIN_CSM already gate session-constant features with defines (frag 1995/2139, url-flags 1070-handoff §1).
findings.proposal:
Mirror the HB_TERRAIN_TRAIL_MAP pattern. When the material is built, add `HB_TERRAIN_FAM_SNOW`, `_MUD`, `_ICE`, `_VOLCANO` and `_SAND` defines from the same booleans that seed the uniforms, and wrap each block (and its weight computation) in `#ifdef`. Keep the uniforms so live tuning still works when a family is on.

terrain_batch and far_terrain already copy defines.

The pixel output is unchanged, because the uniform is 0 for the whole session.
findings.expected_gain:
Unknown, possibly zero.

Derived: about 12% fewer FS code lines, and fewer DXBC instructions and temporaries. Any GPU gain depends on whether the dead blocks raise the peak register count, and with it occupancy, in a shader doing ~20 texture fetches.

Assumed: 0-0.3 ms of the terrain's ~6.1 ms at ultra, plus a shorter first-sight D3DCompile for the terrain program.
findings.novelty_check:
- ledger, slices, walls for `define|register pressure|occupancy|dead code|uniform gate`: only the 18→14 sampler-budget gating (CSM/trail map) and terrainFarSimplify. Neither gates the off-by-default families.
- git log has no family define-gating.
- No url-flag.
findings.verify_how:
- **Node:** the terrain_far_simplify-style test asserts the default-flag assembled FS contains none of the family block markers, and that `?terrainSand=on&terrainSandSparkle=on` restores them.
- **1070 (cheap, no fps run):** dump the terrain program's translated HLSL via WEBGL_debug_shaders, compile with `fxc /T ps_5_0` in both arms, and compare `dcl_temps` and instruction counts. Only if temps drop, run a GPU timer A/B on the terrain draw.

verdicts.code_truth:
Every citation holds at HEAD.
- materials.js:1747/1753/1763 sample `texture2D(uPomMap, …)` before, inside and after `for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++)`, and the loop exits through `if (i >= steps) break; if (currentLayerDepth >= currentHeight) break;`.
- materials.js:1784 has the same shape inside `_pomShadow`'s `for i<16`.
- The calls sit inside runtime ifs: 1823 `if (_pomLod > 0.001) {` → 1834 `if (_pomGrazeW > 0.001) {` → 1836 `_pomPerturbedUv(...)`; and 1880 `if (_pomLodG > 0.001) {` → 1882 hit-depth sample plus 1883 `_pomShadow`.
- Small miscount: there are 5 uPomMap samples, not 6.

ANGLE source fetched this session confirms the mechanism:
- ASTMetadataHLSL's gradient list includes texture2D and texture.
- `visitLoop` calls `onGradientLoop()` for any loop with a gradient op in its call graph. That marks the innermost if; `visitIfElse` PostVisit propagates the mark to parent ifs, and a call to a function with `mHasGradientLoopInCallGraph` marks the enclosing if.
- OutputHLSL emits `FLATTEN ` for those ifs.
- `lod0 = (mInsideDiscontinuousLoop || mOutputLod0Function)`. A break inside an if (not directly in the loop body) makes the loop discontinuous.
- Renderer11.cpp compiles with `loopMacros[] = {{"ANGLE_ENABLE_LOOP_FLATTEN","1"}}`, so FLATTEN expands to `[flatten]` on D3D11.

POM_UNIFORM_DEFAULTS lodNear 5 / lodFar 10 (1597-1613) and quality.js:540-541 (24/12 at ultra) are as cited. statPom does use textureGrad with `_statUvGx/_statUvGy = dFdx/dFdy(vMapUv)` (static_atlas.js:635, 703-704) and a real distance gate (`_pomVd < uStatPomFar`).

The finder overstates the reach. Legacy POM rides only DoubleSide base materials:
- entity parts via `getCached(did, true)`, entities.js:5420;
- plan-less non-atlased statics, statics.js:3126/3194/3971.

The FrontSide clones (4059), VFX-plan variants (`_fragMat` → getCachedVariant clone), cell-baked walls, cell statics and building shells carry no POM at all (see gpu-shading-2).
verdicts.novelty:
New.
- No ledger row (compact, open or walls) mentions flatten, lod0, textureGrad, gradient or HLSL translation.
- git log POM commits (8ae0afe5, fede9728, fdad6a05, 3aa0565d, 6e0f8213, bba2d59f) never touch the sampling form.
- url-flags.md has no pomGrad.
verdicts.wall_conflict:
- **Wall 105 (CPU-bound frame, POM theories dead):** superseded by the 10-19 picture (fill-bound at ultra), and this is a backend-correctness mechanism, not a re-pricing.
- **Wall 97 (half-res cut GPU with no fps change):** any GPU saving turns into fps only on GPU-bound frames.
- **Wall 101 (SwiftShader cannot judge GPU claims):** respected; the finder routes proof to the 1070.
verdicts.visual_safety:
Correctly flagged needs-eyetest. On D3D the in-loop height reads move from SampleLevel 0 to the base-UV mip. That changes march hits in the 5-10 m fade band and is plausibly an improvement (it removes mip-0 aliasing that only D3D has). GL backends change little.

The proposal must convert all five uPomMap samples, including the pre-loop, post-loop and hit-depth ones. Otherwise FXC may still flatten or hoist because of gradient ops inside the now-dynamic ifs.
verdicts.gain_realism:
Mechanism: certain at the ANGLE level. That FXC then executes the [loop] unconditionally under [flatten] is inferred, not proven: it needs a translated-HLSL dump plus fxc on the 1070.

Per-fragment cost today: relief_height pillow fields make the march take several steps, so roughly 4-15 height fetches (in-loop ones at mip 0) plus ~60-80 ALU on every legacy-POM fragment at any distance.

Reach is limited to NPC parts and non-atlased singletons. Corrected estimate: about 0.05-0.3 ms GPU in NPC-dense towns at ultra, unmeasured. It counts toward fps only when the frame is GPU-bound. Its main value is as a correctness fix and as the prerequisite for any POM widening.
verdicts.corrected_claim:
On ANGLE/D3D11 the legacy POM patch compiles its three distance/graze ifs as [flatten] (ANGLE_ENABLE_LOOP_FLATTEN=1), and its in-loop height reads as LOD-0 samples. So every fragment of a legacy-POM material (entity parts and plan-less non-atlased statics only) runs the march and self-shadow regardless of the 10 m fade, and D3D marches mip-0 heights inside 10 m.

The fix: route all five uPomMap samples through textureGrad with unconditional dFdx/dFdy(vMapUv), as statPom does. That removes FLATTEN and LOD0, so the gates become real branches.

Ship behind `?pomGrad`, needs-eyetest (D3D pixels change in the 5-10 m band). Gain is unmeasured, probably 0.05-0.3 ms. Proof first: a WEBGL_debug_shaders dump showing FLATTEN/lod0 today, plus an fxc instruction comparison.

Forcing clip z = 0 in the vertex stage gives window depth exactly 0, the same constant the fragment writes today. The GreaterEqual test therefore passes and fails on exactly the same samples. Clipping moves from the 0.1 m near plane to the eye plane, but sheets hundreds of metres away put no on-screen pixels in that slab.

Overstated. The shader is a trivial MeshBasic plus one texture tap. Early-Z only saves fragments that end up occluded, and these sheets sit at high sky elevation over pixels that are mostly real sky, which pass and are shaded anyway.

Upper bound if all nine sheets covered the whole 1440p screen: about 0.3-0.4 ms of late-Z raster, of which only the occluded share is recoverable.

Corrected estimate: about 0-0.15 ms typical (more with the camera pitched up near tall buildings or trees); unmeasured, and orientation/coverage is unknown from code alone.

- **Vendor build:** index.js:3371 calls `this.shadowMaps.update(...)` inside the shared-uniform update. CloudsEffect.update (≈3426-3443) runs `++this.frame; updateSharedUniforms; shadowPass.update(renderer, this.frame, deltaTime); cloudsPass.shadowBuffer = shadowPass.outputBuffer; cloudsPass.update(...)`.
- **ShadowPass.update** (src/ShadowPass.ts:124-139): sets `frame`, copyShadow, march, then the resolve, copyReprojection and swapBuffers when temporalPass is on.
- **Presets:** high = defaults with shadow cascadeCount 3, mapSize 512, maxIterationCount 50; ultra uses 1024. The default cloudQuality is high, and cloudShadowRes is unset by default (index.js:6038-6043).
- **holtburger tuning:** cloud_volume.js:175-177 sets shadow `temporalAlpha = 0.05` and varianceGamma 4.
- **Terrain feed:** cloud_volume.js:516-534 copies only `mats[0]` and `cloudsPass.shadowBuffer`.

One extra detail: `updateSharedUniforms` also advances `localWeatherOffset` and `shapeOffset` every frame. On skipped frames the held shadow lags the cloud field by one frame of drift, which is sub-texel at 512² cascades.
verdicts.novelty:
Advances open lead #67 with a same-quality cadence idea rather than another resolution knob.

The finder missed a direct precedent in git. Commit 6638fd9b 'perf(clouds): frame-skip cloud composer every other frame' was reverted by 928841d5 because cloud motion looked visibly stepped (the owner: "30 Hz or something that looks awful").

This proposal differs in substance: it touches only the EMA-resolved shadow map (α=0.05) and holds buffer and cascades together, not the visible cloud imagery. But the precedent defines the eye-test risk and should have been cited. No cadence flag exists in url-flags.
verdicts.wall_conflict:

verdicts.visual_safety:
Correctly flagged needs-eyetest.
- Holding the cascades and buffer together keeps the clouds pass, AP shafts and terrain consistent in world space.
- Per-run drift is about 0.3 m at N=2, sub-texel.
- The real risks: (a) visible 2-frame stepping of shaft or shadow edges (the 928841d5 failure class), and (b) doubled EMA lag. Variance clipping limits the trail, but it is still a look change.
verdicts.gain_realism:
The 10-17 arm (1024→512: clouds+AP 9.17→5.64 ms) implies the 512² pass costs at most ~1.2 ms. Some of that saving likely came from cheaper shadow sampling in the clouds march and AP, so the pass itself is about 0.6-1.2 ms.

- **Effect order:** pmndrs 6.39.1 EffectPass.setEffects sorts `b.attributes - a.attributes` (stable). fxDistort, fxDecals, clouds and AP are DEPTH; ssaoComposite is NONE. A NONE haze appended last therefore keeps today's AP → AO → haze order.

findings.proposal: ?iblStableEnv (default ON, =off escape). In IblEnvironment.refresh keep ONE persistent PMREM target (the first fromScene result becomes this._envRT, assigned to scene.environment once). On later refreshes: rt = fromScene(...) as today; renderer.copyTextureToTexture(rt.texture, this._envRT.texture) (r184 blits render-target textures via blitFramebuffer — exact, same 768x1024 RGBA16F CubeUV layout, no mips); rt.dispose(). scene.environment never changes identity, so no material sees envMap !== envMap. findings.proposal: ?particleBucketMemo (default ON, =off escape), all output-identical: (1) cache the bucket key on the emitter (recompute only if _instKey changes); (2) memoise _alphaMatSig per (material, frameId) in a WeakMap (drizzle: ~1,000 emitters share one material); (3) read _sharedFrameId() once per tick and pass it down; hoist the makeIm closure to a method taking (emitter,gfx,layer,alpha); (4) stamp shared buckets {sortedFrame, sortedN, sortCamX/Y/Z} and skip a re-sort when all equal (the second manager's finalize on an unchanged bucket); (5) replace the comparator sort with a stable 3-pass 11-bit LSD radix on ~floatBits(distSq) (keys are finite >= 0, so bit order == numeric order; stable => same tie order as V8's stable comparator sort), comparator fallback for n<128; (6) gather with plain 16/3-float loops (no subarray views).

findings.title: Particle InstancedMesh buckets re-upload their whole CAPACITY (instanceMatrix + instanceColor) every frame — and even when parked to count 0
findings.evidence: particle_manager.js:741-743 (shared alpha finalize) and 3129-3131 (per-manager finalize) set instanceMatrix.needsUpdate / instanceColor.needsUpdate with no update ranges; an idle bucket parked dark also flags a full upload just to draw nothing (726, 3111-3114). three r184 WebGLAttributes.updateBuffer (three.module.js:141-151): with updateRanges empty it issues `gl.bufferSubData(bufferType, 0, array)` — the entire typed array, i.e. capacity, not im.count. Capacity: _INST_BUCKET_MIN_CAP = 256 (853), _growBucket doubles (863-866), buckets are only reaped after 180 idle ticks (859), so capacity tracks the historical peak. The repo's newer FX code already uses ranges for the same kind of buffer: particle_fx_kids.js:397-399, fx_showcase.js:880-882, fx_ribbons.js:661-662, fx_decal_effect.js:582-584.
findings.proposal: ?particleUploadRange (default ON, =off escape): before each needsUpdate in both finalize paths, `attr.clearUpdateRanges(); attr.addUpdateRange(0, n * attr.itemSize)` for instanceMatrix (16) and instanceColor (3); when a bucket parks to n=0 set im.count = 0 only (no upload). Instances >= count are never drawn, so stale tails are invisible; a grown bucket's fresh buffer still gets its initial full bufferData.
findings.expected_gain: Per bucket per frame saves (capacity - n) x 76 B (64 matrix + 12 colour): >=19 KB for every small bucket at the 256 floor, ~40% of a large doubled bucket. Derived ~0.3-1 MB/frame in emitter-dense towns (Cragstone: 8,492 particles across gfxobj buckets), i.e. ~15-50 MB/s less through the renderer->GPU-process transfer buffer and ANGLE UpdateSubresource; estimated 0.05-0.4 ms/frame split across CrRendererMain memcpy and CrGpuMain (assumed per-MB costs, not measured). CrGpuMain was 79% busy (fps-review).
findings.novelty_check: Ledger: only 'Perf T9: animated scenery uploads only changed instance span' (ledger-compact 219) and scatter updateRanges alias (549) — particles never. rg 'addUpdateRange|clearUpdateRanges' in scene3d/particles: only particle_fx_kids.js (the kids layer), not the main buckets. rg 'particleUploadRange' url-flags: none. Wall #83 says CrGpuMain cost is invisible to CPU profiles — this targets it directly.
findings.verify_how: Node test over tests/helpers/fake_webgl2.mjs counting bufferSubData bytes per frame for particle buckets: today sum(capacity)x76, with flag sum(n)x76; instance data visible to draws (first n) identical. 1070: gputrace.mjs + scripts/perf-worker/gpu_thread_split.py WebGL ms/frame on CrGpuMain in a particle-dense town, default vs =off.

findings.title: Occlusion proxies re-query every ~2 frames even when stably VISIBLE — coherent query cadence (hidden at full rate, visible every K frames)
findings.evidence: occlusion_cull.js:272 `m.visible = !p.queryPending;` — a proxy is redrawn (and re-queried, onBeforeRender/onAfterRender begin/endQuery at :219-235) the frame its previous result lands (results land 1-2 frames late, header :28-31), whatever its verdict. stepProxyState (:79-95): hidden->visible on the FIRST visible result, visible->hidden after HIDE_AFTER(3)+ consecutive occluded results. beginFrame (:150-190) polls getQueryParameter for every pending proxy. PERF-LOG-1070-2026-10-06 Fix 2: '+~170 proxies' per frame at Holtburg. Each proxy is a full three draw (renderObject, modelView+normalMatrix compute, 3 matrix uniform uploads, drawElements) plus a D3D11 query begin/end on CrGpuMain.
findings.proposal: ?occlusionCoherent=K (default ON, K=8; =off escape) — the CHC-style rule: in want(), draw the proxy when `!p.queryPending && (!p.visible || ((this.frame + p.phase) % K === 0))`, phase = small hash of key, so a VISIBLE proxy re-queries every K frames while a HIDDEN proxy keeps today's every-landing cadence. Reveal latency (the visible artefact) is unchanged; only visible->hidden decisions arrive up to K x later (pure perf). Entity boxes are padded around the rig, so an occluded proxy means occluded content: drawing it longer is pixel-identical; cell boxes are shrunk, so a cell may simply stay drawn a little longer (never hidden earlier than today).
findings.expected_gain: With f = share of proxies stably visible and today's ~2-3 frame query period, saves ~f x 170 x (1/2.5 - 1/K) query draws/frame: ~30-60 at Holtburg if half are visible; at an assumed ~10-20 µs per proxy draw across main thread + CrGpuMain, ~0.3-1.2 ms combined. Wall #107 applies (cheap draws) — hence medium impact, low confidence on magnitude.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger: occlusionCull shipped (ledger-compact 558), pop-in study (576), restore fix (413), doorway-step lead (ledger-open 267) — no query-cadence/coherence item. rg -i 'coheren|requery|CHC' in ledger: none. rg 'occlusionCoherent' url-flags/scene3d: none. git log -i occlusion: only the 10-06 culler and portal occlusion-gate commits.
findings.verify_how: Node test on OcclusionCuller with a fake GL query: (a) a hidden proxy that becomes visible flips on the first landed result exactly as today; (b) a stably visible proxy issues 1/K as many queries; (c) a proxy turning occluded hides after <= K x HIDE_AFTER results. 1070: window.__occlusionCull.stats.issued per frame, renderCPU and gpu_thread_split CrGpuMain at Holtburg/Linvak, default vs =off.

findings.title: Forced synchronous layouts inside the rAF tick: selection brackets read canvas.clientWidth/clientHeight every frame after the net pump wrote HUD DOM; combat/target handlers restart CSS animations with `void el.offsetWidth` inside the pump
findings.area: scene3d/selection_brackets.js tick; plugins/combat-hud.js, combat-bar.js, target-bar.js, status-indicators.js, vitals-hud.js
findings.evidence: tickPerFrame starts with window.__netFramePump() (loop.js:3004), which dispatches this frame's client events into the HUD (chat/vitals/combat DOM writes); at its end loop.js:3641 calls selectionBracketLayer.tick, whose selection_brackets.js:940-941 reads `this.canvas.clientWidth/clientHeight` EVERY frame while a target is selected (brackets are the default mode, selection_brackets.js:552-560) — a style+layout flush mid-frame whenever the pump dirtied the DOM, after which later rAF callbacks' writes need a second layout before paint. Event handlers that run inside the pump force reflow on purpose: combat-hud.js:529-533 (`transition=none; width=0%; void fill.offsetWidth` on every attack commence), combat-bar.js:2432-2435 (strike pulse per hit), target-bar.js:687-690 (selection blink), combat-hud.js:922-925, status-indicators.js:443-446, vitals-hud.js:279.
findings.proposal: HUD fix, no flag (owner rule HUD-fixes-skip-url-flag-gating): (1) selection_brackets: take CSS width/height from a ResizeObserver on the canvas (or the renderer's tracked CSS size, the same values) cached on the layer — identical numbers, no layout read; (2) replace `remove class; void offsetWidth; add class` with Web Animations restarts (`for (const a of el.getAnimations()) { a.cancel(); a.play(); }`) or two alternating identical keyframe names, and the combat-hud charge bar with `fill.animate([{width:'0%'},{width:pct}], {duration, easing:'linear', fill:'forwards'})` — same visuals, no forced reflow.
findings.expected_gain: Unmeasured: removes one forced document layout per frame while something is selected (and one per combat event), each sized by the dirty HUD (assumed 0.1-1 ms with large windows open). Basis: code reading only; the 10-17 1070 profile shows 17% '(program)' native time on CrRendererMain that includes the Blink lifecycle.
findings.novelty_check: rg -i 'forced reflow|forced layout|layout thrash|clientWidth' in ledger: none (the 10-19 HUD fixes were orb CSS loops, minimap style writes and radar repaints — write-side, not read-side). git log -i 'reflow|selection bracket': none for this.
findings.verify_how: Laptop is fine (DOM, not GPU): Chrome DevTools Performance trace with a target selected while chat/combat events arrive — look for 'Forced reflow' / Layout under selection_brackets.js tick and under the plugin handlers inside the scene3d rAF task; after the fix none. Existing bracket placement tests (lastRect) must report the same rects.

verdicts.code_truth: Every citation checks out at HEAD. ibl_environment.js:83-95 readIblFlag returns !(v==='off'), so it is default ON. readIblRefreshMs (97-106) defaults to 15000. loop.js:3339 ticks it inside the sky group. refresh() starts at :492: line 498 is `const rt = this._pmrem.fromScene(...)`, 500 is `this.scene.environment = rt.texture`, 502 is `if (old) old.dispose()`, and comment 496-497 claims a 'texture-object swap does not recompile programs'. In three r184 (package.json 0.184.0), setProgram sets needsProgramChange when `materialProperties.envMap !== envMap` (three.module.js:18380). getProgram (:18087) runs programCache.getParameters and getProgramCacheKey (:18098-18099) before the 'same program' early-out (:18124-18130). It also sets environment for Standard, Lambert and Phong (:18105). PMREMGenerator.fromScene (src/extras/PMREMGenerator.js:109-145) takes only size and position, and always calls _allocateTargets(). _allocateTargets (:286) builds a new cubeUV target on every call. fromCubemap and fromEquirectangular accept a renderTarget; fromScene does not. scene3d sets no explicit material.envMap anywhere, and async_link_guard keys on material.version, so the env swap neither defers nor skips draws. I re-ran the finder's bench (real r184 renderer over fake_webgl2) and reproduced it: 800 materials, +12.94 ms on the swap frame, 16.17 us/material, programs=1. Independent 1070 evidence in the repo: three_batchedmesh_colortexture_fix.js header measured getProgram 258->78/frame giving renderCPU -3.35 ms, about 18.6 us per redundant getProgram on the 1070 box.
verdicts.novelty: This is an open lead (ledger-open:157, '[render-cpu] IBL refresh every 15 s swaps scene.environment PMREM -> needsProgramChange on every standard material', WHY-OPEN 'unverified lead'). It is not in git log (IBL commits are a6bc2d7f, 73d7e31b, 54980ff0, none about a stable env). url-flags has no iblStable, pmremReuse or stable-env flag. The finder adds decisive material: a verified r184 mechanism with line numbers, proof that fromScene cannot reuse a target, a measured per-material cost (now corroborated by the repo's own 1070 getProgram measurement), and a pixel-identical fix. That qualifies as a real advance.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None. Wall #110 (framework glue negligible) covers 70 ns per-object glue, not a full getParameters plus cache-key build, which is measured at ~16-19 us. Wall #91 (asyncLink skips swaps) does not apply because the program is unchanged and the guard keys on material.version. Walls #107/#137 (draws x us) do not apply because this is a re-resolve count, not draw removal.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical. Copying a same-size RGBA16F target with copyTextureToTexture uses r184's blitFramebuffer NEAREST branch (three.module.js ~:19325, taken for isRenderTargetTexture), which is an exact copy. The CubeUV layout and the uniforms (envMap, envMapRotation, environmentIntensity) are unchanged. One implementation note: copyTextureToTexture leaves READ/DRAW framebuffer bound to null. That is harmless here because refresh runs in tick outside any pass and _cleanup has already restored the previous target. The cheaper variant (wrapping _allocateTargets) avoids the blit but relies on a private API. Both keep the first-assignment compile.
verdicts.gain_realism: Plausible. The extra frame cost is about (standard/Lambert materials drawn) x ~16-19 us. The ledger figure '1,544-item main pass (603 materials)' gives roughly 600 x 18.6 us, about 11 ms, on the refresh frame. That frame already carries fromScene (sky faces plus PMREM passes) and the terrain cube, so this removes the larger part of a recurring ~15 s spike (one ~31 ms frame instead of ~20 ms at 50 fps). It also removes the 6 MB render-target alloc/dispose churn on each refresh. Steady-state fps is unchanged, and it is too rare to move p99 (1 frame in ~750). It shows in worst-frame and 1%-low numbers.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Every IBL refresh (every 15 s, default ON) gives scene.environment a new PMREM texture object. On the next frame three r184 re-runs getParameters plus getProgramCacheKey for every MeshStandard/Lambert/Phong material drawn, only to land on the same program. That costs ~16 us/material in node and ~18.6 us per redundant getProgram on the 1070 (repo-measured), roughly 10 ms at ~600 drawn materials, once every 15 s. The fix: keep one persistent PMREM target as scene.environment and copy each fresh fromScene result into it (or reuse the target), so the environment's identity never changes. Pixel-identical, S effort. It removes a periodic ~10 ms hitch and does not change steady fps.

verdicts.code_truth: Verified at HEAD in scene3d/particles/particle_manager.js (3222 lines). _defaultFrameId (665-671) reads document.timeline.currentTime. _alphaMatSig (676-680) builds an 8-element array with map.uuid and color.getHex() and joins it. SharedAlphaBuckets.finalize (721-745) sorts every live bucket (sortFn at ~739), and the protocol note at 643-645 says 'EVERY manager's finalize re-sorts and republishes it'. _finalizeInstBuckets (3096-3101) calls sharedAlphaBuckets.finalize from each manager, and there are two managers (entities.js:15031, statics.js:5623). The static manager ticks in its own rAF (statics.js:6533-6546). _appendInstances (2830-2849) builds a template-string key per emitter and, for alpha emitters, calls acquire(key, scene, _alphaMatSig(...), new closure, _sharedFrameId()) on every call. _sortBucketBackToFront (818-842) does idx.sort(comparator) on a Uint32Array (833) and gathers with m.set(_sortMat.subarray(...)) plus a colour subarray per moved instance (839-840). I re-ran the drizzle DAT probe: setups 0x02000407/0x02000406 -> emitters 0x32000142/0x32000143 (maxParticles 5/7) -> hwGfx 0x01001166 -> surface 0x0800005D, type 0x4 (ClipMap, not Additive 0x10000). baseIsAdditive is therefore false (2268-2279) and all drizzle goes into one shared alpha bucket. My own node benches: per alpha emitter key+sig+acquire = 817 ns (sig alone 621 ns; document.timeline is not counted in node). Comparator sort plus subarray gather at n=1024: 261 + 91 us random. A re-sort of already-sorted data costs 102 + 7 us, because V8's typed-array comparator sort is a merge sort with no run detection.
verdicts.novelty: New. The ledger has only the shipped particleInstancing/InstancingAlpha/SharedAlpha flags (ledger-compact 475/559/575) and the eye-test lead (ledger-open 245), with no item on key/sig cost, double finalize sort, radix or gather. git log only has the E5/FU1 sortObjects commits (e1339afc, 221fa1cd). url-flags has no particleBucketMemo or radix flag.
verdicts.wall_conflict: Brushes wall #135 (GC ~2 KB/frame refuted) but differs: the claim is measured CPU time in the sort, gather and per-emitter signature, not GC. No conflict with #110 because the per-emitter overhead measures ~0.8 us, about 10x the glue figure, and it is real string/array work. Particle pooling walls (#165) are not touched.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical if implemented as described. A stable LSD radix on float32 bits of non-negative finite keys (a sum of squares cannot be -0) reproduces V8's stable comparator order including ties. The skip-re-sort stamp must compare copied camera values: both managers' _instSortCamWorld point at the same module-level _sortCamWorld vector (particle_manager.js:2578). It must also re-sort when n changes, because a partial first-manager bucket is followed by appends from the second. A NaN key would order differently from the comparator's NaN-as-equal handling, but that ordering is already ill-defined today.
verdicts.gain_realism: Plausible, concentrated at Linvak Tukal (main-thread-bound per f0b6a74e). With staticScriptRadius=2 and the RP6 220 m cull, I estimate 300-1,000 visible drizzle emitters (~256 per LB) and a shared bucket of ~1,000-3,000 instances. That gives append overhead ~0.25-0.8 ms, first sort+gather ~0.35-1 ms, and the second sort ~40% of the first (not 100%, since presorted input still costs a full merge sort). The memo, radix and loop-gather variant would save ~0.5-1.2 ms/frame there on laptop CPU and ~0.05-0.2 ms in ordinary towns. The visible-emitter count is my estimate, not a measurement.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Per-tick particle bookkeeping does avoidable work. Each visible alpha emitter rebuilds its bucket key, an 8-field joined material signature (getHex with colour conversion), a closure and a DOM frame-id read, about 0.8 us each. Every shared alpha bucket is comparator-sorted by both ParticleManagers each frame, and the second sort of already-sorted data still costs ~40% of the first. The gather allocates two subarray views per moved instance. Memoising key and signature, stamping buckets to skip an unchanged re-sort, and using a stable radix plus plain-loop gather gives identical output and saves ~0.5-1.2 ms/frame at drizzle-heavy Linvak Tukal (~0.1 ms elsewhere).

verdicts.code_truth: Verified. occlusion_cull.js:272 is `m.visible = !p.queryPending;`, so a proxy is redrawn and re-queried whenever no result is in flight, whatever its verdict. onBeforeRender/onAfterRender begin/end the query at :219-235. stepProxyState (:79-95) reveals on the first visible result and hides after HIDE_AFTER(3) or more occluded results, with flip damping up to 24. beginFrame (:150-190) polls getQueryParameter for every pending proxy. Consumers are cells.js:3515 (cell drop) and entities.js:3278 (rig hide via _renderCullHidden only). Proxies share one geometry and one MeshBasicMaterial and draw last in the transparent list.

verdicts.wall_conflict: Runs into wall #107/#137 (proxies are the cheapest possible draws: one program, no material switch, a 12-triangle box) and, unaddressed, wall #115/#138 (parked wins can be moving losses). With K=8 and HIDE_AFTER=3, a visible proxy that becomes occluded needs ~3 results x 8 frames before hiding. Each delayed rig keeps ~40 part draws, or a whole interior cell, alive for ~17 extra frames. During camera pans, the many visible<->occluded transitions can cost more content draws than the proxy draws saved.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical as claimed. Hidden->visible latency is unchanged, and keeping depth-tested occluded content drawn longer changes no pixels. The only effect is a later hide (never an earlier one).
verdicts.gain_realism: Overstated. Assuming about half of ~170 proxies are stably visible at a 2-3 frame query period, K=8 saves ~20-25 proxy draws/frame (not 30-60). At ~5-10 us main-thread per same-program proxy draw plus the D3D11 query begin/end, that is ~0.1-0.4 ms combined when parked. While moving it may break even or lose unless cadence reduction applies only while occludedRun===0 (falling back to full rate after the first occluded result), which bounds the extra hide latency to <=K frames.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Stably visible occlusion proxies re-query every 2-3 frames. Throttling visible proxies whose last result was visible (occludedRun===0) to every K frames, while keeping hidden and just-occluded proxies at full rate, would cut ~20-25 cheap proxy draws/frame plus their queries at Holtburg. verdicts.code_truth: Code facts check out. loop.js:3004 calls window.__netFramePump() at the top of tickPerFrame, and loop.js:3641 calls selectionBracketLayer.tick. selection_brackets.js:940-941 reads canvas.clientWidth/clientHeight each frame while a target is selected and the display is on, and brackets are the default mode (552-560). This is the only per-frame layout read in the default scene path: the hud.js NameplateLayer read at :254 belongs to the default-off DOM nameplates, and camera.js:369 runs at construction only. The `void offsetWidth` restarts exist at combat-hud.js:531 and :924, combat-bar.js:2434, target-bar.js:689, status-indicators.js:445 and vitals-hud.js:279.
verdicts.novelty: New. There is no reflow or forced-layout item in the ledgers. The git hits are c1081f01 (an unrelated title-tab ResizeObserver) and bracket art commits.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None directly, but the gain is speculative (an evidence-rule concern).
verdicts.visual_safety: The ResizeObserver/cached-size path is identical except for a possible one-frame stale size during a window resize. Replacing class-restart reflows with WAAPI cancel/play or element.animate is close but not guaranteed identical: fill modes, class-driven keyframes and the charge-bar transition need a quick look. As HUD fixes they fall under the owner's no-flag rule, but they are not strictly pixel-identical by construction.
verdicts.gain_realism: Mostly overstated. A clientWidth read after the pump's HUD writes forces the style and layout work the frame would do anyway at the lifecycle; it moves that work earlier, it does not add it. The brackets' own writes afterwards then need only a small incremental relayout of absolutely positioned elements. The real waste is in event bursts, where several handlers in one pump interleave write -> forced read -> write (chat append, vitals flash, strike pulse), causing repeated incremental layouts. That is event-rate (a few per second in combat), not per frame. Likely <0.1 ms/frame on average, unmeasured.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The selection-bracket tick reads canvas.clientWidth/clientHeight every frame after the net pump may have dirtied HUD DOM, and several combat/target/vitals handlers restart CSS animations with `void el.offsetWidth` inside the pump. The per-frame read mostly moves layout work rather than adding it. The handler reflows can cause a few extra incremental layouts per combat-event burst. Caching the canvas CSS size (ResizeObserver) is a free, identical cleanup. The WAAPI restarts are optional HUD polish needing a quick look. Expected gain is well under 0.1 ms/frame on average and unmeasured.

findings.title: Terrain batch without gl_DrawID: pack the LB origin into aLbSlot so ANGLE stops re-uploading uniforms per range, then merge index-adjacent LB ranges into spans
findings.evidence: terrain_batch.js:210-222: the batched vertex shader includes `<batching_pars_vertex>` and computes `mat4 lbBatchMat = getBatchingMatrix( getIndirectIndex( gl_DrawID ) );` only to get the per-LB TRANSLATION (it is applied at :223-237). terrain_batch.js:941-942 `state.bm.setMatrixAt(iid, lbMesh.matrix)`: the translation is lbX*192, lbY*192. terrain_batch.js:914-916 writes `aLbSlot` as `Float32Array(vcount).fill(slot)`. terrain_batch.js:610-611 sets sortObjects=false and perObjectFrustumCulled=true. Each LB has its own geometry, so buildRuns finds no repeats and batchedRuns can never help: every frustum-visible LB is one emulated range. batched_runs.js:7-15 (ANGLE notes): gl_DrawID is set per range uncached, and the whole vertex default uniform buffer is re-uploaded before each range.
findings.proposal: At absorb (terrain_batch.js:914), write aLbSlot = slot + 256*lbX + 65536*lbY. The value is below 2^24, so float32 holds it exactly. In _buildBatchedGlsl: drop the `#include <batching_pars_vertex>` decl and replace the lbBatchMat line with an exact unpack (floor and subtraction by powers of two): `lbPlacedPos = displacedPos + vec3(vec2(lbX, lbY) * 192.0, 0.0)`, worldXy computed the same way, `vLbSlot = slot`, and WATER_BANK_FETCH_BATCHED reading the unpacked slot. The program then never references gl_DrawID. ANGLE's MultiDrawElementsGeneral takes its no-draw-ID branch (no per-range setDrawIDUniform, no constant-buffer re-upload), and batchingTexture/batchingIdTexture are optimised out, which removes two texture binds per terrain draw. Since nothing then depends on the draw index, a `markBatchedCoalesce(bm)` mode in the batched_runs wrapper merges entries where starts[k+1] === starts[k] + counts[k]*bpe into spans and hands them over through the already-patched multiDrawElementsWEBGL. Flag `?terrainSpans` (default off until the GPU smoke proves bit-identity, then on). Optional arm `=all` sets perObjectFrustumCulled=false so every resident unparked row draws in about 1-5 spans: terrain is roughly 25-40k triangles resident, which is not the +420k-triangle statics trade in wall #113, but it needs a 1070 number. Instance matrices stay as they are for three's CPU culling.
findings.expected_gain: Removes the per-range uniform upload for every terrain range (about 50-100 visible LBs per frame at ultra, assumed from the 151-203 resident ring) and cuts the range count to the number of index-contiguous spans. Plausibly 0.2-0.5 ms CrGpuMain per frame (assumed, unmeasured). Small vertex-shader saving (four matrix texel fetches plus an indirect fetch per vertex).

findings.title: Particle instance buckets re-upload their entire capacity (matrices and colours) every frame, and once more when they go dark
findings.evidence: particle_manager.js:740-743 and :3128-3131 set `im.count = b.n; im.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true; if (im.instanceColor) im.instanceColor.needsUpdate = true;` every tick with no update range. :726 and :3111-3113 also mark a full upload when a bucket goes dark (count → 0, so nothing is read). three WebGLAttributes.js:87-90: with no updateRanges, `gl.bufferSubData(bufferType, 0, array)` sends the WHOLE array. Capacity: _INST_BUCKET_MIN_CAP = 256 (:853), and _growBucket (:862-866) doubles and never shrinks while the bucket stays live. That is at least 256×(64+12) B = 19.5 KB per bucket per frame regardless of live count, and 2048-4096 slots (150-300 KB per frame each) after a burst. Bucket creation (:2963) and _growBucket set no DynamicDrawUsage. The newer FX code already does this right: particle_fx_kids.js:398, fx_showcase.js:881, fx_ribbons.js:662 and fx_decal_effect.js:583 all use `addUpdateRange(0, n*itemSize)`, and animated_scenery.js:827 sets DynamicDrawUsage.

On the go-dark transition, set count = 0 without marking an upload. At creation (:2963) and in _growBucket (:866), call `setUsage(THREE.DynamicDrawUsage)` on instanceMatrix (and on instanceColor once setColorAt creates it), before the first upload. A grown mesh's first bind is still a full bufferData of the copied array, so that stays correct. Flag `?particleUploadRange` (default ON, `=off` escape). Instances at or beyond count are never read by drawElementsInstanced(count), so the output cannot change.

findings.title: Cause of the 256-512 glBlitFramebuffer warnings: the depth format of a multisampled buffer is fixed at its first bind while pmndrs swaps depth textures per pass. The default path has had no such producer since 10-17; a one-boot validator can close the lead
findings.area: scene3d/atmosphere_pipeline.js, scene3d/msaa_world.js, three WebGLTextures, pmndrs EffectComposer
findings.evidence: three fixes a multisampled target's depth renderbuffer format at its first setup, from whatever depthTexture is attached at that moment (WebGLTextures.js:2119-2120 → setupRenderBufferStorage :1676-1700 → getInternalDepthFormat :254-290: null/UnsignedInt → DEPTH_COMPONENT24, Float → DEPTH_COMPONENT32F). It later resolves COLOR|DEPTH into the CURRENT attachment (:2306-2329). pmndrs nulls the output buffer's depth texture and re-attaches its own FloatType texture to the input buffer before EVERY pass (postprocessing build/index.js:1276-1277, createDepthTexture :1047-1066). holtburger additionally attaches a bespoke UnsignedInt (DEPTH24) texture to both ping-pong buffers at construction and on every resize (atmosphere_pipeline.js:1280-1297, 2610-2619). On the legacy multisampled ping-pong composer, any buffer first bound with one depth type and later resolved into another is rejected with GL_INVALID_OPERATION, and the colour is lost too: exactly the 2026-10-07 'NO DEPTH RESOLVE' incident (gl.getError 1282 every frame, atmosphere_pipeline.js:548-562). The 'Attachments are not all the same size' variant was Bug 11 (atmosphere_pipeline.js:2570-2586). 256 is Blink's per-context cap on WebGL console errors (kMaxGLErrorsAllowedToConsole), so 256 means a sustained producer. 512 fits two contexts: init3D built a second renderer until ?preInitShare (29e76419, 2026-10-17). Default path today: (i) W's resolve is consistent by construction (msaa_world.js:117-134 attaches composer.depthTexture before the first bind; :140-158 rebuilds on identity change and keeps the size), (ii) the pmndrs stable blit copies a FloatType texture into its clone at the same drawing-buffer size (build/index.js:1072-1102, 1311-1330), (iii) shadowStaticCache blits run only with csm on (off in every preset) and are already checked with getError (shadow_caster_list.js:527-532). No other blitFramebuffer, copyTextureToTexture or copyFramebufferToTexture caller exists in scene3d, vendor or pmndrs (rg).
findings.proposal: Close ledger-open:264 with one 1070 bare-URL boot: count the console warnings, which should be 0. Add a debug-only `?blitCheck=on` (default off) that wraps gl.blitFramebuffer. Before each call it checks gl.checkFramebufferStatus(READ_FRAMEBUFFER/DRAW_FRAMEBUFFER) and, when the mask includes DEPTH, compares getFramebufferAttachmentParameter(DEPTH_ATTACHMENT, FRAMEBUFFER_ATTACHMENT_DEPTH_SIZE/COMPONENT_TYPE) and the attachment sizes. It logs the JS stack once per call site, so any remaining producer is named in one boot. Note in url-flags.md that `?msaaWorldOnly=off` still carries the trap for any pass that draws into a ping-pong buffer after pmndrs has re-pointed its depth texture.
findings.expected_gain: Correctness and diagnostics: confirms no rejected (colour-losing) resolves on the default path and retires a pre-existing unexplained warning flood. No fps claim.

What I add: the mechanism traced through three, pmndrs and holtburger code; the reading of the counts as Blink's 256 cap times two renderers before preInitShare; an enumeration of every blit producer showing the default path has had none since msaaWorldOnly and preInitShare (both 2026-10-17, after the 10-09/10-11 reports); and a validator that settles it in one boot. Searched the ledgers and docs for glBlitFramebuffer: only the two handoff notes and the Bug 11 comment.

verdicts.code_truth: Every citation checks out at HEAD. batched_runs.js:426 gates on `!ctl.off && _chunksPatched && object.sortObjects === false && (object._multiDrawCount | 0) > 1 && _eligible.has(object)`. buildRuns (:200-243) groups ranges by start in first-seen order, which reorders instances. markBatchedRuns is called only at static_batch_x.js:2388 and static_atlas.js:1346. buildings.js:329-368 adds each shared BufferGeometry once per bucket (gidOf) and gives it one instance per placement; :383-384 sets sortObjects=false and perObjectFrustumCulled=true and never marks the bucket. _batchEligible excludes ShaderMaterials. BatchedMesh.js:1567-1613 writes multiDrawStarts and indirect ids in sorted order. rg finds gl_DrawID only in batched_runs.js and terrain_batch.js, and no customSort anywhere in scene3d. Two corrections. (1) The static_batch_x sorted buckets are ALREADY marked (the 2388 call is unconditional, before `bm.sortObjects = _shouldSortBucket(mat)` at 2393), so only the wrapper's sortObjects gate excludes them. (2) The census figure (per-instance-walk.md:251, 'drawnSorted 2,022') counts instances walked in buckets that were drawn, not ranges submitted after the per-instance frustum cull, so the number of sorted ranges is smaller.
verdicts.novelty: This advances ledger-open:232, which only names the gap ('never attempted'). The order-keeping consecutive-run builder that makes sorted buckets exactly eligible is a new design. Not in ledger-compact (statBatchNoSort :727 drops the sort, which is a different idea), not in git log, no batchedRunsSorted flag in url-flags.md. The building opt-in itself is trivial once noticed.
verdicts.wall_conflict: Respects #29/#107/#137: it gives no ms figure. It sits on top of batchedRuns, whose ANGLE per-range saving has never been measured on the 1070 (ledger-open:231). It should therefore wait on that reading rather than extend an unproven mechanism.
verdicts.visual_safety: Sorted path: grouping only CONSECUTIVE identical ranges keeps the exact primitive order. GL instanced semantics draw instance by instance, and D3D11 rasterization ordering does the same, so the result is truly pixel-identical. Building path: it reorders instances inside an opaque bucket, the same class as the shipped batchedRuns. That is identical except at exact-equal-depth ties between coplanar surfaces of different instances, so it rides the batchedRuns eye check that is still owed.
verdicts.gain_realism: Buildings: tens of ranges per frame (Linvak 126 meshes in 11 batches, Holtburg 56). Repeats are plausible only where identical models share a landblock and material (housing settlements, Linvak treehouses), so this is at most tens of ANGLE ranges. Sorted buckets: R/n is unknown and the submitted count is below 2,022. While the camera moves, the sorted order changes every frame, so each bucket pays a rebuild plus an extra indirect-texture upload on top of three's own. That needs a minimum-gain threshold (for example R < 0.75n) or it can lose. Corrected estimate: at best a few hundred ranges per frame removed, likely 0.0-0.3 ms CrGpuMain. Unmeasured.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Opting building batches into batchedRuns is a one-line, safe change (stock batching chunks, unsorted, shared geometry instanced per placement). Static_batch_x sorted buckets are already marked; a consecutive-run builder would let the wrapper accept them with exact order. The gain is unmeasured and probably small: buildings give tens of ranges, the sorted R/n is unknown, and moving frames pay an extra texture upload. It depends on batchedRuns itself proving out on the 1070, and should include a minimum-gain threshold.

verdicts.code_truth: Verified. terrain_batch.js:210-213 includes `<batching_pars_vertex>`. :222 computes `getBatchingMatrix( getIndirectIndex( gl_DrawID ) )`, and the result is used only at :224 (worldXy) and :235-237 (placement). :941-942 calls setMatrixAt with lbMesh.matrix, and terrain.js:6878-6882 sets that position to (lbX*192, lbY*192, 0), translation only. :914-916 builds aLbSlot as Float32Array.fill(slot). :610-611 sets sortObjects=false and perObjectFrustumCulled=true. TB_SLOT_CAPACITY=256 (:123), so slot + 256*lbX + 65536*lbY stays at or below 2^24-1 and float32 holds it exactly. terrainBatch is default ON (:96-110). The patched batching_pars_vertex also injects hbBatchSlot, which references gl_DrawID, into the terrain program. Dropping the include (as proposed) is therefore required, not optional.
verdicts.novelty: New mechanism. Ledger-open:232 says unique-geometry buckets get no run gain and gives no design. No ledger, git log or url-flags item covers removing the gl_DrawID dependence or span coalescing; only ?terrainBatch exists.
verdicts.wall_conflict: The `=all` arm brushes #113 (perObjectFrustumCulled must stay on). The finder correctly argues terrain triangle scale is not the +420k statics case and leaves it as an optional 1070 arm. #29/#107: the ms estimate is assumed.
verdicts.visual_safety: The arithmetic argument holds. A translation-only mat4·vec4 computes x*1 + y*0 + z*0 + tx, which rounds once, exactly like x + tx. The offsets are integers times 192, and the unpack uses only powers of two and floor. It is bit-identical in IEEE; FXC reassociation cannot change sums of exact zeros. A SwiftShader smoke does not exercise the D3D compiler, so a 1070 readback compare is still advisable.
verdicts.gain_realism: ANGLE's no-draw-ID branch skips the per-range setDrawIDUniform and the vertex default-uniform-buffer re-upload. Each range still issues its own DrawIndexed unless coalesced. The terrain vertex uniform block is small, and about 50-100 visible landblock ranges gives roughly 0.05-0.2 ms CrGpuMain, below the claimed 0.2-0.5. Span contiguity depends on how the streaming insertion order, evictions and optimize() line geometry rows up with instance order. With frustum culling on, spans will be fragmented. `=all` could reach 1-5 draws, but only a 1070 number can price it. The removed batching textures save 2 binds per frame, which is negligible.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Packing the landblock origin into aLbSlot and dropping batching_pars_vertex removes terrain's gl_DrawID reference. ANGLE then skips the per-range draw-ID uniform and vertex UBO re-upload for every terrain range, and exact coalescing of index-adjacent rows into spans becomes possible. It is bit-exact by construction. The gain is likely about 0.05-0.2 ms CrGpuMain at default culling; span benefit is uncertain, and the =all arm needs a 1070 number.

verdicts.code_truth: Verified. WebGLRenderer.js:1757-1766 calls updateMultisampleRenderTarget after every render into a target. WebGLTextures.js:2306-2318 adds DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT when resolveDepthBuffer is true. supportsInvalidateFramebuffer is OculusBrowser-only (WebGLTextures.js:10), so the multisample depth survives a color-only resolve. msaa_world.js:196-205 hands W to every pass before the first swap, the sky RenderPass included. atmosphere_pipeline.js:1302-1316 sets skyRenderPass.needsDepthBlit=false; only skyCapturePass (its own RT) and worldMaskPass sit between the sky and world passes. worldRenderPass is never disabled per frame (:2324-2367 toggles only the clear flags), so the next writer of W always resolves COLOR|DEPTH. PostChainSourcePass already does the same toggle (:563-568). Side finding confirmed: postprocessing 6.39.1 build/index.js has 0 occurrences of 'clearDepth', so the writes at :1392/:2363/:2366 are dead. With clear=false the world pass depth-tests against the sky pass's multisample depth (takram StarsMaterial depthWrite:true at vendor :5655; sky camera far 50 km, sky_dome.js:31-32).
verdicts.novelty: New. c3709b93 removed only pmndrs' stable depth blit after the sky pass, and msaaWorldOnly (15565e4d, ledger-compact:614) removed the post-pass resolves. No ledger entry covers the sky pass's own three resolve; no skyResolveTrim flag exists; and the dead clearDepth is not recorded anywhere.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None. GPU fill is near saturation at ultra per the current picture, so a GPU-side trim is not contradicted by #105/#141 (those were CPU-bound-era walls). The census number is a single-call GPU timer, which avoids the #85 trap.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical. The multisample depth renderbuffer the world pass tests against is untouched. composer.depthTexture is rewritten by the world pass's resolve before any reader, because no pass between the sky and world passes reads it.
verdicts.gain_realism: Overstated for the default configuration. msaa defaults to 2 at every preset (index.js:868-880; the preset only gates on/off via quality.flags.antialias), while the census ran an msaa=4 override. Still plausible: ANGLE D3D11 resolves depth with a shader pass, whose cost does not scale with sample count like the colour ResolveSubresource. Corrected: about 0.05-0.15 ms GPU per outdoor frame at default msaa=2, plus a little ANGLE depth-resolve setup on CrGpuMain. Small but nearly free.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Clearing resolveDepthBuffer around the sky pass's render into W (and restoring it) skips a depth resolve nobody reads; pixel-identical. Gain is about 0.05-0.15 ms GPU at default msaa=2 (the 0.12-0.16 figure assumed msaa=4). Separately, `clearDepth` is not a pmndrs 6.39.1 RenderPass property, so the world pass inherits the sky pass's depth (harmless today); the comments and dead writes should be corrected.

verdicts.code_truth: Verified. particle_manager.js:740-743 and :3128-3131 set count=b.n and needsUpdate on instanceMatrix/instanceColor with no update range. :726 and :3111-3113 mark a full upload when count drops to 0. _INST_BUCKET_MIN_CAP=256 (:853). _growBucket (:862-866) doubles, copies the whole array (:886-888) and never shrinks. Creation at :2962 sets no usage hint. WebGLAttributes.js:87-90 sends the whole array via bufferSubData(0, array) when updateRanges is empty. The newer FX code uses addUpdateRange: particles/particle_fx_kids.js:398, vfx/fx_ribbons.js:662, vfx/fx_decal_effect.js:583, vfx/fx_showcase.js:881 (the vfx/ paths differ slightly from those cited); animated_scenery.js:827/848 set DynamicDrawUsage. verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical: drawElementsInstanced(count) never reads instances at or beyond count, and a count-0 bucket draws nothing. setUsage before the first upload is only a storage hint.
verdicts.gain_realism: Derived, not measured. At least 19.5 KB per bucket per frame regardless of live count, more after growth. With roughly 10-40 town buckets that is about 0.2-0.8 MB per frame, copied renderer to transfer buffer, then into ANGLE staging, then into D3D. Plausibly 0.05-0.3 ms across the renderer and CrGpuMain, more after bursts have grown buckets.
verdicts.corrected_claim: As stated. Upload only [0, n) of the particle bucket instanceMatrix/instanceColor each tick, skip the upload when a bucket goes dark, and mark the buffers DynamicDraw. Pixel-identical, S effort, a small CrGpuMain/renderer saving (likely ≤0.3 ms) that grows with bucket capacity.

verdicts.code_truth: occlusion_cull.js matches the citations: one shared BoxGeometry and MeshBasicMaterial (:113-130), one Mesh per proxy with onBeforeRender/onAfterRender query bracketing (:204-237), and a per-proxy scale+translation matrix (:262-276). The main-thread mechanism is wrong, though. WebGLRenderer.js:2116-2121 (renderObject) computes modelViewMatrix and normalMatrix per RENDER ITEM, so a grouped mesh still does both matrix ops per group, and each group is still its own render-list entry and sort item. Only projectObject and the frustum test are saved. The CrGpuMain part is right: WebGLUniforms' mat4 setter is value-cached, so groups after the first skip uniformMatrix4fv because modelViewMatrix is identical, and ANGLE stops re-dirtying the vertex uniform block.
verdicts.novelty: New. The ledgers have only RENDER-3 (ledger-compact:413), the occlusionCull row (:558) and the doorway eye test (ledger-open:267). Nothing in git log or url-flags.
verdicts.wall_conflict: Wall #110/#139 (three's per-object glue costs 70.7 ns, negligible) contradicts the main-thread half of the claim, and the finder did not overcome it. #29/#107: the 2-5 µs per proxy figure is assumed.
verdicts.visual_safety: Same boxes, same states and same queries give the same verdicts, so it is pixel-identical in principle. But it rewrites a system that was eye-tested for flip damping, and a geometry-groups bug would silently change verdicts. The stats A/B the finder proposes is needed.
verdicts.gain_realism: Main thread: about 170 × ~70 ns, roughly 0.01 ms, i.e. nil. CrGpuMain: removes about 85-170 uniformMatrix4fv calls and small vertex-UBO updates per frame, while every query draw stays. Corrected estimate: about 0.03-0.15 ms CrGpuMain, against M effort in an eye-tested subsystem.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Batching the occlusion proxies as groups of one shared Mesh lets three's uniform cache skip the per-proxy modelViewMatrix upload, saving roughly 85-170 uniform uploads and the matching ANGLE vertex-UBO updates per frame on CrGpuMain. Per-group render items, sorting and matrix ops stay, so the main-thread change is negligible. Expected about 0.03-0.15 ms for M effort.
