coverage_notes:
I read ledger-walls.txt (209) and both streaming-hitch slices in full, and searched ledger-compact, ledger-open, git log and url-flags.md for every candidate. Code I read in full or in depth: xu7_textures.js (transcode, budgeted FIFO, texture-worker client), texture_worker.js header, bake_worker.js, bake_worker_client.js (coalescing, settle), upload_stage.js, tex_upgrade_queue.js (index, backpressure, pump), bc7_textures.js (upgradeMaterialToBc7 / buildAndSwap), materials.js (_repointAlbedoForDid, _patchSetCacheKey, the get() build path), adapter.js (texture wrappers), landblock_lru.js (evict, tickEviction), static_atlas.js (evict, refeed, optimize, array builders), terrain_batch.js and static_batch_x.js optimize ticks, terrain_bc7.js (ladder staging), async_link_guard.js, shader_prewarm.js, bake_prewarm.js, portal_space.js (tunnel warm), atmosphere_pipeline.js (ParticlesOverCloudsPass), particle_manager/particle_fx (bucket materials), fx_glow_effect, fx_ribbons, landblock_stream.js (populate paths), shard_fetch_worker.js header, lib.rs fetch_landblock_scenery. I checked three r184 internals directly: WebGLPrograms key, compile(), WebGLProgram onFirstUse, WebGLTextures array uploads, BatchedMesh delete/optimize, WebGLAttributes range merge.

Light probes I ran (node, laptop CPU, scripts in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-wbterminal/98168d1d-a7fa-4057-8cdb-22b89664f038/scratchpad/agent-scratch/):
- getParameters plus getProgramCacheKey: 11.1 us per object.
- Scene.traverseVisible light-gather: 0.50, 1.10 and 2.33 ms for 10k, 20k and 40k nodes.
- Normal-map RGB-to-RGBA pad: 0.14, 0.54 and 2.05 ms per surface at 128, 256 and 512 px square.

On the dimension's explicit question: wall #123 ("every XUBC7 transcode runs on the window thread") is stale. texWorkers has been on by default since 2026-10-06 (xu7_textures.js:657-760), so the transcode runs in texture_worker.js with transferables. The main-thread budgeted FIFO is now only a counted fallback, used when the worker is loading or dead, or the queue is over 64. tex_upgrade_queue's backpressure at depth 8 should keep it from engaging (finding 3).

Dropped or walled:
- Default-path upload staging. upload_stage.js is never constructed in production, but wall #88 says pre-upload did not fix the first-turn hitch.
- BatchedMesh optimize() re-upload: r184 merges adjacent update ranges, and the buckets are small.
- deleteGeometry is O(instances) per gid. That is real, but the atlas holds about 120 nodes, so it is small.
- Whole-array generateMipmap after every single-layer addLayerUpdate on the RGBA8 NRA and diffuse DataArrayTextures (static_atlas.js:344-352, 374-384; three WebGLTextures.js:1378). It is real, but the GPU-process cost depends on ANGLE and needs a 1070 probe. Lead only.
- Terrain t1024 promotion costs 2 x ~44 ms, once per session. Chunking it by layer is blocked by three r184 calling clearLayerUpdates inside the mip loop (WebGLTextures.js:1054-1066), which is the already-open chain-bucket item.
- The asyncLink drain is capped by count (64), not by time. Lead only; magnitude unmeasured.
- renderer.debug.checkShaderErrors defaults to true, which costs 3 extra synchronous IPCs per first program use. Small, and it conflicts with the read-the-console-first rule.
- statics.js calls fetch_landblock_scenery with per-object getters while fetch_landblock_scenery_soa exists unused. Minor.

Walls that shaped the search: #88 and #123, #94/#124 (program key comes from geometry and target), #81/#82/#83 (CrGpuMain is invisible to CPU A/Bs), #91 (asyncLink skips draws) and #57.

findings.title: Particle/FX first-sight links: no current warm path compiles the program key the late particle pass actually draws with
findings.area: shaders-compile / particles_over_clouds / tunnel warm / archetype warm
findings.evidence:
Particles are drawn by ParticlesOverCloudsPass into its own `lateScene = new THREE.Scene()` (atmosphere_pipeline.js:612). At draw time it sets `scene.fog = worldScene.fog; scene.children = objs` (atmosphere_pipeline.js:712-713), so that render has no lights. three r184 pushes numDirLights, numPointLights and the other light counts into EVERY program key, including MeshBasic and ShaderMaterial (WebGLPrograms.js:333-338 and 467-479). Every existing warm is therefore mis-keyed or empty:
(a) asyncLink defers only draws whose scene is the main scene (`if (scene === mainScene)`, async_link_guard.js:518; header lines 24-27: ShaderMaterials and particles draw as before). Late-pass draws link synchronously.
(b) The tunnel warm treats the late pass as a scene pass and calls warmSceneMaterials(pass.scene) (portal_space.js:1355-1361). Outside render, lateScene.children is the empty `_noChildren`, so it compiles 0 materials. The world-pass warm compiles the hidden particle buckets against the world lights (shader_prewarm.js:668, :698), which is the wrong key. Its release hold also skips them, because MeshBasic counts as 'guarded' (portal_space.js:1339).
(c) The archetypeWarm particle proxies (bake_prewarm.js:250-261) are a plain Mesh with stock MeshBasic, compiled against host.scene. The real bucket is an InstancedMesh with instanceColor plus applyParticleFxMaterial defines, onBeforeCompile and customProgramCacheKey, plus applyAdditiveParticleFog (particle_manager.js:2956-2963; particle_fx.js:1230-1259). That differs on 4 key axes.
(d) The glow twins render in their own `glowScene` (fx_glow_effect.js:79, :230). fx_ribbons is a ShaderMaterial registered as a late source (fx_ribbons.js:373, :405). fx_decal_effect, fx_fields, fx_showcase and particle_fx_kids have no warm at all (no compile/prewarm reference in the files).
Measured symptom: the 10-11 1070 bench at ultra showed first-turn frames over 100 ms going from 15.5 (FX legacy) to 37 (all FX), and jank from 5.7 to 8.4 s (HANDOFF-1070-session-2026-10-11.md §3).
findings.proposal: 1) Add `warmLateFx(renderer, camera)` to particles_over_clouds.js. It asks every registered late source for ALL its objects (add an `{all:true}` argument; sources currently push only visible, parented objects). It then sets `lateScene.children = all; lateScene.fog = worldScene.fog`, calls warmSceneMaterials(renderer, lateScene, camera, getWarmTarget(), {seen}), and restores children. This reproduces the late draw's key exactly: no lights, the world fog, and a non-null HalfFloat target class like T. Do the same for the glow pass: glowScene stand-in, glow twins, glow target class. 2) Call it from warmWorldPrograms on each tunnel warm pass, adding its pending programs to `_warmHeld` (the guard never defers them). Also call it from a 1 Hz idle tick whenever particle_manager `_makeBucketIm` or a vfx module mints a new material. 3) Replace the archetypeWarm particle proxies with faithful ones: an InstancedMesh(count 1) with instanceColor, through applyParticleFxMaterial / applyAdditiveParticleFog / _configureAlphaBucketMaterial, for additive and alpha × map/mapless × Front/Double side, plus one glow twin, the ribbon mesh and the decal/fields/kids materials. Compile them through the step-1 helper. This set is closed because the FX keys are constant per blend (particle_fx.js:1157 latches the tier variants). Flag: `?fxLateWarm`, default on (pixel-identical). Optional `?lateLinkDefer`, default off and needing an eye-test: collectLateFx skips objects whose program isReady()===false and kicks a compile, mirroring asyncLink.
findings.expected_gain: Removes the synchronous in-frame links of every late-pass, glow and ribbon program the first time each FX class is seen. Basis: the 10-11 measurement says FX roughly doubled first-turn hitching at ultra (37 vs 15.5 frames over 100 ms). Assumption: most of that delta is these links, since D3D11 links for MeshStandard run 0.5-2.9 s on the 1070 and MeshBasic+FX costs are unmeasured. Hypothesis to test: the unattributed ~1 s first-turn frame present in both lightLoops arms may be the first late-pass draw.
findings.novelty_check: This advances ledger-open '[shaders-compile] (perf-oct) Prewarm FX programs ... during the login tunnel | tunnelWorldWarm covers composer/world/sky only'. It adds: (1) proof that light counts sit in the r184 key, so a world-scene warm is the WRONG variant even when it runs; (2) proof that the tunnel warm visits the late pass but compiles an empty scene; (3) proof that the shipped archetypeWarm particle proxies (url-flags archetypeWarm row) are mis-keyed on 4 axes, so that 'shipped' warm warms nothing; (4) asyncLink's scene===mainScene exemption; (5) a concrete design. Searched the ledger for 'archetype', 'late', 'particle' plus 'warm', and url-flags for fxWarm/fxPrewarm/lateWarm: none. Git log: no late-FX warm commit.
findings.verify_how: Node test: build a bucket material via the real particle_manager `_makeBucketIm` path, compute WebGLPrograms.getProgramCacheKey for (world lights, world fog) vs (no lights, world fog), and assert the keys differ. That proves (b) and (c) without a GPU. Then assert warmLateFx compiles exactly the late keys. Laptop: `?linkProbe=on` boot, turn the camera toward a fountain or brazier, and read `__linkProbe.ledger()`; the programs created during the late render should drop to 0 with the flag on. 1070: the 10-11 first-turn bench at ultra with fresh profiles, arms fxLateWarm=on vs off, measuring frames over 100 ms and jank s.

findings.title: Every prewarm compile walks the whole world scene for lights and prepares every duplicate mesh: use the light stand-in and a per-key dedupe
findings.area: bake_prewarm.js guardedCompileAsync / per-LB bake, entity spawn, interior build
findings.evidence: guardedCompileAsync calls `renderer.compile(object, camera, targetScene)` with `host.scene` (bake_prewarm.js:57, :103, :261). In three r184, compile() first runs `targetScene.traverseVisible(...)` over the ENTIRE world graph to gather lights (WebGLRenderer.js compile). It then calls prepareMaterial, i.e. getParameters plus getProgramCacheKey, for every mesh in the subtree with no dedupe; a transparent DoubleSide mesh gets two calls. Call sites: terrain.js:6987, statics.js:3315 (every node of an LB), buildings.js:1330/1336, entities.js:5690 (every entity spawn rig), cells.js:2542 and 2725 (ONE compile over all new cells of an interior, after an otherwise 6 ms time-sliced build), terrain_batch.js:653, lifestone_fx.js:741. The code already knows the fix: async_link_guard.js:368-395 builds a cached-light stand-in 'without walking the whole world on every drain', and shader_prewarm.js warmSceneMaterials dedupes per material and uses the same stand-in. entities.js:5680-5700 notes hub bursts of 177 entity warms. Measured on the laptop with a node probe: 11.1 us per object for getParameters+key, and 0.50, 1.10 and 2.33 ms per traverseVisible at 10k, 20k and 40k nodes.
findings.proposal: In bake_prewarm.js: (1) build and cache a target-scene stand-in. Copy async_link_guard targetFor: `{isScene:true, get fog/environment/environmentRotation from main, traverseVisible/traverse over a light list refreshed at most every 500 ms}`. Pass it instead of host.scene. Lights, fog and environment are the only targetScene inputs to getParameters and getProgram, so the program keys are identical. (2) Before compile(), walk the subtree once and keep ONE representative renderable per key: material.id | isInstancedMesh, instanceColor!==null, morphTexture | isBatchedMesh, _colorsTexture | isSkinnedMesh | isPoints and has uv | geometry has normal | tangent (when normalMap/anisotropy) | color itemSize 4 (when vertexColors) | morphAttributes signature. These are every object/geometry input getParameters reads (WebGLPrograms.js getParameters lines that read object./geometry.). Hand compile() a duck-typed root over the representatives, as warmSceneMaterials does. The returned material Set, and so the readiness poll, is unchanged. Flag `?prewarmStandIn`, default on, with an off escape.
findings.expected_gain: Derived from the measured laptop costs: 0.5-2.3 ms saved per prewarm call (world traversal, 10k-40k nodes), about 4 calls per landblock bake plus one per entity spawn. A hub arrival with ~177 entity warms saves about 90-400 ms of main-thread work in the spawn burst. Each duplicate mesh saves about 11 us: a statics LB with hundreds of nodes loses milliseconds, and an interior with thousands of cell meshes (academy, 568 cells) loses tens of ms from one synchronous task.

findings.title: Texture worker client keeps one job in flight, so the worker idles for a busy main-thread turnaround per job; the texWorkers=2 burst datum predates the upgrade queue's backpressure
findings.evidence: _twPump posts only when `_twPending.size === 0` (xu7_textures.js:960-970). The next job is posted only from _twOnMessage (:922-948), i.e. after the result message has waited for a free slot on a renderer main thread that is about 98% busy. The worker handles jobs FIFO and already supports worker-side cancel of jobs it has not started (texture_worker.js header: 'A cancel for a seq not yet processed ... cancelled'), so the one-in-flight rule is purely client-side. Measured 1070 worker cost: BOOTWARM 193 jobs / 7,485 ms = 38.8 ms per job; TAIL 204 jobs / 5,276 ms = 25.9 ms per job (batch-A-2026-08-09.json). The 64-deep backlog with 38 main-thread FIFO fallbacks behind the open '?texWorkers=2' lead was measured 2026-08-10. That was before texUpgradeQueue went default-on on 10-09 with 'no new xu7 dispatch while worker depth > 8' (tex_upgrade_queue.js:150 `WORKER_BACKPRESSURE_DEPTH = 8`, :1061-1065, :1139-1141). Every full-tier upgrade passes that queue (materials.js:6320-6330), so the client queue should now stay well under the 64 cap. Worker throughput now sets how fast HD textures converge.
findings.proposal: (1) Let `_twPump` keep up to TW_INFLIGHT_MAX = 2 jobs posted, plus a cap on in-flight payload bytes (e.g. 8 MB). The worker then always has its next job queued in its own event loop, and cancelTextureWorkerJob keeps working (worker-side cancel). Results stay serial, because the worker is single-threaded, so the main thread sees no upload burst. Flag `?texWorkerDepth`, default 2. (2) Re-run TEXWORKER-BOOTWARM with today's defaults before anyone builds a second worker plus a second 1.04 MB transcoder. Measure maxQueueDepth and fifoFallbacks (expected about 0 now), __texUpgradeQueue.stats().backpressureBlocks, and worker utilisation = msTranscode / wall span. The second worker is only worth building if utilisation is near 1 at depth 2.
findings.expected_gain: Assumption: each main-thread turnaround is about 5-15 ms at 98% busy and ~20 ms frames. Worker idle per job is that divided by (turnaround + 26-39 ms transcode), i.e. 15-35%, which depth 2 recovers. HD and full-tier textures sharpen correspondingly sooner after arrival or teleport. No fps change. It also removes the reason to add a second transcoder instance.

It adds: (1) the burst datum is stale, because the 10-09 upgrade-queue backpressure at depth 8 caps exactly that queue (file:line above); (2) part of the backlog is caused by the one-in-flight client pump, not worker CPU; (3) a cheaper fix than a second worker. Searched the ledger for texWorker, backpressure, 'in flight' and 'one job': nothing on pump depth. Git: d8cfd82e/23383e2a only.

Read __texWorkerStats() (jobs, msTranscode, maxQueueDepth, fifoFallbacks), the first-to-last job span, and __texUpgradeQueue.report() time to HD-complete.

findings.title: HD (pre and full BC7) swaps bump material.version for nothing, so asyncLink skips every affected draw for a frame on each swap
findings.evidence: buildAndSwap does `mat.map = tex; mat.needsUpdate = true;` for both the pre and the full phase (bc7_textures.js:2093-2104). _repointAlbedoForDid does the same for every clone family (frontSide/floorBias/staticBias/cellBaked) and for the emissiveMap alias (materials.js:6361-6382). A map-to-map swap cannot change a three r184 program: the key reads only map presence, mapUv channel and the video decode flag (WebGLPrograms.js:124, 212, 269, 359), and the house key `_patchSetCacheKey` has no map-type bit (materials.js:597-631). The version bump alone does the damage. linkDecision sees `material.version !== mp.__version` with no trust yet (verNoop < 2) and returns 1 (async_link_guard.js:315-321). The wrapper then queues a compile and `return`s without drawing (async_link_guard.js:518-549). The draw comes back only after the setTimeout drain plus the 10 ms poll, i.e. the next frame. The pre swap (verNoop 0) and the full swap (verNoop 1) of a surface both fall inside the defer path. Batched and instanced variants mirror `version` as a hot key (batched_material_variant.js:98-100; anim_scenery_gpu.js:270), so a whole bucket using that surface skips its draw too. Scale: 306 singletonUpgrades in one legacy-arm session (T15R report), plus about as many pre swaps.
findings.proposal: In buildAndSwap, set `mat.needsUpdate = true` only when `!old || (old.channel|0) !== (tex.channel|0)` (map presence or uv channel changed). Apply the same rule to clone.map, clone.emissiveMap and mat.emissiveMap in _repointAlbedoForDid. Everything else already propagates without a version bump: refreshUniformsCommon re-reads material.map on every material switch, the variant mirrors copy `map` every frame (hot key), and the atlas refeed is driven by _rsVerdictResolved, not version. Flag `?hdSwapNoBump`, default on, `=off` escape.
findings.expected_gain: Removes roughly 2 one-frame dropouts per upgraded surface, covering every mesh, clone and batched bucket using it. That is hundreds of draw dropouts concentrated in the first minute after arrival while HD sharpens, together with their deferred compile() and poll work. It also stops HD re-seats from building VERSION_NOOP_TRUST, which the asyncLinkKeySig note identifies as what later let a real key change link synchronously.

Laptop headless (asyncLink logic is CPU-side): fresh boot, compare the `__asyncLink.stats.deferred` delta against `bc7Stats().preSwaps + singletonUpgrades`, flag on vs off. 1070: eye-check a street at arrival for single-frame pops while textures sharpen.

findings.title: A coalesced bake reply builds up to 64 materials in one microtask drain, each padding its normal map RGB to RGBA on the main thread
findings.evidence: `?bakeSurfaceCoalesce` (default 64 DIDs) answers every member of a merged post in one synchronous loop of `p.resolve(...)` (bake_worker_client.js:1473-1499). Each member is a MaterialCache.get(did) awaiting that fetch, so all their continuations (the material builds at materials.js:5455-5470) run back-to-back in the same microtask drain. This is the same shape as the xu7 tombstone 'N sibling settles in ONE task'. Each build calls surfacePixelsToNormalTexture, which allocates w*h*4 bytes and pads RGB8 to RGBA8 in a scalar loop on the main thread (adapter.js:1207-1224). The bake worker already copies the plane out of wasm (bake_transfer.js:327-329) and could emit RGBA at the same cost. Measured on the laptop with a node probe of that exact loop: 0.14, 0.54 and 2.05 ms per surface at 128, 256 and 512 px square.
findings.proposal: (1) In bake_transfer.js serializeSurfacePixel (worker side), pad normalPixels to RGBA while copying it out and send it transferred as `normalRgba`. adapter.js then skips the pad when byteLength === w*h*4 (fall back to the current loop for the main-thread path). Better still, have normal_gen emit RGBA in Rust at the next wasm rebuild. (2) Optionally spread the fan-out: resolve coalesced members in slices of a few ms each, yielding through a MessageChannel post (the house pattern; walled #100 forbids scheduler.yield here). Flag `?bakeNormalRgba`, default on.
findings.expected_gain: From the measured per-surface cost: up to about 35 ms (64 × 256 px) or more (512 px surfaces) of main-thread padding per coalesced reply, removed from a single task during landblock arrivals. Smaller in the common case where fewer DIDs share a post.
findings.novelty_check: Searched the ledger for coalesce, microtask, fan-out, pad, RGB8 and normal map. bakeSurfaceCoalesce is recorded only as a queue-depth win (coldload §4.21); the main-thread fan-out burst and the pad are not recorded. No flag found.
findings.verify_how: Node test: the worker-side pad equals adapter.js's pad byte for byte for a real SurfacePixels fixture, and adapter skips the loop for RGBA input. 1070: stall probe (`__stallArm` / `__stallReport`) on a town walk; the longest task attributed to a bake reply should drop. Laptop: performance.now() around _settleCoalesced plus its microtask drain.

Emitting RGBA directly from Rust normal_gen at the next wasm rebuild is the free version and should be preferred.

This happens on the coalesced single-DID path (up to 64) and on the multi-DID preload path (one request for all needed DIDs, e.g. Step C's 232). Each build pads the RGB8 normal plane to RGBA8 in a scalar main-thread loop (adapter.js:1207-1224). Delivering RGBA from the producer (Rust normal_gen at the next wasm rebuild, or the worker serializer as a stopgap that costs bake-worker time) removes that loop. Slicing the settle loop through MessageChannel posts would bound the per-task burst. Pixel-identical. Saves a few to tens of ms per burst task during landblock and interior arrivals.

coverage_notes:
I read all of ledger-walls.txt and both wasm-boundary slices. I checked every candidate against ledger-compact/open/walls, git log (3,581 commits) and url-flags.md.

**What I examined:**

I parsed the release pkg wasm's sections and target_features: 7,601,324 B, no name section, features = mutable-globals, nontrapping-fptoint, bulk-memory, sign-ext, reference-types, multivalue. There is no simd128.
- The counting global allocator (dlmalloc behind it): negligible overhead.

- Per-frame JS→wasm traffic: syncTickHop/tickMovement, pollRemotePoses, pollEntityUpdates, camera sweeps (wrappers are freed correctly), motion-sequence playhead. Payloads are tiny. The crossing-count wall holds, so I proposed nothing there.

- The record-read path: V2Source get_file_*, HbaReader, ShardCache, catalogs, CRC, packs.

**Deliberately skipped:**
- Anything already open or covered: camera viewer-transit, getLocalPlayerPose free leak, shard sha verify, decode-as-discovery waves, de-indexed geometry/HBG1, Theory 12, the equipment decode cache, the XU7 transcode move (it now runs on the texture worker), the threads/SAB experiment.

**Walls that shaped the search:**

findings.title: Release wasm is built with no LTO, 16 codegen units, and wasm-opt in size mode (-O = -Os)
findings.area: build profile / all Rust compute (bake-worker decode, physics, net parse) + wasm size
findings.evidence:
**Current settings:**
- Root Cargo.toml defines only [profile.dist] (:119-122, which already uses lto="thin" for native dist) and [profile.profiling] (:124), plus dev-only per-package overrides (:155-200). There is NO [profile.release], so every `wasm-pack build --release` (scripts/serve.py:967, ci-smoke.sh:36) uses Cargo defaults: lto=false (thin-local only), codegen-units=16.
- apps/holtburger-web/Cargo.toml has no [package.metadata.wasm-pack]. wasm-pack 0.14.0 therefore runs `wasm-opt -O`, which binaryen defines as -Os (optimize level 2, shrink level 1).
- .cargo/config.toml:18-19 rustflags carry only the stack size.

**Why it matters:** the app crate (lib.rs) calls hot non-generic functions in holtburger-dat (height_seam::relief_height_classed, seam_normal_rgb8, compute_stats, BSP predicates in physics.rs/transition/*) and holtburger-world. Without LTO, those cross crate boundaries as real calls unless they are #[inline] or tiny leaves. With codegen-units=16, the 50K+-line lib.rs is split into 16 LLVM modules.

The pkg wasm is 7,601,324 B and instantiated three times (main, bake worker, net worker).
findings.proposal:
**First, an A/B with no file change:**
```
CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=thin wasm-pack build --release --out-dir pkg-lto
```
then `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=fat CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=1`, each under capped-build, recording peak RSS.

**If it wins:** add a dedicated profile, so native wsbridge/cli builds keep fast compiles. Either `[profile.wasm-release] inherits="release"` with `lto="fat"` (or thin if fat exceeds the 3.5 GB cap), `codegen-units=1`, `panic="abort"`, built with `wasm-pack build --profile wasm-release`; or the same keys under [profile.release].

**Also add**, in apps/holtburger-web/Cargo.toml:
```
[package.metadata.wasm-pack.profile.release]
wasm-opt = ["-O3"]
```
(and in the custom profile if one is used).

No runtime flag is needed: it is a build change, and the previous pkg stays as the fallback.
findings.expected_gain:
Assumed, not measured for this project:
- Typical Rust→wasm results for thin→fat LTO + 1 CGU + binaryen -O3 are roughly 3–15% less wasm CPU and 5–15% smaller code.
- Here that applies to the measured long poles: bake-worker statics decode 2.5–5.9 s on the 1070 (coldload §4.28/4.30), 313-surface surfbench 3,212 ms on the laptop, and boot zstd/catalog work.
- It also applies, to a lesser extent, to per-frame TickMovement physics on the saturated main thread.
- A smaller wasm downloads (gzip) and compiles faster on all three instances.
findings.novelty_check:
- No profile.release, lto, codegen-units or wasm-opt matches in ledger-compact/open/walls.
- git log has nothing for lto/codegen/wasm-opt; the only 'profile' commits are dev-profile opt-level fixes (c628b329, 81567301).
- No docs or url-flags mention.
- Walls 13/131/147 are about release-vs-dev size detection: it keys on the name section, which stays absent with LTO, so harness/lib/wasm_profile.mjs still classifies the build as release.
findings.verify_how:
Orchestrator only, one heavy job at a time, capped-build:
1. Build pkg-base and pkg-lto release arms and record wasm sizes.
2. With serve.py up, run `node scripts/perf-worker/coldboot/surfbench.mjs pkg-base A.json` and `WASM=pkg-lto/holtburger_web_bg.wasm node … B.json`. All plane hashes must be identical (the script's python one-liner prints 0 differing); compare decodeMs.
3. Native cargo test is unchanged.
4. Optionally, a 1070 hbbench cold-load arm comparing furnished time.

findings.title: Enable wasm SIMD (+simd128): today the whole-row decode loops are scalar
findings.area: build flags / bake-worker surface decode (height_seam, texture decode)
findings.evidence:
**Current state:**
- The release wasm's target_features section has no simd128 (parsed from pkg/holtburger_web_bg.wasm).
- .cargo/config.toml:19 sets only `-zstack-size`.

**Hot loops that would vectorize:**
- height_seam.rs grey_morph_with: the vertical passes run over whole rows (:267 `*c = pick(prev[x], s[x])`, :276, final :286). `min_nn`/`max_nn` (:169-177) are `a<b?a:b`, which maps exactly to `f32x4.pmin`/`pmax` with no loop-carried dependence.
- lib.rs:14751 height plane `(v.clamp(0,1)*255) as u8` and seam_normal_rgb8 (height_seam.rs:970-975: sqrt, clamp, `as u8`) are element-wise.
- coldload §4.28 measured these functions as the decode: normal_and_height_pixels was 75% of it. After the 2.8x scalar fix, the statics' 232-surface decode is still one synchronous 2.5–5.9 s stretch in the bake worker.

**Loops that will not vectorize as written:** texture.rs to_rgba8 (:333-341, :350-358, P8 path) uses bounds-checked `source_data[i*3]` plus `out.extend_from_slice(&[r,g,b,0xFF])`.

**Bit-identity:** glam is a declared dependency of holtburger-world/core but has 0 source references, so no library switches to different SIMD math paths.
findings.proposal:
**Step 1, flag only:** add `"-C","target-feature=+simd128"` to [target.wasm32-unknown-unknown] rustflags in .cargo/config.toml. Build the experiment arm with CARGO_TARGET_DIR on /mnt/wbterminal1: a new RUSTFLAGS value duplicates the whole wasm artifact set, and the system disk is about 87% full.

**Step 2, optional, M:** rewrite the to_rgba8 format arms as `vec![0u8; n*4]` plus `chunks_exact(3).zip(out.chunks_exact_mut(4))` (and a 256-entry `[u8;4]` LUT for P8), so LLVM drops the bounds checks and vectorizes. The output stays byte-identical.

**Browser support:** Chrome 91+, Firefox 89+, Safari 16.4+. If older Safari must keep booting, ship a second non-SIMD pkg selected by `WebAssembly.validate` on a 1-instruction v128 module. Otherwise accept the floor; the owner runs Chrome.
findings.expected_gain: Assumed: about 1.2–1.6x on the vectorizable fraction of surface decode, which shortens the 2.5–5.9 s bake-worker statics decode (the interior 'furnished' long pole) and terrain/texture decode. Per-frame physics gets little: 3-lane Vector3 code is mostly not profitable to SLP-vectorize. The exact figure must come from surfbench decodeMs.
findings.novelty_check:
- 'simd' and 'target-feature' do not appear in the ledger, git log, url-flags.md or any doc. The only RUSTFLAGS docs are the atomics/threads SCOPE-2.5 experiments.
- It brushes wall 135 (wasm chatter) only in name: this is compute inside Rust, not crossings.
- Bit-identity rests on LLVM never reassociating FP or contracting to FMA on wasm, and on integer lanes being exact. Reductions such as compute_stats sums stay scalar.
findings.verify_how:
1. Orchestrator builds a simd arm into pkg-simd (capped-build, /mnt target dir).
2. Confirm `+simd128` appears in the target_features custom section.
3. Run surfbench.mjs on base vs simd: 0 differing hashes over the 313 surfaces; compare decodeMs.
4. Bare-default boot smoke (wireframe) to confirm the module validates in Chromium.
5. cargo test -p holtburger-dat --lib height_seam (24 tests) on the orchestrator.

findings.title: crc32_ieee runs bit by bit (8 shift/mask steps per byte) over every catalog and pack
findings.evidence:
**The algorithm:** catalog.rs:354-364 `crc32_ieee` loops `for _ in 0..8 { mask = (crc&1).wrapping_neg(); crc = (crc>>1) ^ (0xEDB88320 & mask) }` per byte, with no table.

**Where it runs:**
- `NamespaceCatalog::read_from` (catalog.rs:248) on every catalog each instance loads, via manifest_source.rs:678/826. Served sizes: eor-portal.bin 1,499,312 B, tex catalogs about 197 KB, regional eor/cell catalogs about 100–195 KB each. The main and bake-worker instances each parse their own.
- `HbpPack::parse` CRCs every pack body (pack.rs:172); `parse_hbsi1` does the same (pack.rs:370). The served pack corpus is 51,953 files, 837 MB, max 4.86 MB.
- insert_pack parses (and so CRCs) BEFORE its duplicate-resident check (pack.rs:655 then :657).
- pack.rs:156-157 states the controller's sha-on-receipt is the integrity gate and the CRC is only a backstop.

**Probe:** node proxy crc_probe.mjs on a 1.5 MB buffer: bitwise 25.9 ms (58 MB/s) vs slicing-by-8 4.0 ms, CRC equal.
findings.proposal:
Replace the body of crc32_ieee with table-driven slicing-by-8: eight 256-entry u32 tables built by a `const fn` (8 KiB static), plus a byte-wise tail. The public signature is unchanged, so pack.rs and the bake tool keep the same function.

Add a unit test comparing the new and bitwise reference over random lengths, plus the existing round-trip and CRC-mismatch tests.

Optionally, in insert_pack, check `index`/`resident.contains_key(hash16)` before `HbpPack::parse`, so a duplicate insert does not pay the CRC.

No flag is needed: the output is byte-identical.
findings.expected_gain:
Derived from the probe:
- Boot: about 2.5 MB of catalogs per instance → roughly 25–45 ms of CPU becomes about 4–7 ms, on both the main thread and the bake worker.
- Under packSource (owner-gated, currently DEV), pack-admission CRC CPU drops about 6x; for example about 1.5 s → about 0.25 s per 100 MB of packs.
findings.novelty_check:
- No ledger hit for crc beyond the dev-profile 'CRC32 fix' (81567301), which only optimised the dev build of the same bitwise loop.
- ledger-open 'Pack admission CPU spikes (decompress at insert)' covers zstd decompression at insert, not the CRC.
- No url-flag.
findings.verify_how:
1. Orchestrator: cargo test -p holtburger-manifest --lib (5 existing tests plus the new reference-equality test) and cargo test -p holtburger-resource-http --lib pack.
2. Real-data check: read_from on dist/manifest/eor-portal.bin succeeds, since its stored footer CRC must still match.
3. The proxy probe already shows identical output with a 6.4x speedup.

findings.title: Record-read hot path: every read probes the boot pack with binrw parsing; boot records are re-decompressed on every read; shard lookups allocate a String key
findings.evidence:
**(a) Boot probe on every read.** V2Source::get_file_shared (manifest_source.rs:1259-1272), get_file_by_key (:1237-1252) and the metadata/exists paths try `self.boot.get_file_by_key(key)` BEFORE the shard cache on every record read. With packSource off, that is every Surface/SurfaceTexture/Texture/Palette/GfxObj/Setup read, including the repeated reads of the ≤8-wave decode-as-discovery walk. For namespaces present in boot.hba (eor/portal 622 entries), a miss is a binary search: find_entry_with_namespace_id (archive.rs:256-288) calls read_entry_at (:298) per probe, which copies 60 bytes and binrw-parses an HbaEntry. That is about 10 parses per miss.

**(b) Boot hits are re-decompressed.** read_entry_data (:305-341) allocates `vec![0; comp_size]`, copies, and runs ruzstd (:327) every time. The comment at manifest_source.rs:1261-1263 admits the boot pack has no resident Arc.

**(c) String key per shard read.** `owned(key)` (manifest_source.rs:311-313) allocates a String for the namespace on every shard-cache lookup, then SipHashes `(String, u32)`.

**(d) Region re-parse.** resolve_region_land_height_table (lib.rs:2933-2947) clones the whole Region record (58,956 B per the eor-portal catalog) and runs a full `Region::unpack` to read 256 floats. It runs on every fetch_landblock_heightmaps / fetch_subdivided_landblocks batch (lib.rs:3172, :3375). Its doc comment (:2930) claims 'a cache read + 256-f32 parse'.
findings.proposal:
All byte-identical:
1. HbaReader::from_source decodes the whole index once into a `Vec<HbaEntry>` (639 entries, about 38 KB) per namespace span. find_entry becomes a slice binary search with no per-probe copy or parse.
2. V2Source keeps `boot_resident: Mutex<HashMap<(u16 ns, u32 id), Arc<Vec<u8>>>>`, filled on the first decompress. get_file_shared then returns an Arc clone; get_file_by_key copies from it. Optionally add a fast 'not in boot' answer from the decoded index (sorted ids or a bitset).
3. ShardCache key becomes an interned `(u16 ns_ordinal, u32)` (or a packed u64), hashed with FxHash or foldhash (both already in Cargo.lock), so there is no per-read allocation.
4. Memoise the land height table (and the Region-derived terrain_desc ids used by fetch_terrain_*) in a thread_local keyed by the Region record's Arc pointer or catalog hash, cleared on manifest re-init like the DEGRADE_* memos.
findings.expected_gain:
Derived:
- About 1–2 µs saved per record read (10 entry copy+parse probes plus String alloc+SipHash → about 50 ns). Over the thousands of reads per LB bake (multiplied by walk waves), that is single-digit to tens of ms per streaming burst, on the main instance and in the bake worker.
- Removes the repeat ruzstd decompression of boot records; the coldload doc measured boot.hba zstd reads at 31 ms in the boot walk window.
- Removes a 59 KB clone plus full Region parse per terrain batch.
findings.novelty_check:
Advances two open leads:
- ledger-open:256 '(perf-oct) zstd boot.hba reads (31 ms) … Documented, not changed'.
- '(reviews) fetch_landblock_heightmaps/fetch_subdivided_landblocks parse full Region every call | Per batch; unverified'.

What this adds: the concrete mechanisms with file:line (no resident decompressed copy; the boot-first probe with per-probe binrw parse on every non-boot read, which neither lead mentions; the String-key allocation), verification that the Region lead is real (and the misleading doc comment), and a byte-identical design. No git commit touches HbaReader caching or ShardCache keys.
findings.verify_how:
1. Orchestrator: cargo test -p holtburger-dat (archive tests, 9) and -p holtburger-resource-http (get_file_shared Arc-identity wrapper test, shard_cache tests), plus new tests: two boot reads ptr_eq; a boot miss does zero entry parses (counter).
2. surfbench.mjs on base vs new: identical hashes and lower decodeMs. Its timed pass re-reads every record from the cache, so it exercises the probe path.
3. Add a `__hbShardCache.bootProbes` counter to quantify reads per LB live.

findings.title: SurfacePixels and terrain/icon pixel getters still copy each plane twice (Rust clone, then glue .slice())
findings.area: wasm-bindgen getters: SurfacePixels / TerrainTexture / TerrainAlphaMask / IconPixels
findings.evidence:
- lib.rs:12352 `pixels(&self) -> Vec<u8> { self.pixels.as_ref().clone() }`, :12374 normal_pixels and :12380 height_pixels do the same. The doc comment at lib.rs:12186-12189 confirms the getters still return owned Vec clones.
- Glue pkg/holtburger_web.js:15068-15073 (pixels), :15049-15054 (normalPixels), :15025-15030 (heightPixels) then does `getArrayU8FromWasm0(...).slice()` followed by `__wbindgen_free`. Net per plane: a dlmalloc alloc, a memcpy, a JS alloc, a second memcpy and a free.
- The same pattern is in TerrainTexture/AlphaMask pixels (lib.rs:3663, :3731) and IconPixels (lib.rs:15863).
- Consumer: bake_transfer.js:327-329 reads each plane once and transfers it.
- Precedent: Perf T3 already converted ModelMesh positions/uvs/normals to `js_sys::Float32Array::from(self.x.as_slice())` (lib.rs:7670-7679), one copy and no transient.
- These pixel planes are the largest buffers crossing the boundary: RGBA up to 1 MB, normal 0.75 MB, height 0.25 MB per 512² surface.
findings.proposal:
Change the five getters to return `js_sys::Uint8Array::from(self.pixels.as_slice())` (likewise normal_pixels, height_pixels, and the terrain/icon `pixels`). The JS type stays Uint8Array and the contents are identical. The result is a fresh non-shared ArrayBuffer, so the postMessage transfer path and pushBuffer's SAB guard behave as before.

Optionally do the same for ModelMesh's remaining small Vec getters (surfaceIndices, sidesTypes, polygonIds, sideKinds, subsetStippled, bakedLightRgb; lib.rs:7681-7754).
findings.expected_gain: Derived: removes one full memcpy plus a malloc/free per plane, about 0.5 MB per average surface, roughly 80 MB of copying per 232-surface academy statics batch. That is about 10–25 ms of bake-worker CPU (under 1% of decode). It also removes up to 1 MB transient linear-memory peaks per read; wasm memory never shrinks.
findings.novelty_check: Advances ledger-open:307 '(perf-summer) De-indexed geometry output and cloning bindgen getters | offline indexed buffers + transferable views never built'. T3 (ledger-compact:212) fixed only ModelMesh's three bulk planes. This adds the specific remaining getters with file:line and an S-effort path that needs no I2 redesign.
findings.verify_how:
1. node tests/test_bake_transfer.mjs and test_surface_planes.mjs (targeted) against the rebuilt pkg: payload bytes identical.
2. surfbench.mjs hashes identical; it reads every getter after the timed pass.
3. A node microbench timing sp.pixels/normalPixels/heightPixels reads, base vs new pkg.

findings.title: Physics BSP leaf polygons are looked up through a SipHash HashMap<u16,…> on every leaf test
findings.area: holtburger-dat physics/transition + holtburger-world spatial (per-frame TickMovement, remoteSweep, missiles)
findings.evidence:
**The lookups:**
- CellPhysicsBsp.polys is `HashMap<u16, ResolvedPolygon>` (scene.rs:1039); ObjPhysicsBsp likewise (obj_collision.rs:133).
- Every BSP leaf polygon test does `polys.get(&pid)` with the default SipHash-1-3 RandomState: physics.rs:296 (sphere_intersects_solid), :425, :559; transition/bspnode_poly.rs:151 (leaf_sphere_intersects_poly); bspnode_solid.rs:191; bspnode_walkable.rs:75, :212; resolver_find.rs:177; bsptree_adjust.rs:115.
- Other integer-keyed per-transition maps also use SipHash: CELL_HANDLE_CACHE `HashMap<u32,…>` (faithful_bridge.rs:866), the scene cell_* maps (scene.rs:1287-1649), BSP_CACHE (obj_collision.rs:183).
- No custom hasher exists anywhere in apps/crates.

**Why a hasher swap is safe:** on wasm32-unknown-unknown, std seeds RandomState from allocation addresses (std/src/sys/random/unsupported.rs `hashmap_random_keys`), and native tests use OS-random keys. Map iteration order (scene.rs:707, :1119 fan triangulation) is therefore already session-arbitrary, and the tests are order-agnostic. rustc-hash 2.1.2 and foldhash are already in Cargo.lock.
findings.proposal:
Add `pub type PolyMap = HashMap<u16, ResolvedPolygon, BuildHasherDefault<FxHasher>>` in holtburger-dat::physics and use it in the about 15 signatures that take `&HashMap<u16, ResolvedPolygon>`. Add a crate-local `FastMap<K,V>` alias for the u32/usize-keyed scene, cell-handle and BSP caches.

A stronger follow-up: since DAT poly ids are dense 0..n, store `Vec<ResolvedPolygon>` plus an id→slot table to get O(1) array indexing. Keep the HashMap only where ids are sparse.

No flag is needed: collision results are identical up to the already-arbitrary iteration order.
findings.expected_gain: Derived: about 20–30 ns saved per leaf-poly lookup (SipHash over a u16 plus probe, vs about 2 ns Fx or about 1 ns indexed). Assumed volume: hundreds to low thousands of lookups per transition-heavy frame, so roughly 0.02–0.3 ms per frame of main-thread CPU, growing with moving remotes under remoteSweep. It is small but on the saturated renderer thread.
findings.novelty_check:
- No ledger, git or url-flags hit for hasher/SipHash/FxHash/foldhash.
- Related open leads (statics_aabbs_near_pose copies, shared geometry deep copy, remote_ground_at scan) are different mechanisms.
- The 'GC ~2 KB/frame' and 'chatter' walls are unaffected (Rust-internal compute).
findings.verify_how:
1. Orchestrator: cargo test -p holtburger-dat --lib transition and -p holtburger-world (academy/townnetwork wedge, remote_* and setup_mover_body suites) all green; they are order-agnostic because native keys are random.
2. A native timing of a transition replay fixture (e.g. academy_wedge_tests' driver loop), before vs after.
3. Live: __framePhase p0 SIM mean at a spawn camp, as part of the owed remoteSweep crowd measurement.

verdicts.code_truth: Every citation checks out. Root Cargo.toml has only [profile.dist] (:119, `lto = "thin"` at :122), [profile.profiling] (:124) and the dev per-package overrides (:155-200). There is no [profile.release] anywhere in the workspace, so a release build uses Cargo defaults: lto=false (thin-local) and codegen-units=16. apps/holtburger-web/Cargo.toml has no [package.metadata.wasm-pack]; wasm-pack is 0.14.0 and its default release wasm-opt is `-O` (= binaryen -Os). .cargo/config.toml:18-19 sets only `-zstack-size`, plus `[build] jobs = 2`. The pkg wasm is 7,601,324 B with no name section; I re-parsed it. Two citations are only printed hints, not invocations: scripts/serve.py:967 and scripts/net-review/ci-smoke.sh:36. `wasm-pack build --profile <PROFILE>` exists in 0.14.0, so the custom-profile route works. Correction: `panic="abort"` does nothing here, because wasm32-unknown-unknown already aborts on panic. lib.rs is 63,411 lines.
verdicts.novelty: New. ledger-compact, ledger-open and ledger-walls have no lto, codegen-units or wasm-opt-level hits. git log has only the dev-profile commits c628b329 and 81567301. The docs mention wasm-opt only as the name-section fingerprint (HANDOFF-2026-08-13) and as `wasm-opt -O -g` builds for profiling. url-flags.md has nothing.
verdicts.wall_conflict: No settled law is contradicted. The finder correctly handles walls 13/131/147: dev detection keys on custom sections, and LTO keeps the name section absent. Two walls bound the payoff. First, the 'Pipeline invariants' wall: 45+ in-shape attempts topped out at 4 ms or less. Second, coldload §4.28 itself says the 2.8x decode win 'did not move the furnished time on this rig: the gap is the bake worker's record walk'. Build risk: the 'rustfmt on lib.rs hits 4.2 GB' trap suggests fat LTO plus 1 CGU over a 63K-line crate and its whole dependency graph could hit the 3.5 GB capped-build limit. Thin LTO is the safer first arm.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical in practice. LTO, CGU count and binaryen -O3 do not change IEEE results: Rust/LLVM do no FP contraction or reassociation without fast-math, and binaryen -O3 does not alter float semantics. The surfbench hash comparison the finder proposes is the right guard.
verdicts.gain_realism: Overstated. The decode hot loops (grey_morph_with, window_extreme, seam_normal_rgb8, texture to_rgba8) sit wholly inside holtburger-dat with `#[inline(always)]` helpers. Cross-crate calls happen per surface or per row, not per texel, so LTO adds little there. Thin-local LTO already inlines across the 16 CGUs inside a crate, and since Rust 1.75 small leaf functions are cross-crate inlinable by default. Binaryen -O3 vs -Os is usually a few percent. Corrected estimate (assumed): about 0-8% less wasm CPU and about 5-15% smaller wasm. On the bake-worker statics decode that is roughly 0.1-0.4 s of a 2.5-5.9 s stretch, and that stretch is not the furnished-time long pole. Per-frame main-thread effect is near zero. Costs: release build time about 1.5-3x, and peak build RSS must be recorded.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The release wasm is built with Cargo default lto=false, 16 codegen units and wasm-pack's default wasm-opt -O (-Os). A thin-LTO arm (then fat LTO with CGU=1 if it fits under capped-build) plus `wasm-opt = ["-O3"]` is a cheap, pixel-identical, file-free A/B (env CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_*). Expected effect is modest: a few percent of wasm CPU and roughly 5-15% size, mainly at load. If it wins, ship it as a dedicated `--profile` so native builds keep fast compiles. Drop panic=abort, which is already the wasm32 behaviour. Record build time and peak RSS, and run the arms one at a time on the orchestrator only.

verdicts.code_truth: Confirmed: the shipped wasm's target_features section is [+mutable-globals, +nontrapping-fptoint, +bulk-memory, +sign-ext, +reference-types, +multivalue], with no simd128 (I parsed it). .cargo/config.toml:19 has only the stack-size flag. height_seam.rs: min_nn at :169 and max_nn at :175 are compare+select; the vertical passes are at :267 and :276 and the final pass at :286, as cited. lib.rs:14751 is the height-plane `(v.clamp(0,1)*255) as u8` map. texture.rs:333-341 and :350-358 are the indexed `source_data[i*3]` loops plus `extend_from_slice`, as cited. glam has 0 source references. Two claims are wrong. (1) seam_normal_rgb8 (height_seam.rs:963-975) is not usefully vectorizable: it gathers through `height[ys[..]+xs[..]]` tables and stores at stride 3, and wasm SIMD has no gather. (2) The pixel-identity claim misses a dependency. holtburger-dat depends on jpeg-decoder 0.3.2 (`default-features = false`, so `platform_independent` is off), and texture.rs:535 decodes the CustomRawJpeg format with it (79 retail records); the shipped wasm contains that path ('unsupported JPEG pixel format' string present). jpeg-decoder's src/arch/mod.rs switches the IDCT and the YCbCr→RGB conversion to wasm.rs under `cfg(all(target_feature = "simd128", target_arch = "wasm32"))`. wasm.rs says outright that its Q15 `i16x8_q15mulr_sat` IDCT has 'slight differences in rounding' and constants of 'different precision'. Its colour conversion uses SHIFT=6 with Q15 multiplies, against the scalar path's FIXED_POINT_OFFSET 20 arithmetic (decoder.rs:1491-1508).
verdicts.novelty: New. simd, simd128 and target-feature appear nowhere in the ledgers, git log or url-flags.md; the only RUSTFLAGS docs are the atomics/threads SCOPE-2.5 experiments.
verdicts.wall_conflict: Brushes wall 135 (wasm chatter) only by name, as the finder says. Coldload §4.28/§4.30 bounds the payoff: decode is about 3.4 s of a 27.9 s academy pipeline, and the record walk dominates. 'Laptop SwiftShader cannot judge GPU' does not apply; this is CPU work.
verdicts.visual_safety: NOT pixel-identical as proposed. A crate-wide +simd128 silently swaps jpeg-decoder onto its approximate SIMD IDCT and colour conversion, so every CustomRawJpeg texture can change by about ±1 LSB in places. The proposed surfbench check (313 interior surfaces) may contain no JPEG surface, so it can pass while JPEG textures differ. The fix is cheap: add `features = ["platform_independent"]` to the workspace jpeg-decoder dependency, which forces the scalar path regardless of target features. Everything else holds up: f32x4 min/max/sqrt and trunc_sat are exact, integer lanes are exact, and LLVM will not vectorize FP reductions without reassociation. With that feature, and a JPEG hash added to the gate, it can be byte-identical. Otherwise it must ship as needs-eyetest.
verdicts.gain_realism: Assumed and optimistic. Only part of grey_morph vectorizes (the vertical and final row passes). The horizontal window_extreme prefix/suffix scans carry a loop dependence, seam_normal_rgb8 is gather-bound, and whether Rust bounds checks get hoisted in the row loops is unverified. Corrected estimate: about 1.05-1.25x on total surface decode. That is roughly 0.2-0.8 s off the 2.5-5.9 s bake-worker statics stretch, which is not the furnished-time long pole. Per-frame effect is about zero. A browser floor of Chrome 91+ is acceptable for the owner.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Enabling +simd128 is a cheap experiment that could shorten bake-worker surface decode by a modest amount, mostly through the grey_morph row passes; seam_normal_rgb8 will not benefit. It is not automatically pixel-identical: jpeg-decoder 0.3.2 switches to an approximate Q15 SIMD IDCT and colour conversion under target_feature=simd128. It must be paired with `jpeg-decoder = { version = "0.3", default-features = false, features = ["platform_independent"] }`, and the verification gate must include JPEG (CustomRawJpeg) texture hashes, not only the 313 surfbench surfaces. Build the arm in a separate target dir on /mnt, orchestrator only.

verdicts.code_truth: Confirmed. crc32_ieee at catalog.rs:354-364 is the bitwise 8-step-per-byte loop with no table. read_from computes it over the whole body at catalog.rs:248. manifest_source.rs:678 and :826 call NamespaceCatalog::read_from. pack.rs:172 (HbpPack::parse) and :370 (HBSI1) CRC each body. insert_pack parses at pack.rs:655 before the duplicate `resident.contains_key` check at :657. The doc comment at pack.rs:155-156 says the CRC is a backstop and the controller's sha-on-receipt is the integrity gate. The served catalogs in ~/hb-serve/dist/current/manifest are eor-portal.bin 1,499,312 B and tex catalogs of 60,126 + 56,939 + 79,873 B (about 197 KB in total, as the finder said). I re-ran crc_probe.mjs: bitwise 24.7 ms (61 MB/s) vs slicing-by-8 3.8 ms, CRCs equal.
verdicts.novelty: New. The only ledger or git hit is 81567301 'CRC32 fix', which raised the dev-profile opt-level for the same bitwise loop; its own comment says crc32_ieee was about 19% of a dev town load. ledger-open:362 'Pack admission CPU spikes (decompress at insert)' covers zstd, not the CRC. No url-flag.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None. The change is byte-identical CPU work that fits the 'system work in Rust' rule. The pack half applies only under packSource, which is DEV-off and owner-gated.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical: same polynomial, init and final XOR, and the same public signature.
verdicts.gain_realism: The JS proxy probably overstates the wasm cost by up to about 2x: LLVM compiles the bitwise loop at about 4 cycles per bit (about 100 MB/s). Corrected estimate: about 12-25 ms of boot CPU per instance on the laptop for about 2.5 MB of catalogs (less on the 1070's desktop CPU), dropping to about 2-4 ms. That is on the main thread and in the bake worker, plus each regional catalog load during streaming. The pack-admission saving (about 6x of CRC CPU) is dormant until packSource ships.
verdicts.corrected_claim: crc32_ieee is a bitwise CRC run over every catalog (eor-portal 1.5 MB, tex and regional catalogs) in each wasm instance, and over every pack body under packSource. A const-table slicing-by-8 body with the same signature is byte-identical and about 6x faster, saving roughly 10-20 ms of boot CPU per instance plus some per regional-catalog load. Moving insert_pack's duplicate check ahead of HbpPack::parse is a free extra.

verdicts.code_truth: All four mechanisms are real. (a) get_file_by_key (manifest_source.rs:1237-1252) and get_file_shared (:1259-1272) probe `self.boot.get_file_by_key(key)` before the shard cache, and boot is `HbaReader<Vec<u8>>` (:333). archive.rs find_entry_with_namespace_id (:256-288) binary-searches by calling read_entry_at (:298-302) once per probe: a 60-byte read_exact_at_compat into a stack buffer plus `HbaEntry::read` via binrw. A namespace missing from boot returns early through lookup_namespace_span. (b) read_entry_data (:305-341) allocates `vec![0; comp_size]` and runs decompress_zstd on every read, and the comment at manifest_source.rs:1261-1263 admits there is no resident Arc. (c) `owned(key)` at :310-312 allocates a String; ShardCache uses a std SipHash HashMap (shard_cache.rs:125). (d) resolve_region_land_height_table (lib.rs:2933-2947) calls get_file_by_key, an owned clone of the 59 KB record, and then runs a full Region::unpack. It is called from fetch_landblock_heightmaps (:3172) and fetch_subdivided_landblocks (:3375), and the doc at :2930 says 'Cheap: a cache read + 256-f32 parse'. One gap: SpellTable, the largest boot record, is read once, in load_world_bootstrap (lib.rs:49056-49086), not repeatedly.
verdicts.novelty: Advances two open leads: ledger-open:256 'zstd boot.hba reads (31 ms) … documented, not changed' and the reviews lead 'fetch_landblock_heightmaps/fetch_subdivided_landblocks parse full Region every call | unverified'. The finder adds new detail: the boot-first probe with a binrw parse per probe on every non-boot portal read, the String-key allocation, and confirmation that the Region lead is real with a misleading doc. git log has nothing on HbaReader caching or ShardCache keys.
verdicts.wall_conflict: Bounded by three walls: 'Cold interior fetch is round-trip structure, not bytes', 'Pipeline invariants: 45+ in-shape attempts topped out ≤4 ms or 0', and 'Record-level dedup measured 0.00 MB'. These do not refute it, but they cap the gain. The resident-boot cache also adds memory (decompressed SpellTable 1.48 MB plus the 3 MB texture set per instance, times three instances) unless it is restricted to small records.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical. These are pure caching and indexing changes that return the same bytes.
verdicts.gain_realism: Overstated. Each portal-namespace read saves about 0.3-0.8 µs (about 10 small binrw parses plus a String alloc and SipHash). At about 1-3K reads per landblock bake that is about 1-3 ms per streaming burst, mostly in the bake worker, off the saturated main thread. The '31 ms boot zstd' is mostly first-time decompression of large once-read records (SpellTable is read once at bootstrap), which a resident cache cannot remove; it saves only repeat reads. The Region memo saves about 0.1-0.3 ms per terrain batch on the main instance.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The V2Source read path has real small inefficiencies: a boot-first binary search that binrw-parses about 10 HbaEntry records on every portal-namespace miss, an owned-String plus SipHash shard key, re-decompression on repeat boot hits, and a full 59 KB clone plus Region::unpack per terrain batch (the doc's 'cheap' claim is wrong). Pre-decoding the boot index, interning the shard key and memoising the land height table are byte-identical. Expected savings are a few ms per streaming burst, mostly in the bake worker. They will not move the 31 ms first-time boot decompression or the furnished time. The low-risk part is the Region memo plus the decoded boot index; the boot resident cache should hold small records only.

verdicts.code_truth: Confirmed. lib.rs:12352 `pixels(&self) -> Vec<u8> { self.pixels.as_ref().clone() }`, with normal_pixels at :12374 and height_pixels at :12380 the same; the doc at :12186-12189 says the getters still return owned Vec clones. In the glue pkg/holtburger_web.js, heightPixels (:15025-15030), normalPixels (:15049-15054) and pixels (:15068-15073) each do `getArrayU8FromWasm0(...).slice()` followed by `wasm.__wbindgen_free`. TerrainTexture/AlphaMask `pixels` (lib.rs:3662-3664, :3730-3732) and IconPixels (:15863) are `self.pixels.clone()`. bake_transfer.js serializeSurfacePixels (:327-329) reads each plane once through pushBuffer and transfers it. The precedent at lib.rs:7670-7679 uses js_sys::Float32Array::from(slice). js-sys `From<&[u8]>` is `new Uint8Array(view)`, a single copy into a non-shared buffer, which AUDIT-sab-views-2026-07-24 also relies on, so transfer stays legal. The finder missed SubdividedLandblockMesh's getters (lib.rs:3230-3262: positions, normals, acLightNormals, terrainCodes, roadCodes, indices), which are also `.clone()` and double-copy on the main instance.
verdicts.novelty: Advances ledger-open:307 '(perf-summer) … cloning bindgen getters | part of I2; … transferable views never built'. verdicts.wall_conflict: None. This is bytes copied, not the refuted crossing-count chatter. The 'wasm-bindgen free() not idempotent' wall does not apply, since getters return fresh arrays and no frees are added.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical. Same JS type (Uint8Array, or Float32Array for terrain), same contents, a fresh non-shared ArrayBuffer, so postMessage transfer and pushBuffer's SAB guard behave as before.
verdicts.gain_realism: Plausible as stated: one memcpy plus a malloc/free of up to about 1 MB per plane removed. That is roughly 10-25 ms of bake-worker CPU per 232-surface batch (under 1% of decode) and fewer transient linear-memory peaks, which matter because wasm memory never shrinks. Small and mostly off the main thread. The terrain getters add a little on the main instance.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The SurfacePixels pixels/normalPixels/heightPixels getters, the TerrainTexture/AlphaMask/IconPixels pixels getters and the SubdividedLandblockMesh plane getters still clone in Rust and then copy again in glue (`.slice()` + free). Returning js_sys::Uint8Array::from / Float32Array::from / Uint32Array::from(slice), as T3 did for ModelMesh, is a byte-identical S change. findings.title: Parent-local particles re-resolve their part anchor once per particle per tick, and each resolve walks the scene-graph parent chain about five times
findings.evidence:
particle_emitter.js:505-528: in updateParticles, `for (let i = 0; i < this.info.maxParticles; i++) { ... if (this.info.isParentLocal) { frame = this._resolveAnchorFrame(); } ... this.particles[i].update(..., frame) }`. The anchor frame is recomputed for every live slot, but it cannot change inside the loop: particle.update only writes the slot mesh, which is never an ancestor of the anchor.

particle_emitter.js:182-201 _resolveAnchorFrame does three things for a part-anchored emitter: reads `this.parent.partFrames[this.partIndex]`, then `this._scene.worldToLocal(f.position)` (updateWorldMatrix(true,false) plus a Matrix4 invert), then `this._scene.getWorldQuaternion(sceneQ).invert()` (another chain walk plus a decompose).

setup_rig.js:209-211 (the proxy getter) runs `part.updateWorldMatrix(true, false); part.getWorldPosition(frame.position); part.getWorldQuaternion(frame.quaternion);`. In three r184 (Object3D.js:996-1018), getWorldPosition and getWorldQuaternion each call updateWorldMatrix(true,false) again, so the getter walks the chain three times where one walk would do.

The same proxy is read once per emitter per tick by shouldEmitParticle→_emitterOrigin (:333), by emitParticle (:492), by rp6CullSphere (particle_manager.js:1563-1567) and by the tier-1 light/distort resolver (particle_manager.js:1852-1858).

DAT census of client_portal.dat (scratch pl_census.py):
- 814 of 2,051 emitters are isParentLocal.
- 9,644 of 10,758 PhysicsScript CreateParticle hooks anchor to a part rather than the root; 3,279 of those use parent-local emitters.
- Parent-local emitters keep about 14.9 particles live on average (estimated as min(max, lifespan/birthrate)).

Node bench with real three r184 and the real setup_rig.js (scratch anchor_bench.mjs, proxy_variant_bench.mjs):
- _resolveAnchorFrame costs 1.69 µs/call today.
- A single-walk proxy costs 1.10 µs/call and is bit-identical.
- The direct root-relative compose costs 0.16 µs/call.
findings.proposal:
Change 1, in ParticleEmitter.updateParticles: resolve the anchor once per tick, lazily on the first live slot, as `let frame = null; ... if (isParentLocal) frame ??= this._resolveAnchorFrame();`. Reuse that frame for the shouldEmitParticle/_emitterOrigin and emitParticle calls in the same tick. It is the same `_anchorScratch` object, and Particle.init copies out of it.

Change 2, in createPartFramesProxy: call `part.updateWorldMatrix(true,false)` once, then read `frame.position.setFromMatrixPosition(part.matrixWorld)` and `part.matrixWorld.decompose(_p, frame.quaternion, _s)`. This drops two of the three walks; the node probe shows the result is bit-identical.

Optional escape flag `?anchorHoist=off`, default on. Both changes are pure common-subexpression removal with identical floats, so no eye-test is needed.
findings.expected_gain: Derived from the node bench on the laptop CPU. Each parent-local, part-anchored emitter saves (live−1)×~1.7 µs per tick: about 24 µs at the DAT mean of 14.9 live particles. With 30-100 such emitters live in a spell fight (buff and debuff scripts on several bodies; the emitter count is my assumption), that is about 0.7-2.4 ms per frame on the main thread. The proxy change also cuts every remaining partFrames read by about 35% (1.69→1.10 µs), which helps the RP6 recheck and the fx light/distort resolves.
findings.novelty_check: Searched the ledger (walls, compact, open, both slices) for partFrames, resolveAnchor, anchor frame, worldToLocal, isParentLocal and per-particle: no hits on this mechanism. The only per-particle ledger items are about pooling (wall 165) and Float32Array storage (open #6), which are different. git log has nothing for partFrames, anchor frame or parentLocal. url-flags.md has no anchor flag.
findings.verify_how: Node test: build a rig (a Group with 34 part Groups under an entitiesGroup under a worldRoot rotated −π/2) and a parent-local emitter on part 5 with about 20 live particles. Animate the parts over 200 ticks and record every slot's position, quaternion and scale; the arrays must be bit-identical before and after the change. Wrap Object3D.prototype.updateWorldMatrix to count calls: expect about N×5 per tick before and about 1-2 after. On the 1070: spell-cast storm at a training dummy or a group buff, comparing main-thread ms per frame with `?anchorHoist=off` against the default, fresh profile per arm.

findings.title: Frozen static script anchors still walk their parent chain: rp6TrueSphere makes the bf474c67 frozen-anchor shortcut unreachable for part-anchored emitters, which is 90% of them
findings.area: particles/particle_manager.js rp6CullSphere + statics.js frozen anchors + fx_lights dedupe
findings.evidence:
particle_manager.js:1563-1573 checks `partFrame = trueSphere && pi !== -1 && ... ? parent.partFrames[pi] : null` first and only reaches the bf474c67 fast path (`else if (parent.userData.__anchorFrozen === true) out.setFromMatrixPosition(parent.matrixWorld)`) when there is no part frame.

statics.js:6108-6117 gives every Setup-model static anchor part frames (attachStaticPartFrames, :5452-5476) and then freezes the subtree (_freezeStaticScriptAnchor, :5131-5139). statics.js:5935-5936 keeps hook part 0 as partIndex 0.

The DAT confirms who this affects: Linvak drizzle setups 0x02000407 and 0x02000406 have default scripts 0x33000113 and 0x33000114, whose emitters 0x32000142 and 0x32000143 hang off part 0. Across all setup default scripts there are 6,860 part-anchored CreateParticle hooks against 719 root-anchored.

So every drizzle, torch and portal emitter takes the proxy, which does three updateWorldMatrix walks up to staticsGroup/worldRoot/scene. Because the anchor and part are frozen, those walks only return the frozen part.matrixWorld anyway; my node probe shows the read is bit-identical.

The recheck is not staggered: particle_manager.js:2546 `const recheck = (this._rp6Frame % interval) === 0` with interval 6 (:171), and the loop at :2558-2563 rechecks every emitter in particleTable on that same frame.

Node bench (scratch frozen_proxy_bench.mjs): 6,400 frozen part-anchored anchors cost 9.70 ms per full recheck (1.52 µs/call) through the proxy, against 1.75 ms reading the frozen matrixWorld (most of that is a decompose the cull does not need).

The same frozen-constant walk is repeated in two more places:
- emitParticle→_resolveAnchorFrame on every drizzle spawn (proxy plus two `_scene` walks).
- fx_lights.js:422-423, which calls `s.resolvePosition(s.position)` on every lit emitter before the >60 m skip, every 500 ms, through _bindTier1's resolver (_emitterOrigin + scene.localToWorld).
findings.proposal:
Change 1, in createPartFramesProxy (setup_rig.js): when `part.matrixWorldAutoUpdate === false && part.matrixAutoUpdate === false`, skip updateWorldMatrix and read part.matrixWorld directly. This is bit-identical, as proven.

Change 2, in rp6CullSphere: for `parent.userData.__anchorFrozen`, cache the cull centre on the emitter the first time (`emitter._rp6FrozenCentre`), since a frozen anchor never moves, and skip the quaternion decompose.

Change 3, in ParticleEmitter._resolveAnchorFrame: memoise the `_scene`-local frame for frozen anchors (`this._frozenAnchorFrame`). Invalidate it if the anchor's `__anchorFrozen` epoch or `__scriptEpoch` changes. This uses the same constancy assumption bf474c67 already relies on.

findings.title: _appendInstances rebuilds each emitter's bucket-key and material-signature strings every tick (about 0.9 µs per on-screen alpha emitter)
findings.evidence:
particle_manager.js:2839 builds a template-literal bucket key (`${gfx}|${layer}...`) per emitter per tick. :2842 then calls `sharedAlphaBuckets.acquire(key, this._scene, _alphaMatSig(emitter._instBaseMat), () => {...}, _sharedFrameId())` for every alpha emitter. Per call that means:
- _alphaMatSig (:676-680) builds an 8-element array and `.join('|')`, including `mat.color.getHex()`, which runs ColorManagement linear→sRGB with pow per channel.
- A fresh closure is allocated.
- _defaultFrameId (:665-671) reads `document.timeline.currentTime`, a DOM getter, once per emitter.

None of these inputs change between ticks.

The drizzle uses the alpha path. Its emitters 0x32000142 and 0x32000143 use hw GfxObj 0x01001166, whose surface 0x0800005D has type 0x4 (ClipMap, not additive), per the scratch surf_one.py run. So baseIsAdditive is false, _instAlpha is true and it takes the shared alpha path.

Node bench (scratch sig_bench.mjs, 3,000 alpha emitters, real three materials): 2.787 ms per tick today (929 ns per emitter) against 0.142 ms with the key and signature cached on the emitter. The bench excludes the DOM getter and the closure.
findings.proposal: Cache the bucket key on the emitter: `emitter._instBucketKey`, recomputed only when `_instKey`, `renderLayer`, `_instAlpha` or `skyGlow` differ from the cached tuple (store `_instKeyLayer`). Cache `emitter._alphaSig = _alphaMatSig(base)` when instancing is set up (addEmitter, _applyInstancing); re-stamp it from the code that mutates the material's map, colour or alphaTest (the additiveFog switch walks materials and can re-stamp). Read `_sharedFrameId()` once per manager tick and pass it in. Hoist the makeIm closure to a per-emitter cached function, or pass a factory with args. Bucket assignment and instance data stay identical.
findings.expected_gain: Microbench on the laptop CPU: about 0.88 µs saved per on-screen alpha emitter per tick, plus one DOM getter call each (not measured). At Linvak, about 76% of roughly 5,000 static emitters are live (rp6TravelReach doc), so up to about 3,800 alpha appends per tick, or up to about 3.3 ms per frame on the laptop basis. Holtburg-class towns with a few hundred live alpha emitters save about 0.2-0.5 ms. Additive emitters save the key build, about 50-100 ns each.
findings.novelty_check: rg in the ledger for alphaMatSig, bucket key, signature, document.timeline and frameId: no hits. `git log -S _alphaMatSig` shows only its introduction (3770cbe4, the one-smoke-sort commit). Wall 135 (GC ~2 KB/frame) is a GC claim; this is CPU time and was measured. No url flag covers it.

Assert identical bucket maps (keys, sharedAlphaBuckets entries) and identical instanceMatrix/instanceColor arrays per tick, cached against uncached. Microbench: the scratch sig_bench.mjs. On the 1070: Linvak Tukal main-thread ms per frame A/B, with optional `?appendKeyCache=off`.

findings.title: Every particle bucket re-uploads its whole instance buffer (capacity ≥256) each tick, not just the n instances drawn
findings.evidence:
particle_manager.js:3128-3131 does `im.count = b.n; im.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true; if (im.instanceColor) im.instanceColor.needsUpdate = true;` with no update range. SharedAlphaBuckets.finalize at :740-743 does the same.

Buckets start at `_INST_BUCKET_MIN_CAP = 256` (:853) and _growBucket doubles the capacity (:862-866).

three r184 WebGLAttributes.js:87-90: when `updateRanges.length === 0` it calls `gl.bufferSubData(bufferType, 0, array)`, the full array. So each non-empty bucket uploads at least 256×64 B of matrices plus 256×12 B of colour (about 19.5 KB) per tick even when n=4, and grown buckets upload their whole power-of-two capacity.

The sibling FX buffers already limit uploads to the live count: particle_fx_kids.js:397-398, fx_showcase.js:880-881, fx_ribbons.js:661-662, fx_decal_effect.js:582-583 and animated_scenery.js:1055-1057 all use clearUpdateRanges plus addUpdateRange.

The fx glow twins share these same attribute objects (fx_glow_effect.js:107-108), so a smaller upload helps both passes. CrGpuMain was the second saturated stage (79%, 15.2 ms/frame WebGL decode).

Example: 40 buckets is about 0.8 MB/frame (about 40 MB/s at 50 fps) of transfer-buffer memcpy plus ANGLE→D3D11 BufferSubData on CrGpuMain, mostly avoidable for small buckets (5-60× less); large grown buckets roughly halve. Expect a fraction of a ms of CrGpuMain per frame in particle-dense towns; the scale needs gpu_thread_split.py.
