findings.title: Instanced synthesized sprite particles (billboard:true) face a fixed direction instead of the camera, and can go edge-on and vanish
findings.evidence:
particle_manager.js:1208-1232 _billboardEmitter takes `const parent = mesh.parent` and, when that is null, does `_bbMeshWorld.copy(mesh.position)` (a _scene-local AC-frame position) and subtracts it from the world-space `camera.position`. The parent-quaternion conversion is skipped as well.

Under instancing, slot meshes are never parented: addEmitter passes `onMeshActive: useInst ? _NOOP` (:2296) and emitParticle calls _onMeshActive instead of scene.add (particle_emitter.js:437-441). So the facing direction is computed in mixed spaces and stays constant as the camera moves.

_billboardEmitterRetail (:1312-1320) handles this correctly by localising the camera through scene.matrixWorld.

Both production managers opt in: `instancing: true` at entities.js:15036 and statics.js:5629.

These emitters carry billboard:true: every synthesized component emitter gets it as the default (particle_attach.js:411), and gemSparkle sets it explicitly (gemSparkle.js:239). gemSparkle, brazier and breathFog are live by default: their readers are `_boolFlag(name, visualAllEffects())` (vfx_flags.js:233-270), visualAllEffects defaults true (:103-111) and visualEnabled defaults true (vfx_catalog.js:27-36), despite DEFAULT-OFF comments.

test_particle_billboard.mjs:52-59 builds its manager without `instancing`, so the production path is never tested. The 1070 validation of particleBillboard (url-flags.md:386) dates from 2026-06-25, before instancing went default-on on 10-06.

Probe with the real ParticleManager (scratch bb_instanced_test.mjs), worst |n·toCam| over 6 azimuths:
- instancing:false gives 1.0000 (faces the camera).
- instancing:true gives 0.0000 (edge-on at some azimuths).

A standalone replica at Holtburg-scale coordinates (bb_probe.mjs) gives the same fixed normal (0,−0.71,−0.71) local for every camera position.
findings.proposal: Pass the manager scene into _billboardEmitter the same way _billboardEmitterRetail gets it. Compute the camera in _scene-local space once per tick: `this._instSortCam` already is that, computed at :2566-2570. For each particle, compute dir = camLocal − mesh.position in local space, with no world round trip. That is correct for both paths, because a per-mesh slot's parent is _scene, and it also removes the per-particle `parent.getWorldQuaternion()` chain walk the per-mesh path does today. While there, hoist _billboardEmitterRetail's per-emitter `scene.matrixWorld` invert to once per tick. Add an instancing:true arm to test_particle_billboard.mjs. This restores the camera-facing look that was validated before instancing went default-on.
findings.expected_gain: Visual: the default-on synthesized sprites (gem sparkles, brazier embers and smoke, breath fog, plus the terrain swamp, sand and volcano emitters when enabled) face the camera again instead of a fixed tilt that goes edge-on from some azimuths. A small CPU saving comes from dropping the per-particle chain walk on the per-mesh path.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger: billboard items are the billboardTickGate perf work (covered #161), the particleBillboard=off census refutation (refuted, perf only) and the statics billboard leak; none mention instanced facing. git log: _billboardEmitter was last touched 07-28 (48236510) and 06-25 (442e5330), before particleInstancing (b60e2085 07-14 opt-in, default-on 10-06). The url-flags particleBillboard row's validation predates the instancing default.
findings.verify_how: Run the scratch test, which uses the real ParticleManager: current code gives instancing:true worst |n·toCam| = 0.0000, and after the fix it should read 1.0000 for both arms. Add that arm to test_particle_billboard.mjs (it must fail on reverted source). On the 1070: eye-test a gem-sparkle item and a brazier from four azimuths at high/ultra; sprites should stay face-on, not appear as slivers.

findings.title: Hot quaternion writes pay three.js's Euler sync: 34 rig parts per human per frame, three per spinning particle per tick, and corpses posed twice every frame
findings.area: motion/motion_sequence.js poseRigAt + particle.js GR update + ragdoll.js applyFrozenPose
findings.evidence:
motion_sequence.js:96-99: poseRigAt calls `g.position.set(...)` and `g.quaternion.set(...)` for every part of every ticked rig every frame (entities.js:17713-17715 one-shot, 17747-17751 cycle).

three r184 Object3D.js:151-155 wires `quaternion._onChange(() => rotation.setFromQuaternion(quaternion, undefined, false))`, and Euler.js:328-332 runs makeRotationFromQuaternion plus setFromRotationMatrix (asin/atan2) on every quaternion write.

Nothing reads part `.rotation`; rg over scene3d finds no part, p or g `.rotation` reads. Human setups 0x02000001 and 0x0200004E have 34 parts each (DAT).

Node bench: Object3D quaternion.set costs 84.6 ns against 3.7 ns for a bare Quaternion.set.

Particles: particle.js:553 `mesh.quaternion.copy(parent.quaternion).multiply(_scratchQuat).normalize()` triggers three Euler syncs per GR-type particle per tick on scene-detached carrier meshes.

Corpses: with RAGDOLL_ON on by default (ragdoll.js:57-63, `!== 'off'`), a corpse with `_ragdollFrozenPose` is posed by the playhead each frame (wasm seq.advance plus poseRigAt), then entities.js:17837-17841 → ragdoll.js:1622-1631 applyFrozenPose overwrites all parts again with the same frozen sprawl.
findings.proposal:
Change 1: at rig build (setup_rig.js part Groups) and slot-carrier creation (particle_manager meshFactory), install a no-op quaternion change callback, `part.quaternion._onChange(() => {})`. This drops the Euler mirror only on nodes whose rotation is never read; updateMatrix still composes from the quaternion.

Change 2: in tick, when a rig has a frozen corpse pose and no ragdoll sim, limp or jump tween, skip the playhead advance/pose/hook-drain branch and apply the frozen pose once, re-applying only when it is replaced (_ragdollPendingPose / restore).

Optional: skip poseRigAt when (desc, globalFrameIndex, inPlace) match the previous frame and no other writer has touched the parts (no jump tween, limb damage or ragdoll). The DAT frame rate is about 30 Hz against a 50-120 Hz render.

Escape flag `?quatSyncLean=off`.
findings.expected_gain: Derived from the laptop node bench: about 81 ns × 34 ≈ 2.8 µs saved per humanoid per frame, so about 0.3-0.6 ms per frame in a crowd of 100-200 rigs. Hunting grounds add per-corpse savings (a wasm advance plus a duplicate 34-part pose). GR particles save about 0.25 µs each per tick. Modest; it only matters in crowd and FX-dense scenes.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger rg for euler, onChange, rotation sync and quaternion.set: no matching item. The only hit is 5b6ff4e1 (scratch Euler/Quat objects in particle update), which is about allocation, not the sync callback. Walls 110/111 (per-object glue, matrix-freeze ceiling) are different mechanisms. Off-screen animation freeze (#63) is not proposed here.
findings.verify_how: Node test: a 34-part rig posed through poseRigAt for 300 frames with and without the no-op callback; every part.matrixWorld must be bit-identical. A corpse test: frozen pose applied once, then no part writes per tick while matrices stay identical. Microbench: quaternion write ns. On the 1070: a crowded town (Holtburg or Town Network) main-thread A/B.

findings.title: Range-gate tier-1 PlayEffect cues: far flashes, shockwaves and marks evict near ones from the 10/8/32 caps
findings.evidence:
play_effect_vfx.js:3596-3600 calls _fireTier1Cue for every resolved PlayEffect. :3674-3687 resolves the target placement and calls fireFxCue plus fireFxShowcaseCue with no distance test. fx_cues.js:103-147 fireFxCue spawns a flash, a shockwave and a decal unconditionally.

Each cap evicts with no regard to distance:
- Flashes: fx_lights.js:291-295 caps at FLASH_MAX=10 and drops the oldest. tickFxLights then pushes every live flash into activeLights with no distance check (:476-484), unlike emitter lights, which have REGISTER_RADIUS 48/56 m (:204-205).
- Shockwaves: fx_distort.js:80-88 caps at SHOCK_MAX=8 and drops the oldest, yet collectFxDistortSources fades a source to k=0 beyond 120 m (:157-158), so a far ring is invisible while still holding a slot.
- Decals: fx_decals.js:89-90 keeps 32 transients FIFO.

ACE broadcasts PlayEffect landblock-wide, so in a town fight or spell storm far casters' cues push out the ones next to the player.
findings.proposal:
In _fireTier1Cue, compute the camera distance to `_cueWorld` once and gate each part separately:
- Skip the shockwave beyond 120 m, where its k is already 0.
- Skip the flash beyond REGISTER_RADIUS_OUT plus the flash range (≈70 m), the same reach rule emitter lights use.
- Skip the decal beyond the decal pass's useful distance.

Use a single constant table in fx_cues.js. Escape flag `?fxCueRange=off`. The real retail emitters still spawn and are culled by RP6 and degrade distance as before.
findings.expected_gain: Correctness: in storms, nearby impact flashes, rings and scorch marks stop being cut short by off-screen or 150 m+ cues. A small CPU saving from fewer cue objects and activeLights candidates per far PlayEffect.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger open lead #37 (entities-fx-open line 37): '_fireTier1Cue fires flash/shockwave/decal at ANY distance — Unverified reviewer lead; far cues compete for 10-flash/8-shockwave caps'. What I add: verified file:line for all three cap/eviction sites; the fact that shockwaves past 120 m are already invisible (so gating them is pixel-identical for them); the flash→activeLights path having no registration radius, unlike emitter lights; and a concrete per-part gate design with numbers.
findings.verify_how: Node test: fire 30 cues at 150 m and 1 at 5 m. With the gate, the near flash, ring and decal survive their full envelope, and fxDistortStats/fxDecal stats show the far ones were never spawned. Without the gate, the near flash is evicted. On the 1070: a group fight eye-check that impact flashes near the player complete.

findings.title: New emitter FX lights stay dark until the next 2 Hz dedupe pass (0-500 ms), so short bursts and bolt trails often never light
findings.evidence:
fx_lights.js:122: FxLightSource starts with `this.registered = false`. bindEmitterFxLight (:323-354) adds the light to _emitterLights but never registers it. tickFxLights runs _dedupeAndRegister only when `now - _lastDedupe >= DEDUPE_INTERVAL_MS` (:486-489, 500 ms per :208). The per-frame loop lights a source only if `want = s.registered && !s.suppressed && k > 0.002` (:512).

A transient emitter (bolt trail, impact burst, about 0.3-1 s; `transient` → __dynamicPriority at :339) therefore waits 0-500 ms (250 ms on average) before it can light. Its `_activity` then eases up at 0.15 per frame, so a short burst can finish before it ever lights.
findings.expected_gain: Correctness and visual: FX lights on transient emitters appear on their first frame instead of 0-500 ms late. CPU cost is O(new sources), negligible.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger open lead #39 (entities-fx-open line 39): 'New transient emitter lights dark up to 500 ms (registered only by 2 Hz dedupe) — Unverified lead'. What I add: verified mechanism lines (ctor flag, bind path, dedupe gate, want gate), the `_activity` ease that makes the delay worse, and a design that keeps the light count stable and avoids forcing an O(E) dedupe on each bind, which would be costly in storms.
findings.verify_how: Node test: bind a transient emitter light 10 m from the reference point and tick once. It must be registered with intensity > 0 on the first or second tick (today it is 0 until the dedupe interval elapses). Also check that a near-duplicate of a static light is still suppressed. On the 1070: an eye-test of fire-bolt trails lighting nearby ground immediately.

findings.title: The velScale gait EMA measures ground speed from east and vertical motion: it uses x/z, but entity roots are in the AC frame, where z is up
findings.evidence:
entities.js:17683-17690: `const dx = p.x - inst._velPrevX; const dz = p.z - inst._velPrevZ; const sp = Math.hypot(dx, dz) / inst._velAccumDt;`, where p = inst.root.position. Entity roots are AC-frame (east, north, height) under worldRoot rotated −π/2 about X; see the comment at entities.js:16700-16705 ('the local AC position (east, north, height) = (p.x, p.y, p.z)'). The sticky code nearby correctly uses hypot(dx, dy) for horizontal distance.

So north-south motion reads as 0 m/s and jumps or slopes add vertical speed. There are two consumers:
- The EMA fallback in _unifiedLocoGaitScale (:11325), used when the stateGroundSpeed getter returns null (stale pkg, or rigs without a forward/sidestep command).
- The idle-fidget stillness gate (:18160). IDLE_FIDGET_ON is on by default: entities.js:1911-1916 reads `!== 'off'`, despite the '?idleFidget=on' comments.
findings.proposal: Sample p.y instead of p.z: store `_velPrevY` and use `Math.hypot(p.x - prevX, p.y - prevY)`. Fix the 'horizontal (XZ)' comment.
findings.expected_gain: Correctness: north-moving rigs no longer read as standing still in the gait fallback and the idle-fidget gate. Visible only on the fallback path (stale wasm or the fidget gate), so impact is small.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger rg for velScale, emaSpeed and ice-skating: no item. git log shows dcc277a1 'velScale fix' (a different, earlier fix) and a handoff note; neither touches the axis.
findings.verify_how: Node test: an EntityManager stub with a rig moving +y (north) at 3 m/s for 1 s. _emaSpeed should converge to about 3 (today it is about 0); a rig rising vertically should read 0.

verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical only if the cached signature never goes stale. A safer variant that is fully pixel-identical: memoise the signature per material object per tick (a tick-id stamp or a per-tick Map), and cache the key string per emitter tuple. Also hoist _sharedFrameId() to once per tick and the makeIm closure out of the hot path.

refutes.reasons:
I could not refute the core claim. I opened every cited site and traced the default-URL path.

**The frozen shortcut is unreachable for part-anchored static emitters.**
- particle_manager.js:1561-1573 tests `partFrame = trueSphere && pi !== -1 && ... parent.partFrames[pi]` first. The `__anchorFrozen` matrixWorld read is only an else-if after it.
- rp6TrueSphereEnabled (:1426) is ON unless the flag is off/0/false/no.
- statics.js:6108-6117 calls attachStaticPartFrames, then `_freezeStaticScriptAnchor`. attachStaticPartFrames (:5452-5476) gives every 0x02 Setup with at least one part a `createPartFramesProxy`. lib.rs `setup_static_part_pose` returns one frame per setup part, with no single-part or identity short-circuit.
- The hook part index passes through unchanged: statics.js:5934 → `_staticCreateFromDecoded` parent: anchor, partIndex → particle_manager.js:2404 setParenting(partIndex).
- The bf474c67 unit test (static_anchor_radius F7) only exercises `partIndex: -1`. That is how it missed the branch order.

**Drizzle is confirmed part-anchored.** I ran datcat myself. Setups 0x02000407 and 0x02000406 each have 1 part. Their default scripts 0x33000113 and 0x33000114 each hold one CreateParticle hook on part 0 with offset z=17, for emitters 0x32000142 and 0x32000143. Both emitters are non-parent-local and BirthratePerSec (max 5/7, birthrate 1.0 s / 2.5 s).

**Each proxy read does three ancestor walks.** setup_rig.js:188-216 calls part.updateWorldMatrix(true,false), then getWorldPosition, then getWorldQuaternion, and each of those calls updateWorldMatrix(true,false) again. Three r184 Object3D.js:1212 recomposes staticsGroup, worldRoot and the Scene on every walk, because `?freezeWorldRoots` is strict opt-in (DEFAULT OFF). The part's own matrixWorld is never rewritten, since matrixWorldAutoUpdate is false. So reading part.matrixWorld directly is exactly identical.

**The recheck is unstaggered.** All static emitters live in one `_staticParticleManager`. `recheck = (_rp6Frame % 6) === 0` (:2546, interval 6 at :171), and the loop at :2584-2588 (not :2558-2563 as cited) calls `_rp6ShouldCull`→rp6CullSphere for every emitter in the table on that one tick.

**My bench confirms the cost.** I ran the REAL rp6CullSphere with the real `_freezeStaticScriptAnchor` and createPartFramesProxy, using 5,000 frozen anchors under scene/worldRoot/statics, on laptop node (131 MB):
- partIndex 0 (the proxy path): 7.58 ms per recheck, 1.52 µs per emitter.
- The same emitters with partIndex -1 (the frozen matrixWorld path): 0.78 ms per recheck.

**No existing mechanism covers it.** None of the commits after bf474c67 (b20cdc37, 6c51237b, d817f9c3) touch the proxy. No flag exists for it.

**Pixels.** Change 1 is pixel-identical by construction.

**Minor corrections.**
- Drizzle has no tier1 light or distort row (particle-fx-tier1.json:211-212 has only sunLit, noise, shadow and rim). The fx_lights / fx_distort part therefore applies only to lit emitters such as torches and portals. It does not apply to the Linvak drizzle population, so that piece is small.
- Loop line numbers have drifted, as noted above.
refutes.strongest_counterargument:
The size of the gain is the weak point, not whether the mechanism exists.

1. **The big cost only exists where drizzle is dense.** Drizzle makes up 99% of the anchors at Linvak. Ordinary towns have a few hundred static script emitters, which works out to about 0.3-0.5 ms per recheck frame there. The "high" rating holds only for Linvak-class rain zones.

2. **The 3.6% figure is not proof that the proxy is the cost.** dcf07ecb says "Needs a wasm rebuild after pulling". If the 1070 ran a stale pkg without fetchSetupPartPose, attachStaticPartFrames returns 0. Profiled that way, it would hit the plain getWorldPosition branch, which bf474c67 did fix. If the pkg was current, the hot getWorldPosition frame was the proxy's own call, and the 3.6% figure supports the claim. Either way, the 1070 host may well be about 2x the laptop's node speed. That puts the real spike nearer 3-4 ms per recheck frame at about 5k emitters, about 0.5-0.7 ms per frame on average, rather than 7.6 ms.

3. **The spike may not cost frames.** It lands only every 6th frame. It costs frames only if the main thread is the bottleneck on that frame. That was true pre-freeze (half-res did nothing), but has not been re-measured since staticAnchorFreeze removed about 5-6 ms.

4. **The spawn and fx_lights pieces are small.** Spawns cost about 0.2 ms per frame. fx_lights does not apply to drizzle.

5. **Changes 2-4 are riskier than Change 1.** They memoise per emitter and must handle park/unpark and the `__scriptEpoch` rebuild. Change 1 is pure and exact, and delivers most of the gain by itself.
refutes.residual_claim:
The claim stands. On the default URL, rp6TrueSphere (default ON) plus staticPartAnchor (default ON) send every part-anchored static emitter's RP6 cull, which includes all of Linvak's drizzle on part 0, through createPartFramesProxy. That costs three updateWorldMatrix walks that recompose staticsGroup, worldRoot and the Scene, and it means bf474c67's `__anchorFrozen` fast path never fires for them. Its unit test only covered partIndex -1.

On laptop node with the real rp6CullSphere, 5,000 such emitters cost 7.6 ms per recheck, against 0.8 ms through the frozen path. That lands all on one tick every 6 ticks, because there is one static manager and the recheck is unstaggered.

Change 1 (read part.matrixWorld directly when part.matrixWorldAutoUpdate === false) is exactly bit-identical. Scaled to a 1070 host, Change 1 plus per-emitter memoising removes an estimated 3-7 ms spike every 6th frame, about 0.5-1.3 ms per frame on average, at Linvak Tukal. It also saves about 0.2 ms per frame of resolves on spawns. Elsewhere the gain is small.

The fx_lights portion does not apply to drizzle, which has no tier1 light; it applies only to lit emitters. The cited loop lines are really :2584-2588.

refutes.reasons:
The code facts hold, but the claimed gain is wrong by more than an order of magnitude. The "high" rating and the "up to ~3.3 ms per frame" figure come from misreading one sentence in a doc.

What I confirmed in scene3d/particles/particle_manager.js:
- :2839 builds the template-literal key for every emitter that reaches _appendInstances.
- :2841-2843 calls sharedAlphaBuckets.acquire with _alphaMatSig (:676-680, an 8-field join plus getHex) and a fresh closure.
- _sharedFrameId (:665-671) reads document.timeline.currentTime.
- particleSharedAlpha (:651-660) and particleInstancingAlpha (:617-627) are both default-on.
- The drizzle emitters are instanced alpha: addEmitter :2420 sets _instAlpha = !baseIsAdditive.
- I re-ran the scratch sig_bench.mjs: 943 ns per emitter against 52 ns cached. The per-call cost is real.

Where the scale breaks:
1. The "76% live" figure is a fraction of the drizzle within 64 m, not of all attached emitters. The source is docs/2026-10-19-water-flow-and-waterfalls.md:93: "the Linvak drizzle going from about 40% to 76% live within its 64 m radius". The finding applied 76% to all ~5,000 attached emitters (staticScriptRadius=2, 25 landblocks).
2. I checked the 64 m against the DAT (scratch skeptic-efx3/degrade.py).
   - Both drizzle emitters, 0x32000142 and 0x32000143, use hw GfxObj 0x01001166. It has DIDDegrade 0x11000085 with entry 0 max_dist 64.0 and entry 1 max_dist FLT_MAX.
   - The wasm max_degrade_distance (src/lib.rs:17051, n<=2 takes entry 0) therefore returns 64.
   - ?particleDegrade is default ON, so addEmitter (:2482-2491) stamps that 64 m onto every drizzle emitter through index.html's __hbWasm.fetch_particle_degrade_distance.
   - _rp6ShouldCull (:1389-1396) then culls every drizzle emitter whose anchor is more than 64 m from the camera.
   - Culled emitters `continue` at :2725, before the append at :2766-2768, so they never pay the key or signature cost.
3. Realistic count: statics.js:5111 measured ~256 drizzle anchors per landblock (36,864 m²), and setups 0x02000407/406 spawn one emitter each (default scripts 0x33000113/114, one CreateParticle hook). That gives about 89 emitters inside a 64 m circle, so about 68 live at 76%. Assuming 2-4 times the local density, the ceiling is about 135-270. At about 0.9 µs each that is about 0.06-0.25 ms per frame on the laptop node basis, not 3.3 ms. The owner's desktop CPU would be lower still.
4. The Holtburg figure is also inflated. The "~200 alpha" cited at :611-613 counts particles, not emitters, so there are tens of alpha emitters. That saves about 0.02-0.05 ms, not 0.2-0.5 ms.

Other checks:
- No existing mechanism caches the key or signature.
- The verifier's per-tick memo variant would be pixel-identical.
- The first verifier repeated the 3,800-emitter premise without checking the degrade cull.
refutes.strongest_counterargument: The per-call overhead is real and measured, about 0.9 µs. It is also paid by emitters with zero live particles, because only `!parts.length` returns early. Relative to each drizzle emitter's own append loop (5-7 particles), it is a large share, perhaps half the per-emitter append cost. The fix is small and pixel-identical with a per-tick signature memo. If some location stacks thousands of alpha emitters with large degrade distances inside the 220 m RP6 cap, the gain could reach the millisecond range. No such location is known: drizzle is the densest static emitter and is capped at 64 m. The DOM getter and closure costs were not measured, so the true per-emitter saving may be somewhat above 0.9 µs.
refutes.residual_claim: A low-impact, pixel-identical micro-optimisation. _appendInstances rebuilds the bucket key, the joined material signature, a closure and a document.timeline read for every non-culled alpha emitter on every tick, at about 0.9 µs each. Three changes would remove almost all of it: cache the key per emitter tuple, memoise the signature per material per tick, and read the frame id once per tick. At Linvak Tukal only about 70-270 drizzle emitters are live: the drizzle's 64 m degrade distance (?particleDegrade, default on) culls the rest before the append. That saves about 0.06-0.25 ms per frame on the laptop, about 0.02-0.05 ms in Holtburg-class towns, and less on the 1070 desktop. It is not "high" and not "up to 3.3 ms".

coverage_notes:
What I read (actual function bodies, not just greps): src/net_worker.rs (proxy + worker loop), scene3d/net_worker.js and net_worker_client.js; holtburger-session receive.rs, send.rs, reliability.rs, auth.rs, plus the ISAAC search in holtburger-protocol crypto.rs; holtburger-transport-ws transport.rs and frame.rs; wsbridge bridge.rs (accept, nodelay, both pumps); wire_integrity.rs; session/mod.rs. In session/messages I read mod.rs fully (pre-route hooks, world routing, the post-route kind=8/kind=11 signalling), position.rs (UpdatePosition, PublicUpdatePosition, VectorUpdate, the head of UpdateMotion), the ObjectCreate arm of objects.rs, and login.rs. Also session/commands/lifecycle.rs (SelectCharacter, keepalive, logoff), the lib.rs recv_loop select, tickMovement, poll_*, the resolve_physics_script_table_did / resolve_sound_table_did / maintain_bridge_indexes_on_routed_create path and should_route_message_to_world, and V2 get_file_by_key in holtburger-resource-http manifest_source.rs. On the JS side: app/frame_pump.js, the pumpNetFrame code in index.html, the client_events.js kinds 8/11/42-44, hud_panels.js, and every playerInventoryChanged / playerStatsUpdated subscriber (inventory.js rebuild, hotbar prune, lore-panel, item_drag, vitals-hud/orbs). I also counted, in the LSD weenie dump, which weenies leave PhysicsEffectTable or SoundTable off the wire (a tiny python probe).

Dropped after checking:
- ISAAC failed-search walk: it fills `xors` without rolling back, but it heals itself and costs little.
- ACK coalescing: already done at 500 ms. Dropping the standalone ACK after a piggyback saves at most 2 pkt/s, too little to matter.
- recv_message cancel-safety under select!: verified safe.
- TimeoutFuture churn per recv iteration: about 1-2 ms/s, negligible.
- wsbridge TCP_NODELAY: already set.
- EntityUpdate getter / FinalizationRegistry overhead and the __diag.wire tap: walled as 'wasm chatter refuted'.
- Remote position dedup: entity dimension, and the gain is speculative.
- In-session relogin state leaks: unreachable, because /logout reloads the page.
- Setup-parse sites on async paths: they prefetch first.

Walls and ledger items that shaped this:
- #50 failure-is-not-absence: finding 2 is a new instance of it.
- pre-4.8 #17 made the inventory snapshot lazy, and panelBatch coalesces per drain. Findings 1 and 3 are the parts those changes left open: the signal itself is still raised for unrelated objects and for vital-only ticks.
- The netWorker s13/s15 not-promoted verdict (+24% settle is real work): finding 4 does not claim to fix it.
- I avoided draw-count or per-getter pricing.

Skipped:
- netbrain and rynth (owner-protected).
- Per-opcode unpack internals.
- The landblock_stream render side.
- The Chorizite coverage pass (an open lead).
- Everything WebAC already fixed.

The dimension is fairly worked over: the transport, ordering and handshake layers have no new defects that I could stand behind. These four are what survived.

findings.title: kind=11 InventoryUpdated fires for every world object create/delete/parent/property change, re-running the full inventory refresh fan-out on frames that changed nothing the player owns
findings.area: src/session/messages/mod.rs post-route signalling → app/client_events.js kind 11 → hud_panels.js / plugins (inventory, hotbar, lore, item_drag)
findings.evidence: src/session/messages/mod.rs:717-726: `WorldEvent::EntitySpawned(_) | EntityReplaced(_) | EntityDespawned(_) | ContainerOpened(_) => { inventory_changed = true; }`. The comment admits 'the snapshot builder filters by ownership, so a false positive here just refreshes the panel one extra time.' Other unconditional sites: mod.rs:728-818 (PropertiesUpdated for ANY guid ends with `inventory_changed = true`), mod.rs:820-850 (EntityAttached/Detached for every wielder in view), mod.rs:1309-1321 (every accepted ObjectDelete under worldLifecycle), mod.rs:1428-1440 (every ParentEvent). worldLifecycle is default ON (should_route_message_to_world, lib.rs:37868-37880), so every ObjectCreate is routed and emits EntitySpawned/Replaced. mod.rs:1544-1553 then pushes CLIENT_EVENT_KIND_INVENTORY_UPDATED. By contrast the UpdateObject arm IS filtered (`w.note_update_object(guid)` → `is_owned_by_player`, mutations.rs:1879-1882). JS side for each frame that carries a kind 11: client_events.js:691-711 → flushPanelBatch → hud_panels.js:351-410 renderInventoryPanel. That clones the snapshot (lib.rs:41815 `latest_inventory.borrow().clone()`), wraps one wasm box per item, and rewrites the innerHTML of both legacy lists. Then the bus emits playerInventoryChanged. Subscribers that always run: hotbar.js:1684-1728 pruneStaleItemBindings (another full playerInventory() snapshot), item_drag.js:1092, scene3d/index.js:3902. When the inventory view is open, inventory.js:1644-1690 rebuild() runs takeInventoryRows: a third snapshot with about 22 getters per item (inventory_helpers.js:458-488), plus renderGrid, renderBagColumn, refreshPaperdollViewport (entityWieldedItems) and refreshBurden. The legacy innerHTML change also fires the MutationObserver (inventory.js:1843-1849). Lore and examine views add more reads when open. inventory.js:1897-1909 already filters kind:47/49 to 'ours' (`wieldEventTouchesLocal`), but the same EntityAttached/Detached arm raises kind 11, which defeats that filter.
findings.proposal: Raise inventory_changed only for events that can change the owned or viewed item set. Put a pure predicate in a native-testable module (wall #17), e.g. `inventory_signal_relevant(w: &WorldState, ev) -> bool`. It is true when any of these holds: guid == w.player.guid; w.is_owned_by_player(guid) (WorldContextExt); the entity's container_id or wielder_id is the player or an owned pack; container_id ∈ w.open_containers; or guid itself is an open container. Per site: for EntitySpawned/Replaced, test the Box<Entity> the event already carries. For EntityDespawned and the ObjectDelete/InventoryRemoveObject post-route arms, test `w` (ObjectDelete only marks an explicit delete, so the entity is still present post-route; evaluate InventoryRemoveObject before routing). For ParentEvent, test the child or the parent. For PropertiesUpdated{guid} and EntityAttached/Detached, test guid or wielder. Keep ContainerOpened/Closed, InventoryActionFailed, EntityIdentified and the vendor/trade paths unconditional. Flag `?invSignalOwned` default ON with an `=off` escape (validated gate, default-on rule), plus a `__diag` counter of suppressed signals. Rider: fix the stale comment at client_events.js:693-696 ('The wasm-side filter excludes entities not owned by the player'), which is false today.
findings.expected_gain: Unmeasured. Frequency is derived from code and the cost is assumed. With worldLifecycle on, every ObjectCreate, ObjectDelete and ParentEvent in view raises kind 11. That means every frame of a town-arrival burst (~300 creates over 1-3 s, already the worst p99 frames), a create plus a delete for every missile, and corpse/creature churn and monster weapon swaps in combat. Assumed cost per triggered frame: about 0.5-1.5 ms main thread always-on (legacy list innerHTML, 2 snapshot clones, ~150 wasm boxes each), and about 2-4 ms with the inventory window open (plus the full rebuild and grid patch at 22 getters per item). After the fix these frames do zero inventory work. Snapshot content is unchanged, so the result is pixel-identical. Bench counter that already exists: `window.__inventoryRebuildStats.rebuilds`.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger: rg 'kind=11|inventory_changed|playerInventoryChanged|renderInventoryPanel|inventory snapshot|panelBatch' hit only pre-4.8 #17 (the snapshot is rebuilt on read, so the RUST rebuild was fixed, but the signal still fires) and the hotbar late-binding lead (webac). panelBatch (url-flags :701) coalesces per drain but never filters the trigger. git log -i 'inventory' shows b9e56994 (per-batch coalescing) and nothing filtering the trigger. url-flags has no invSignal-like flag. The 2026-10-07 review §1 #17 text confirms that only the Rust side was addressed.
findings.verify_how: Targeted node test: an extracted predicate over a WorldState::synthetic() world (NPC spawn → false; item created into a player pack → true; item in an open corpse → true; ParentEvent of an NPC weapon → false). Laptop: a headless wireframe Holtburg arrival with `__diag.wire.summary()` counters 'event:11' and `__inventoryRebuildStats.rebuilds` over 60 s, flag on vs =off: expect a large drop. Loot/pickup/equip/corpse-open must still refresh (the corpse-loot-bar refreshContents path). 1070: a Performance trace of the arrival burst and a combat window, comparing per-frame main-thread time on frames that carry kind 11.

findings.title: ObjectCreate resolves the PhysicsScriptTable and SoundTable from the Setup synchronously, once; when the Setup is not resident yet it stamps 0 for good (lost VFX and sound hooks) and re-parses the Setup twice per create
findings.area: src/lib.rs resolve_physics_script_table_did / resolve_sound_table_did; session/messages/objects.rs ObjectCreate; maintain_bridge_indexes_on_routed_create
findings.evidence: lib.rs:38856-38904 resolve_physics_script_table_did: if the wire PhysicsDesc carries no petable, it calls `global_source().get_file_by_key(eor/portal, setup_id)` and returns 0 on Err. lib.rs:38945-38983 resolve_sound_table_did does the same for default_sound_table. V2 get_file_by_key (holtburger-resource-http manifest_source.rs:1237-1253) does not fetch: a record not in a pack, boot.hba or the shard cache returns Err('record not prefetched'). boot.hba holds only essential tables plus the boot-LB walk (apps/holtburger-tools dat_shard.rs:69-89). The call sites run synchronously inside the recv loop, before any JS spawn has prefetched that Setup on the main instance: lib.rs:39441-39446 (routed create stamps `physics_script_table_did`; the index entry is inserted only if != 0), objects.rs:124 (self-seed), objects.rs:487-489 (KIND_SPAWN `sound_table_did`). Nothing re-resolves later. entities.js:8634-8644 getPhysicsScriptTableDid only reads the index. play_effect_vfx.js:2420-2426 and :3657-3661 treat 0 as missNoTable and show the placeholder. entities.js:6052 prewarms the SoundTable only when it is != 0, and entities.js:18468-18486 returns silently on 0 for remotes. Scope, measured from the LSD dump (agent-scratch/lsd_tables*.py): 1940/1941 Portal weenies omit wire PhysicsEffectTable and 1914/1941 omit SoundTable. Also omitting PhysicsEffectTable: 348/362 Vendors, 1295 non-attackable Creature NPCs (attackable monsters almost all carry it: 38/3827 do not), and 1522/3197 Generic objects; 1492 Generic objects also omit SoundTable. ACE sends these only from the weenie property (WorldObject_Properties.cs:889-901, WorldObject_Networking.cs:476-480). Every instance created in the burst before the JS spawn of the first instance of its Setup lands is affected. Perf side: each ObjectCreate runs up to two full SetupModel::unpack calls (binrw plus HashMaps for holding/connection/placement frames, setup_model.rs:362-422) after copying the record bytes. No Setup memo exists (rg found none).
findings.proposal: (1) Add `SETUP_DEFAULT_TABLES: thread_local HashMap<u32 setup_id, (u32 phstable, u32 stable, u32 default_script)>`. Fill it only on a successful parse, never on not-resident (wall #50). Clear it in init_resource_source like the other memos (global_source.rs). Route both resolvers and `setup_default_script_id` through it, so each Setup type is parsed once per session instead of twice per create. Opportunistically populate it wherever the main instance already parses that Setup (the fetchEntityAnimationKeyframes path). (2) Make resolution lazy on miss. In `entity_physics_script_table_did(guid)` (lib.rs:42381), when the index has no entry, `try_borrow` the world, read the entity's petable/csetup, consult or fill the memo, and insert on success. Add `entitySoundTableDid(guid)` with the same logic. In JS, `_spawnImpl` re-queries it after the rig fetch resolves when meta.soundTableDid === 0 (the Setup is resident by then), and the hook path at entities.js:18468 re-asks once per instance on 0. Move the pure resolver into a generic `<S: ResourceSource>` helper under `cfg(any(wasm32, test))`, as `setup_default_script_id` already is, so it can be unit-tested natively. No flag is needed for the memo (byte-identical). The lazy re-resolve can ride `?setupTableLazy` default ON with an `=off` escape.
findings.expected_gain: Correctness, derived from code plus the LSD census: on first sighting, PlayEffect/PhysScript VFX, DefaultScript(17/18) hooks and SoundTable(2) animation hooks start resolving for portals, vendors and town NPCs (NPC emote PhysScripts), and for generic objects whose weenie leaves the table off the wire. Today they fall back to the placeholder or silence, depending on arrival order. Measurable via `VFX_COVERAGE.realVfxMissBreakdown.noTable` (play_effect_vfx.js:4859). Perf (unmeasured; assumed ~20-80 µs per SetupModel parse in release wasm): roughly 2 parses × ~300 creates, i.e. ~10-50 ms spread across a town-arrival burst, goes to 1 parse per distinct Setup.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger: rg 'phstable|script table|sound table|soundtable|missNoTable|not prefetched|not resident' found only pre-4.8 #8 (the JS facade cached a failed PhysicsScriptTable *record* fetch, ui/ac_physics_script_table.js). This is a different, upstream site: the DID is never resolved from the Setup in Rust. RUSTCORE-2 memoised resolve_degrade_part_frame (fetch_model_meshes), not the ObjectCreate path. git log -i 'phstable|script.table|sound.table' shows 62ee171e (SG-A1, self-seed resolve: same one-shot pattern, no retry) and nothing else. No url flag. It brushes wall #50 (failure is not absence); this is a new concrete violation of it, not a re-proposal.
findings.verify_how: Native cargo-free node probe is not possible, so use a targeted Rust unit test (orchestrator build): a fake ResourceSource returns Err for 0x02xxxxxx, then Ok. Assert the memo does not cache the Err, and that the lazy getter returns the table once the record is resident. Laptop wireframe: teleport to a town with fresh portals and vendors, then read the `entityPhysicsScriptTableDid(guid)` and `physicsScriptTableIndex` sizes vs the count of resident Setup-only entities, before and after. In-world: trigger an NPC emote PhysScript and check realVfxMissBreakdown.noTable. 1070 eye-test of a portal and an NPC emote effect on first sighting.

findings.title: Every vital tick (regen heartbeat, each hit or spell) raises the broad kind=8 stats refresh and three full Rust snapshot rebuilds, although the narrow kind 42-44 vital events already carry the change
findings.area: src/session/messages/mod.rs VitalUpdated → stats_changed; client_events.js kind 8 → flushPanelBatch → 47 playerStatsUpdated subscribers
findings.evidence: mod.rs:586-603: `WorldEvent::VitalUpdated { vital, prev_current } => { stats_changed = true; ... push kind 42/43/44 {current, buffed_max, prev} }`. mod.rs:1460-1488: when stats_changed is set, every message rebuilds `publish_player_stats_snapshot` (vitals + attributes + attribute/vital/skill xp tables, lib.rs:49765+), `publish_player_known_spells_snapshot` and `publish_player_enchantments_snapshot`, then pushes kind 8. That happens per message, so ACE's 3-vital heartbeat (Creature_Vitals.cs:81-95, every 5 s by default, WorldObject_Tick.cs:47-48) means 3 rebuilds, and in combat each health/stamina/mana update costs one. JS: client_events.js:666-690 coalesces to one renderVitalsPanel (hud_panels.js, a full innerHTML rebuild of the attribute and skill tables) plus one 'playerStatsUpdated' emit per drain. That emit has 47 subscriptions (rg count), including inventory.js refreshBurden/aetheria, spellbook, stance-toggle, status-indicators x3, target-bar, hotbar reconcile and options-panel. vitals-hud.js:458/474-476 and vitals-orbs.js:1549/1565-1567 subscribe to BOTH the broad event and vitalChanged*, so each vital tick renders them twice.
findings.proposal: (a) Pixel-identical rider, Rust only: mark the three snapshots dirty and rebuild on read, as pre-4.8 #17 did for inventory (INVENTORY_SNAPSHOT_DIRTY pattern, lib.rs:41805-41816), and push at most one kind 8 per handle_message batch. (b) Main part: do not set stats_changed for current-only vital messages (PrivateUpdateVitalCurrent / PrivateUpdateAttribute2ndLevel, i.e. ACE GameMessagePrivateUpdateAttribute2ndLevel). Keep emitting kind 42-44. Audit the kind-8 subscribers that read current vitals (spellbook mana affordability, target-bar, combat-hud) and subscribe them to vitalChanged*; drop the broad-event re-render in vitals-hud and vitals-orbs. Gate (b) behind `?vitalNarrow` default OFF until the 1070 eye-test.
findings.expected_gain: Unmeasured; the cost is assumed. In combat about 2-4 vital messages/s each trigger a full 47-handler fan-out plus a legacy table innerHTML rebuild (assumed ~1-3 ms per fan-out frame), and idle regen does so every 5 s. With (b), those frames run only the cheap per-bar update. With (a), burst batches (buffs, level-up, login) rebuild the Rust snapshots once instead of N times. Small average fps gain; it lowers combat frame spikes.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger: rg 'stats snapshot|kind=8|playerStatsUpdated|VitalUpdated|stats_changed|renderVitalsPanel|known.spells snapshot' returned nothing. pre-4.8 #7 fixed only JS triple enchantment pulls inside a batch. panelBatch (b9e56994, url-flags :701) coalesces renders per drain but keeps raising kind 8 on every vital tick. The 85fb4784 git hit only added a subscriber. No url flag exists.
findings.verify_how: Laptop wireframe in-world: count `__diag.wire.summary()` 'event:8' vs 'event:42/43/44' over 60 s of regen and a short fight. With (b) on, 'event:8' should drop to non-vital stat changes only. Check that the vitals HUD/orbs, the spellbook mana greying and the target bar still update (DOM assertions, `node` test over client_events kind-42 handling). The 1070 eye-test with ?vitalNarrow=on covers HUD look and cadence.

findings.title: netWorker (auto-on for bot/agent) posts one worker→main postMessage plus two copies per game message; batching per recv turn cuts main-thread tasks by the messages-per-packet factor
findings.area: src/net_worker.rs worker loop + scene3d/net_worker.js / net_worker_client.js inbound
findings.evidence: net_worker.rs:455-490: `for ev in events { ... worker_post(RX_KIND_MESSAGE, &bytes) }`. That is one post per message even when one S2C packet carries several (ACE packs many fragments per packet). Each worker_post (net_worker.rs:390-397) runs `Uint8Array::from(bytes)` (a JS-heap copy), then net_worker.js:72 posts `self.postMessage({t:'rx', bytes}, [bytes.buffer])`. On main, every post is a separate MessageEvent task. net_worker_client.js:254-256 calls `net_proxy_push_inbound(m.bytes)` (wasm-bindgen copies into a new Vec, net_worker.rs:325-331), and RemoteSessionProxy::recv_message yields a single message per wake (net_worker.rs:191). netWorker is forced on for `?agent=1`/`?bot=1` (net_worker_client.js:140-150), the rynth/bot population that runs saturated main threads, and stays default off for humans (NET_WORKER_DEFAULT=false, :128).
findings.proposal: In the worker loop, accumulate every Message/TimeSync record produced by one `recv_message()` call (and any further ones drained in the same worker task turn) into one buffer with tagged, length-prefixed records [u8 kind][u32 len][bytes]. Post it once with a transfer. Add `net_proxy_push_inbound_batch(bytes)` on main to split the records in Rust and `unbounded_send` them in order. Order is preserved because there is one channel and one post per turn. Link status and disconnect stay as they are. `RemoteSessionProxy::recv_message` may also drain everything already queued (`try_next` loop) into one Vec<SessionEvent>, so the recv loop handles a whole batch in one wake.
findings.expected_gain: Derived from code; magnitude assumed. Main-thread message tasks and JS↔wasm copies per S2C packet drop from k (messages per packet, often 5-15 in busy areas) to 1. That is a modest main-thread saving for netWorker sessions (bots, agents, and any future promotion) and no change for default human sessions. It does NOT address the s13 +24% settle verdict (1121.md §4 measured genuinely more streamed work), so it is not offered as a promotion fix.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger: the netWorker entries are RUSTNET-1/2/3, R9, 'outbound actions need unpack arms', 'hb_mem_census error ends session' and 'ping RTT freeze'. None mentions inbound batching or postMessage volume. git log -i 'net.?worker' (90c725a9, 8938741e, 8efcb5e5, bbe47004) shows no batching. docs/1121.md §4/§5 attribute the settle delta to real work, so this is presented as an independent efficiency change. No url flag.
findings.verify_how: Targeted node test of the batch codec (split order, TimeSync interleave) via the native-testable net_worker_outbound-style module. Laptop: a headless `?agent=1&nullRender=1&renderOnDemand=1&netDrainHz=30` bot in Holtburg (the one allowed tab), counting worker 'rx' posts/s vs messages/s through a counter in net_worker_client. Expect posts/s ≈ packets/s. `__diag.wire.integrity()` totals must be unchanged.

verdicts.code_truth: All cited sites hold at HEAD. mod.rs:717-726 sets `inventory_changed = true` for EntitySpawned/EntityReplaced/EntityDespawned/ContainerOpened, and its comment admits the over-firing ('a false positive here just refreshes the panel one extra time'). The PropertiesUpdated arm (mod.rs:728-818) ends with an unconditional `inventory_changed = true`. EntityDetached/EntityAttached (mod.rs:820-850) set it for every wielder in view. ObjectDelete (mod.rs:1308-1321) and InventoryRemoveObject (mod.rs:1323-1330) set it whenever worldLifecycle is on. The ParentEvent arm (mod.rs:1428-1440) sets it for every accepted ParentEvent. worldLifecycle is default ON (lib.rs:667 reader is `!= worldLifecycle=off`), so every ObjectCreate is routed, and liveness.rs:653/663 pushes EntityReplaced or EntitySpawned for every create. mod.rs:1544-1553 then marks the snapshot dirty and pushes kind 11. By contrast the UpdateObject arm is filtered (mod.rs:1394 `if w.note_update_object(guid)`, mutations.rs:1879 `is_owned_by_player`). JS side: client_events.js:698-711 / flushPanelBatch :64-67 run renderInventoryPanel. hud_panels.js:351-410 calls playerInventory() (one wasm box per item) and rewrites innerHTML of both legacy lists. The bus then emits playerInventoryChanged. Subscribers confirmed: hotbar.js:1746-1749 (refreshUnresolvedIcons plus pruneStaleItemBindings, another full snapshot), item_drag.js:1092, scene3d/index.js:3902, corpse-loot-bar, lore-panel, tinker, vendor-ui, examine-target, combat-bar. inventory.js:1897-1909 filters kind:47/49 with wieldEventTouchesLocal, but rebuild() also runs from both the playerInventoryChanged bus event and the MutationObserver on the legacy lists (:1843-1849, :1912). Because the same Rust arm raises kind 11, that filter is defeated whenever the inventory overlay is connected. The stale comment at client_events.js:693-696 ('The wasm-side filter excludes entities not owned by the player') is false.
verdicts.novelty: New. The ledger has only pre-4.8 #16/#17 (Rust snapshot made lazy, compact:518) and the hotbar late-binding lead (open:62). Neither filters the trigger. b9e56994 (panelBatch) coalesces per drain and does not filter. git log has no ownership filtering of the signal, and url-flags has no invSignal-like flag. The defeated 2026-10-07 kind:47/49 filter is a new bug inside a shipped item.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None directly. It brushes wall #135 ('wasm chatter refuted') only loosely: the cost here is per-item snapshot boxing of N≈100-200 items plus DOM innerHTML and a plugin fan-out, not ~22 fixed crossings. It also respects wall #17 (pure predicate outside session/).
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical only if the predicate is complete. As written, the proposal tests ownership AFTER routing for PropertiesUpdated/EntityReplaced. ACE's drop path (Player_Inventory.cs:1439-1442) sends PublicUpdateInstanceID(Container→Invalid), so post-route the item is no longer owned. The predicate would then return false, the INVENTORY_SNAPSHOT_DIRTY mark would be skipped (the Rust snapshot itself would go stale, not just the panel), and the panel would only recover if a same-session player-guid update such as EncumbranceVal happened to follow. The predicate must be 'owned before OR owned after', e.g. guid ∈ the last published inventory guid set, or is_owned_by_player captured before routing. A second hidden dependency: scene3d/index.js:3902 uses playerInventoryChanged as an invKick to re-mark every live wield-retry ladder, remote PENDING-MOUNT ladders included. After the filter, remote wielders rely on their timer rungs and _flushPendingAttach (the index.js:3640-3660 comments say the latter suffices). The likely effect is a small attach-timing shift; check `wieldRetryStats.resolvedRetry` in the A/B.
verdicts.gain_realism: Unmeasured, and the frequency is derived correctly from code. panelBatch already caps the fan-out at one per frame, so the saving is about one fan-out per frame that carries kind 11: most frames of an arrival burst, plus missile create/delete, corpse churn and monster ParentEvents in combat. Steady idle town is only a few per second. Per fan-out with the inventory closed: playerInventory() boxing plus ~6 getters per item plus innerHTML of ~150 li, a second snapshot in the hotbar prune, then frees. Corrected estimate about 0.5-2 ms main thread on affected frames; with the inventory open add the full rebuild (takeInventoryRows ~22 getters/item, grid, doll). Real but bounded: a hitch/p99 and combat-frame trim, not a mean-fps step. Bench with __inventoryRebuildStats.rebuilds and __diag.wire 'event:11'.

coverage_notes:
I read the full ledger-walls.txt and both hud-audio slices first. Then I read code bodies, not just grep hits, in these areas.

**HUD steady state**

- scene3d/hud.js: the DOM nameplate layer, default OFF via ?nameplateDom=on.
- scene3d/selection_brackets.js: translate3d writes go to the compositor only, and _hideAll repeats the same value, so no invalidation.
- scene3d/loop.js DOM hooks: only the nameplate and bracket ticks.

**Per-event HUD**
- chat-panel.js and app/chat_log.js.
- hotbar.js cooldown path plus inventory_helpers.cooldownStep, checked against the decomp UIElement_UIItem::UpdateCooldownDisplay and the retail layout 0x21000037 JSON plus the exported sprites.
- combat-hud.js and combat-bar.js meters and timers, target-bar, buffs-hud, status-indicators, hover-tooltip, item_drag, the ac_font.js <ac-text> render path.
- Every rAF and setInterval site in plugins/, ui/, app/ and index.html.
- A global listener add/remove audit across plugins and ui. The unmatched adds are all once-guarded module-level installs, so I found no close/reopen leak.

**Secondary WebGL viewports**
- ui/ac_paperdoll_viewport.js, ui/ac_dye_viewport.js, plus the inventory.js and examine-target.js lifecycles.

**Compositing angle**
- three r184 always requests alpha:true, and the canvas context attributes are in shader_logdepth.js. I did not propose anything here: the gain is uncertain and it is outside HUD.

**Audio**
- audio_manager.js (decodeAudioData is off-thread, the LRU, voice claim and release), voice_pool.js, ambient_runtime.js.
- No new defect beyond the already-open `_startVoice` source.start-catch node leak. Listener AudioParam writes per frame land on the audio thread, not on the three saturated threads.

**Skipped or not reported**
- I did not dig into rynth beyond its timers (fragile, owner-protected).
- Minor, not reported: the vitals-orbs hit gate reads currentCSSZoom (a computed-style read) for all 3 panes on every document pointermove, before its cheap rect test (vitals-orbs.js ~1247). It is the same pattern the radar cached, but it only costs anything when style is dirty at input time. Possible S fix: rect test first, and cache zoom together with rect.
- Not reported: the radar repaints with up to ~1.8k fillRects per change at 40 Hz while moving. A pixel-identical cheaper path is unclear.
- Not reported: the combat-hud fill uses a `width` CSS transition (a main-thread animation, so layout+paint every frame for each swing). The pixel-identical alternative is non-trivial because the fill is a repeat-x sprite.
- Not reported: the selection-bracket mask-image on composited layers creating render surfaces (low confidence).

**Walls that shaped the search**

- 83/86: CrGpuMain raster is invisible to CPU profiles, so I priced findings as raster plus main thread.
- 105/141: CPU-bound frame, which favours findings that cut renderer-main work too.

findings.title: Hotbar cooldown overlay is an invented dark wipe that animates in 4 discrete jumps; retail's 10-step clock+bar sprites are exported and the retail phase is already computed every 250 ms but never drawn
findings.evidence:
plugins/hotbar.js:586-599: `.hb-hotbar-slot.cooldown-active::after { background: rgba(0,0,0,0.55); clip-path: polygon(...); animation: hb-hotbar-cd var(--hb-cd-dur) linear var(--hb-cd-delay) forwards }`. The @keyframes polygons have 7 / 6 / 5 / 4 / 2 vertices at 0/25/50/75/100%. Polygons with different vertex counts cannot be interpolated (CSS Shapes basic-shape interpolation; Blink falls back to discrete), so the 'sweep' is really four flips at 12.5/37.5/62.5/87.5%. It is also a dark radial wipe over the icon, which retail never draws.

hotbar.js:1835-1844: `const step = cooldownStep(dur, remaining); ... el.dataset.cdStep = String(step);` is refreshed by the 250 ms timer (:1847), but no CSS rule reads data-cd-step (rg finds only the write at :1838 and the delete at :1785).

inventory_helpers.js:1431-1436 implements retail's phase `trunc(r/d*10+1)`, clamped 1..10. tests/item_cooldown_step.test.mjs asserts that phase table ('shows ONE of the ten m_elem_Icon_Cooldown_10..100 overlays'), yet nothing paints it.

findings.title: Paperdoll creates and destroys a whole WebGL2 context on every inventory open, every inventory→examine→back round trip, and every creature examine; make one persistent shared viewport
findings.evidence:
ui/ac_paperdoll_viewport.js:73-82: each construction makes `new THREE.WebGLRenderer({alpha, antialias:true, preserveDrawingBuffer:true})`, a fresh WebGL2 context with a fresh three program cache.

:232-239: loadPlayer has a `_lastLoadKey` debounce, but it only helps within one instance.

:292-315: for a player with sub-palettes every load runs wasm `fetchEntitySurfacesPixels` over all surfaces, then `surfacePixelsToTexture` and a new MeshStandardMaterial per surface, uploaded into the new context.

:577-590 dispose(): `renderer.dispose(); renderer.forceContextLoss()`.

plugins/inventory.js:762/834: `doMount` builds `new PaperdollViewport(...)` on every inventory view mount. :1577 calls loadPlayer on it. :1937 disposes on cleanup.

plugins/main-panel.js:308-314: `_mountCurrent()` runs `_runCleanup()` before mounting ANY view, including `pushView` (:338-345). So inventory.js:1365 `pushView("examine", …fromInventory)` disposes the inventory doll, and closeView() re-mounts inventory with a brand-new context and a full rebuild.

plugins/examine-target.js:753 creates another PaperdollViewport per creature or player examine. :1541-1549 disposes and recreates it on every entityAppearanceChanged; its comment claims the '_lastLoadKey debounce will no-op', but the debounce never applies to a new instance.
findings.proposal:
Add a module-level singleton in ui/ac_paperdoll_viewport.js: `acquirePaperdollViewport(width, height)` returns one long-lived instance. On a size change it calls renderer.setSize and the camera aspect (224×214 vs 224×178). `release(host)` detaches the canvas without disposing.

inventory.js doMount and examine-target.js renderEntityPaperdoll append `vp.dom` into their host and call loadPlayer. With the debounce, an unchanged appearance is a no-op, and the existing IntersectionObserver re-renders on show (preserveDrawingBuffer already keeps the image).

Cleanup detaches instead of disposing. The appearance-refresh path calls loadPlayer on the same instance instead of dispose+recreate. Dispose only on pagehide or a webglcontextlost of that context.

Inventory and examine are both main-panel views, and only one is mounted at a time, so one context serves both. Flag `?paperdollPersist` default on, `=off` restores today's per-mount construction.

findings.title: Every incoming chat line forces two synchronous document layouts (hidden legacy #chat-log plus the HUD mirror's per-line scrollToBottom); coalesce to one per batch
findings.evidence:
app/chat_log.js:341-351: after `chatLog.appendChild(li)` it reads `chatLog.scrollHeight - chatLog.scrollTop - chatLog.clientHeight` and writes scrollTop for EVERY line. #chat-log lives in `<div id="chat-panel" hidden>` (index.html:788), which agent-mode CSS (index.html:510) display:none's on the owner's autoLogin shortcut, so the read buys nothing yet still forces a document style+layout update when anything is dirty.

plugins/chat-panel.js:775-779: the MutationObserver callback loops records and calls `mirrorOne(node)` with batch=false for each LI. mirrorOne (:750-766) then runs refreshTimestampFlag + updateEmpty + `scrollToBottom()` per line, and scrollToBottom (:657-660) is `log.scrollTop = log.scrollHeight`: a forced layout of the 300-line HUD log per line.

The batch path already exists: `mirrorOne(srcLi, batch=true)` is used for the initial sync at :772. Lines arrive from the ClientEvent drain inside the frame, so a burst of N lines in one task gives N forced layouts in the HUD log and N in the hidden one.
findings.proposal:
In chat-panel.js attachSource's observer:
1. Call `mirrorOne(node, true)` for every added LI.
2. Then run the post-batch once: refreshTimestampFlag(); updateEmpty(); if (pinned || anyEchoInBatch) scrollToBottom(); else unread += count of batch lines visible in the current filter; showUnread().

In app/chat_log.js appendChatLine:
- Track `pinned` from a passive scroll listener (the same isNearBottom helper chat-panel uses), instead of measuring after every append.
- Defer the `scrollTop = scrollHeight` write to a single rAF per frame (one flag).
- Skip both when the log has no layout box (agent mode).

No flag needed (HUD rule). Final scroll positions are identical.
findings.expected_gain: Removes 2N-1 forced layouts per N-line chat burst, leaving 1 batched read. Scale assumed at ~0.05-0.3 ms per avoided incremental layout, so combat bursts of 5-10 lines save roughly 1-3 ms in the frame they land. Steady-state impact is low and unmeasured. Pixel-identical.

Not a flag in url-flags.md (chatFade/chatErrors are unrelated).
findings.verify_how:

verdicts.code_truth:
The mechanism is real.
- app/chat_log.js:341-351 appends the li, then reads scrollHeight/scrollTop/clientHeight and may write scrollTop, per line.
- plugins/chat-panel.js:772-779: the MutationObserver callback calls mirrorOne(node) with batch=false for every added LI.
- mirrorOne (:750-766) appends a line, trims (removes the first child at 300), then refreshTimestampFlag + updateEmpty + scrollToBottom.
- scrollToBottom (:657-660) is `log.scrollTop = log.scrollHeight`, which forces a layout after each append.
- The batch path exists (attachSource :771-774).
- No CSS containment on the HUD log (rg 'contain:' finds none in chat-panel.js).

Inaccurate: the 'hidden legacy log' premise holds only in agent mode.
- index.html:510 display:none's #chat-panel under html.agent-mode (the autoLogin shortcut, :620-629).
- There the li append dirties no layout (display:none subtree has no layout objects). The read only flushes whatever else is dirty, so it is usually near-free, not a layout.
- In manual-Connect mode, client_events.js:241/:424 set chatPanel.hidden=false on world entry. There the legacy 400-li list IS laid out, and each read is a real layout.
verdicts.novelty:
New.
- No ledger hits for scrollHeight, forced layout, reflow or chat mirror.
- git log chat commits are feature/layout-port only.
- No url-flag.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None. Wall 135 (rAF count) and the framework-glue walls do not apply. This is per-line forced synchronous layout, not callback count.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical. Batching scrollToBottom to once per observer delivery leaves the same final scrollTop, pinned state and unread count. The unread count stays the same if computed per visible line in the batch.
verdicts.gain_realism:
Overstated.
- Saved work per N-line delivery: N-1 incremental layouts of the 300-line HUD log, which has cached LayoutNG children. Roughly 20-100 µs each (assumed).
- In agent mode the legacy-log reads are mostly free style flushes.
- So a 5-line burst saves ~0.1-0.4 ms, not 1-3 ms.
- Most frames carry 0-1 chat lines, so steady-state gain is ~0. Login backlog and multi-mob combat are the only real bursts.
verdicts.corrected_claim:
chat-panel's MutationObserver mirrors each added line with batch=false, so an N-line delivery (lines appended in one task) forces N layouts of the uncontained 300-line HUD log via scrollToBottom's scrollHeight read.

Fix: call mirrorOne(node, true) for each node, then run refreshTimestampFlag/updateEmpty/scrollToBottom once (scroll if pinned or the batch has an echo; otherwise add the batch's visible lines to unread). This saves N-1 forced layouts per burst.

The legacy #chat-log read in app/chat_log.js:348 is a real layout only in manual-Connect mode, where the dev panel is unhidden on world entry. In agent mode it is a near-free flush; skipping it when the log has no layout box is a minor extra.

Pixel-identical, low value: about 0.1-0.4 ms in burst frames, ~0 steady state.
