Findings 1 and 2 are the strongest. The no-store responses are confirmed live, and terrain_bc7.js says three times in its comments that it relies on an 'immutable HTTP cache' that the server never provides.

findings.title: Terrain BC7 tiers (.hbc7, 103 MB) are served no-store: re-downloaded every warm boot, by the SW's background refresh on every hit, and on every context-loss restore
findings.area: scripts/serve.py headers + service-worker.js SWR + scene3d/terrain_bc7.js mirror restore
findings.evidence:
1. serve.py:871-877: only .js/.mjs/.wasm/.bin/.hba/.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp/.ktx2/.exr get revalidating `no-cache`. Everything else falls to :887 `no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`, and .hbc7 is not in the tuple. Live probe of /apps/holtburger-web/scene3d/assets/terrain_bc7/t1024/0x06006D06_color.hbc7 returned `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`.
2. Tier sizes on disk: t128 1.3 MB, t512 20.3 MB, t1024 81.1 MB, 59 files each. terrain_bc7.js:491 does a plain `fetch(`${base}/${name}`)`; DEFAULT_BASE is scene3d/assets/terrain_bc7 (:109).
3. service-worker.js:442-443 marks every /scene3d/assets/ URL as SWR. :483-492: on a cache HIT it returns the cached bytes and ALSO runs `fetch(event.request)` followed by `cache.put`. With a no-store origin, that background fetch cannot revalidate, so each boot re-transfers the full body of every tier it served.
4. terrain_bc7.js:831-832 ("rehydrate by re-fetching their payloads (immutable HTTP cache)"), :706 and :1373 (`_rebuildTierMips`) all assume an HTTP-cache copy. `_releaseArrayMirror` (:1316) frees the CPU mirror unconditionally after upload (:1452-1466). So a context-loss restore under ?nosw=1 or a non-secure origin re-downloads the whole tier over the network.
5. serve.py also gzips .hbc7 (:576 BIN_COMPRESS_EXTS). Measured ratio is 0.94 at 19.6 MB/s on this laptop, and the compressed t512+t1024 set (~95 MB) overflows the 96 MB COMPRESS_CACHE (:618), so it gets re-gzipped on later requests.
findings.proposal:
(1) scripts/serve.py end_headers: add ".hbc7" to the revalidating `no-cache` tuple. 304s then work through the existing If-Modified-Since paths: :785-798 for compressed bodies, the stdlib path for identity.
(2) Serve .hbc7 identity. Either drop it from BIN_COMPRESS_EXTS, or add the HBC7 header magic to `_is_identity_only`. 6% savings is not worth ~4 s of gzip CPU per t1024 set plus a TTFB that waits for whole-body compression.
(3) service-worker.js SWR branch: make the refresh conditional. Send `fetch(url, {cache:'no-store', headers:{'If-Modified-Since': cached.headers.get('last-modified')}})` and skip `cache.put` on 304, so an unchanged asset costs one header round trip instead of a full body plus a Cache Storage rewrite. Same rule for the PNG/EXR assets under /scene3d/assets/.
(4) Fix the three 'immutable HTTP cache' comments, or make the restore read from the SW cache explicitly. No URL flag needed: server and SW behaviour only, same bytes delivered.
findings.expected_gain:
Derived from measured file sizes, live headers and code reading:
- Warm boot at high bandwidth tier: ~97 MB of wire avoided (t128+t512+t1024 color+nra, x0.94 gzip). In the foreground on no-SW origins (?nosw=1 dev/bench URLs, the raw tailnet http origin); in the background but competing with boot traffic on SW origins.
- Low tier (t128+t512): ~20 MB, which is ~4 min of a 666 kbps link on every returning boot.
- Every WebGL context loss without the SW (summer handoff: ~7/session on the 1070): ~76-81 MB re-download turns into an HTTP-cache hit. Terrain is missing until that download lands.
- serve.py: ~4-5 s less gzip CPU per t1024 set served.
None of this shows up in fresh-profile cold benches.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger-compact/open/walls checked for hbc7, SWR, stale-while, scene3d/assets, no-store, Cache-Control, immutable. The only related item is the open lead '/scene3d/assets/ SWR pairs stale manifest with mixed files' (unverified, and about generation mixing, not bandwidth). The 'Remacri costs are wire (81 vs 20 MB)' item counts first-visit bytes only. Git log has no .hbc7 caching commit (661971a8 added Cache-Control for shards only). url-flags has no row.
findings.verify_how:
1. Laptop: `curl -sI` a .hbc7 URL and expect `Cache-Control: no-cache` plus Last-Modified, and a 304 with If-Modified-Since.
2. Node: extend tests/service_worker_cas_verify.test.mjs or harness/test_service_worker_v3.mjs (vm-loaded SW, fake cache/fetch). Assert that the SWR hit issues a conditional fetch and skips put on 304.
3. Orchestrator, one headless wireframe tab on a loopback origin with the SW active: boot twice with the same profile and sum transferSize of .hbc7 entries in resource timing (after setResourceTimingBufferSize).
4. 1070, ?nosw=1: force WEBGL_lose_context and compare terrain_bc7 _stats.bytes delta and mirrorRestores before and after.

findings.title: All .json/.jsonl is served no-store: per-LB scenery/spawns/events layers, data catalogs and 51 plugin manifests are re-downloaded every boot, and force-cache does nothing
findings.area: scripts/serve.py headers; per-LB layer fetch (src/lib.rs, baked_ambient_source.js); plugins/*
findings.evidence:
1. serve.py:561 has .json/.jsonl as compressible text, but they are missing from the revalidating tuple at :871-877, so they get :887 no-store. Live probes on :8765 and :7080 of data/spells-catalog.json, dist/scenery-retail/0xA9B3.scenery.jsonl, dist/spawns/0xA9B4.spawns.jsonl and plugins/index.json all return `no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`. proxy.cjs:110-113 passes the header through.
2. Per-LB layers: lib.rs:4569 (scenery) and :5505 (spawns) via fetch_bytes; baked_ambient_source.js:194 (events). Holtburg 121-LB ring measured at 7.48 MB raw / 1.30 MB gzip, plus wcid_to_setup.json at 150 KB gzip. The wasm caches are evicted with their LB (pre-4.8 #18), so re-entering an LB downloads the body again.
3. Callers that ask for HTTP caching get none: `{cache:'force-cache'}` at spellbook.js:108, spell-research-panel.js:67, api.js:174, ac_spell_cast_sequence.js:119, ac_icon_cache.js:485, scene3d/index.js:2297, dye-preview.js:75.
4. spells-catalog.json (1.79 MB raw, 145 KB gzip) has four independent loaders, each with its own fetch and JSON.parse: buffs-hud.js:366 (at mount, :1251), spellbook.js:108, spell-research-panel.js:67, rynth/hud_bridge.js:1053. JSON.parse measured 11.5-13.2 ms (node, laptop). data/*.json total is 6.8 MB raw / 0.54 MB gzip.
findings.proposal:
(1) serve.py: put .json and .jsonl in the revalidating `no-cache` set. Narrow the exclusion from `path.endswith("manifest.json")` to the top-level dist pointer (`/dist/manifest.json`) plus `_health.json`. The current suffix test would also catch plugins/*.manifest.json.
(2) Drop `force-cache` from the /data fetches so revalidation stays authoritative and a regenerated catalog is never sticky. This also removes the documented 'spells-catalog force-cached (nosw+hard reload)' trap. The alternative is stamping those URLs with a build hash. rynth/hud_bridge.js:1048 is owner-protected: either leave it (it would become sticky until a cache clear) or exempt /data from step 1.
(3) Add one shared `loadSpellsCatalog()` in plugins/api.js, the same pattern as `_ensureComponentCatalog` at :170, and use it from buffs-hud, spellbook and spell-research-panel. Rynth stays untouched. Do the same for spell-components.json (4 fetchers).
findings.expected_gain:
Derived from measured sizes:
- ~1.9 MB gzip per warm Holtburg boot: 1.30 MB ring JSONL + ~0.4 MB of boot-time data JSON + 0.15 MB wcid_to_setup. That is ~23 s of a 666 kbps link on every returning boot; busier rings are larger (scenery LBs reach 270 KB raw each). Bodies become 304s; request count is unchanged.
- Re-entering an evicted LB in-session goes from full bodies to 304s.
- Main thread: ~12 ms of JSON.parse saved per duplicate catalog consumer (buffs-hud at boot; spellbook, research and others on first open), plus their duplicate downloads.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger checked for no-store, jsonl, json caching, force-cache, spells-catalog. Related only: the open lead '2.1 MB cast-table JSON parse on main thread at idle' (parse cost, not caching or duplication) and the wall noting spells-catalog 'force-cached (nosw+hard reload)'. That wall is actually false under serve.py's no-store. The 2026-08-03 and 06-11 serve.py fixes moved JS/wasm/images to no-cache and missed JSON. Nothing in git log; no url-flag.
findings.verify_how:
1. Laptop curl: expect `no-cache` plus 304 on revalidation for the JSONL, data JSON and plugin manifests, and no-store still on /dist/manifest.json.
2. Node: an api.js unit test asserting one fetch across three consumers of loadSpellsCatalog (mirror plugins_late_client_bind style).
3. Orchestrator headless warm reboot: sum transferSize of .jsonl/.json entries (raise the resource-timing buffer first).

findings.title: Importmap deps (three, postprocessing, takram, addons) are never modulepreloaded and sit 4 serial fetch levels deep, 2 of them cross-origin on jsdelivr, before any boot code runs
findings.evidence:
1. index.html:1001-1013 and index-bundled.html:1002-1012 map three, three/addons/, postprocessing and tiny-invariant to https://cdn.jsdelivr.net.
2. Unbundled arm: the boot module statically imports scene3d/adapter.js (index.html:1840), which does `import * as THREE from "three"` (adapter.js:30). So the inline module, including wasm init and login, cannot evaluate until three.module.js arrives, and that file then pulls ./three.core.js (node_modules/three/build/three.module.js:6). That is two serial cross-origin levels.
3. Bundled arm (what the proxy serves when fresh): the bundle's top-level static imports include three (85), postprocessing (12), @takram/three-atmosphere (5), three-clouds (2), geospatial-effects, OrbitControls and BufferGeometryUtils. vendor/takram/three-atmosphere.js imports @takram/three-geospatial. three-geospatial.js imports three/addons/loaders/EXRLoader.js (CDN). EXRLoader.js:12 imports ../libs/fflate.module.js (CDN). That is 4 serial levels after the 6.5 MB bundle.
4. Nothing preloads them. gen-modulepreload.mjs:86 skips bare specifiers by design, and index-bundled.html:1031-1033 preloads only the pkg glue, the snippet and the app bundle. Local vendor .js files are no-cache (serve.py:871), so a warm boot pays 2 serial 304 levels.
5. No SRI, and boot hard-depends on a third-party CDN being reachable.
findings.proposal:
(1) In both generators (gen-modulepreload.mjs and build-shell.mjs), resolve bare specifiers through the page's importmap and walk the static imports of the targets (vendor/ files directly; CDN targets through the identical node_modules copies). Emit `<link rel=modulepreload>` for the closure: three.module/core, the 3 addons, fflate, postprocessing, and the 5 takram files.
(2) Self-host three@0.184.0, postprocessing@6.39.1 and tiny-invariant from the exact node_modules builds (e.g. vendor/three@0.184.0/...) and repoint the importmap. Use the unminified files so the three.core.js line references in docs still hold. Update harnesses that `page.route` the CDN URL, e.g. scripts/net-review/npc-counter-probe.mjs.
(3) If the CDN stays, at minimum add `<link rel=preconnect href=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net crossorigin>`.
findings.expected_gain:
Derived from RTT x levels; RTTs are assumed:
- Cold boot: up to 4 serial levels plus CDN DNS/TLS leave the pre-login critical path, ≈0.25-0.75 s at 50-150 ms WAN or tunnel RTT.
- Warm boot: 2 serial 304 levels (~2 RTT).
- Robustness: boot no longer fails when jsdelivr is blocked or down.
- Same module bytes, so no behaviour change.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger searched for jsdelivr/cdn/importmap/three.core/preconnect/self-host. Only hit: the stars.bin external-CDN open lead, which is a different asset fetched post-boot. The modulepreload open leads (STATIC_RE / loop.js subtree, regenerate without dropping wasm preload) are about relative modules. Bare specifiers are skipped deliberately at gen-modulepreload.mjs:86 and nothing covers them. Git log: only 658d1798 (importmap for clouds). No url-flag.
findings.verify_how:
1. Node: extend the preload generator test to assert the importmap closure is emitted (13 entries) and that every emitted URL resolves.
2. Orchestrator, one headless tab, fresh profile through the proxy: use CDP Network timing to compare the requestWillBeSent time of fflate.module.js and three.core.js against the bundle's responseEnd, and time-to-`form-shown` (__bootStateHistory), with and without the preloads.
3. Offline test: block cdn.jsdelivr.net and confirm a self-hosted build still boots.

findings.title: The shell-bundle rebuild only starts when a request arrives, so the first visitor after any source edit gets the 384-module unbundled page, including the first arm of a 1070 cold-boot A/B
findings.evidence:
1. shell_gate.cjs:146-163: `decide()` serves unbundled when the bundle is stale, and it is the ONLY caller of `scheduleBuild` (:158). There is no watcher or poll. proxy.cjs:92 calls decide() only for index.html requests.
2. Observed live today: index.html mtime 17:45:13. At ~23:05, GET :7080/apps/holtburger-web/index.html answered `x-hb-shell: unbundled; changed: index.html` with `cache-control: no-store`. shell-manifest.json and index-bundled.html were rebuilt only at 23:06:10, after that request (app-fd6a99ed.js became app-6c8efc04.js). The bundle had been stale for 5 h 20 min with nothing rebuilding it.
3. scripts/perf-worker/coldboot/coldboot.mjs:58 boots `/apps/holtburger-web/index.html` through the proxy with a fresh profile per arm (`hbb-cold-${LABEL}-${Date.now()}`). So the first arm after any edit measures the unbundled page and later arms the bundle.
4. Cost of the unbundled page (slow-link doc and shell_gate.cjs header): 384 files / 3.95 MB vs 15 / 1.35 MB, ~370 more requests, ~35 s more at 666 kbps.
findings.proposal:
In createShellGate, add an unref'd interval (e.g. 15 s) or a debounced fs.watch on app/, scene3d/, plugins/, ui/, rynth/ and index.html that runs `check()` and calls `scheduleBuild(c)` when stale. The bundle is then rebuilt within quietMs (+~2 s build) of the last edit, whatever the traffic. Keep the never-serve-stale rule.
Respect the laptop rules: before spawning, take harness/lib/heavy_lock.mjs or check free memory; the build is ~240 MB / 2 s and already niced. Harness side: coldboot.mjs and flag-bench should request index.html until `x-hb-shell: bundled` before arm 1, and record that header per arm.
findings.expected_gain: The first visitor after each edit gets the 15-file bundle instead of ~384 modules: ~2.6 MB and ~370 requests less, ~35 s less at 666 kbps, a few seconds faster to ready on a fast link. Basis: the measured slow-link and shell_gate figures; the 14→6 s ready figure covers items 1-5 combined. It also removes a systematic bundled/unbundled asymmetry between cold-boot A/B arms.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger searched for shell_gate/unbundled/bundle/quiet. Only the 10-07 deleted-input bug is covered ('shell_gate served unbundled for 2 days... fixed 10-09'), plus the T11 deploy open lead (plugin lane, pkg hashing). Neither covers request-triggered rebuilds or arm asymmetry. Git log has no shell-gate watcher. The url-flags `shell` row documents only the escapes.
findings.verify_how: Node: add a shell_gate test with injected fake timers and runBuild. Edit an input, issue no requests, advance quietMs+poll, and assert runBuild was called and that `decide()` then returns serveBundled. Live check: edit a comment in a scene3d file, wait ~30 s, and confirm the next `curl -sI :7080/apps/holtburger-web/index.html` shows `x-hb-shell: bundled`.

findings.title: Login waits on a serial chain: 51 no-store plugin-manifest fetches (initPluginBar) run before the 7.6 MB wasm compile even starts, and boot.hba is not preloaded
findings.area: index.html boot sequence; app/plugin_bar.js; plugins/loader.js; plugins/gen-index.mjs; bake_worker(.js/_client.js)
findings.evidence:
1. index.html:1958 `await initPluginBar(...)` completes before the wasm `init()` at :2017. init() is where the preloaded bytes start compiling. initAutoLogin (:6772) and the form come after everything.
2. initPluginBar → buildBarSlotsViaLoader → fetchManifestIndex (loader.js:916-958): plugins/index.json, then 50 *.manifest.json (24.8 KB total), all served no-store. That is 2 serial levels, ~10 rounds on HTTP/1.1's 6 connections. Then loadPlugins and mountBar. The bundle only inlines plugin modules (build-shell.mjs:329-357), not the manifests.
3. init_resource_source (index.html:2560) fetches manifest.json and then the 2 MB boot.hba, but only after initPluginBar + wasm init + SW register; nothing preloads boot.hba.
4. The `?sharedWasm=on` branch already shows the safe pattern works with this glue: `WebAssembly.compileStreaming(fetch(url))` then `init({module_or_path: module})` (index.html:1998-1999).
5. The bake worker separately runs `init({module_or_path: URL})` (bake_worker.js:144) unless threads-lite passes module+memory (bake_worker_client.js:1131).
findings.proposal:
(1) Before `await initPluginBar`, start `const modP = WebAssembly.compileStreaming(fetch(<same stamped URL as the preload>))`. At the existing init point, call `init({module_or_path: await modP})`, falling back to the URL path on rejection. Compile overlaps the manifest fetch and plugin mount. Instantiation, and therefore every JS-visible wasm state, happens at exactly the same point as today, so plugin mount order and the client:null contract are untouched.
(2) Post the compiled Module to the bake worker at prewarm (a `module` field without sharedMemory). The worker then calls `init({module_or_path: msg.module})`, which skips its wasm fetch/304 and any re-compile.
(3) plugins/gen-index.mjs: embed each manifest in its index.json descriptor, and have fetchManifestIndex use the embedded manifest when present (1 request instead of 51). build-shell.mjs: emit the manifests into the bundled registry (0 requests).
(4) Add `<link rel=preload href="../../dist/boot.hba" as="fetch" crossorigin>` to both pages. It matches the wasm's later same-origin cors fetch. Allowlist the 'preloaded but not used' console warning if it fires on slow links.
findings.expected_gain: Assumed; no phase timings exist. ~2 serial RTTs and 50 requests come off the pre-wasm path. Liftoff compile of the 7.6 MB module (~100-300 ms) overlaps with plugin-bar work. The 2 MB boot.hba download starts at HTML parse instead of after the chain. Net estimate: ~0.1-0.5 s earlier form/login on WAN or tunnel boots, more on slow links where the link idles during the chain.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger searched for initPluginBar/plugin manifest/preload/WebAssembly.Module/compileStreaming/overlap. Covered so far: concurrent manifests (49 serial became concurrent), the wasm preload, bakeWorkerPrewarm (A6), and threads-lite sharedWasm (needs COOP/COEP plus a threaded pkg). None moves compile ahead of initPluginBar, shares a Module without shared memory, inlines manifests, or preloads boot.hba. Nothing in git log; url-flags only has bakeWorkerPrewarm/sharedWasm.
findings.verify_how: Node: a fetchManifestIndex test with an embedded-manifest index (1 fetch) and a fallback test (51 fetches); a gen-index test. Orchestrator, one headless wireframe tab: add performance.mark around initPluginBar, init and init_resource_source. Compare time-to-`form-shown` (__bootStateHistory) over 3 boots per arm, cold and warm, and check that console errors stay at 0.

findings.title: Ring-layer requests ignore lane priority: 4 high-priority GETs per landblock (one an advisory sidecar) share the browser's high-priority queue with the urgent interior lane
findings.evidence:
1. fetch_bytes = FetchPriority::Auto (http.rs:48-50), which Chromium treats as HIGH (http.rs:52-58).
2. Per cold LB: the scenery JSONL (lib.rs:4569). The `urgent` argument is only plumbed to the Setup resolve; the comment at lib.rs:5101-5108 says the JSONL is a direct GET.
3. A fire-and-forget `.scenery.jsonl.sha256` sidecar for the advisory E5 WARN (lib.rs:4662-4669), default ON (`freezeHash`, parser lib.rs:13052-13055).
4. The spawns JSONL (lib.rs:5505) and the events JSONL (baked_ambient_source.js:194, default fetch priority).
5. The first scenery call and the first spawns call AWAIT a debug-only `bake-source.sha256` / `source.sha256` log fetch before any LB is fetched (lib.rs:5118, :5685; SoA twins :6041, :6180).
6. shard_fetch_worker sends the normal lane as 'low' and the urgent lane as 'high' (worker header). So the player's urgent interior records queue FIFO behind ~484 ring-layer HIGH requests per 121-LB ring on HTTP/1.1 routes: LAN, tailnet, and the 1070's loopback relay.
findings.proposal:
(1) Pass `urgent` into scenery_fetch::fetch_one_lb and spawn_fetch::fetch_one_lb, and use FetchPriority::Low when not urgent.
(2) maybe_gate_freeze_hash: fetch at Low and after the LB's records land. Better, make it opt-in (`freezeHash=on`) or sample 1 in N, since it is WARN-only.
(3) Turn both maybe_log_sha256 awaits into `spawn_local` at Low.
(4) baked_ambient_source.js: `fetch(url, {priority:'low'})`.
Needs one wasm rebuild; JS part is live.
findings.expected_gain: Derived: on 6-connection HTTP/1.1 pools at ~3-5 ms per small request, ~484 high-priority requests ≈ 0.25-0.4 s of queue the urgent lane can wait behind. 121 requests per ring disappear entirely if the sidecar becomes opt-in. Two serial round trips come off the first scenery and spawn batch (the player's own LB). Near zero on the h2 public route.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger searched for priority/urgent lane/freezeHash/sidecar/A13a. The freezeHash row (S14) moved the sidecar off the blocking path but kept a HIGH request per LB and called that 'zero streaming latency'. Nothing covers JSONL priority or the awaited debug sha logs. Wall check: interiorStabChunk/walkPace/bakeUrgentReserve are wasm-side permits and chunking, while this is the browser socket pool's priority class for non-shard GETs.
findings.verify_how: Native Rust unit test that fetch_one_lb chooses Low when !urgent (via a priority-recording fetch shim, or a source-pin test as used for other wasm32-only paths). Orchestrator headless on the HTTP/1.1 proxy: CDP Network.requestWillBeSent `initialPriority` per URL class, plus the urgent-record queue time (requestTime→sendStart) during the ring fan-out, before and after.

findings.title: Service worker static routing: let the hundreds of requests the SW never handles skip its fetch event
findings.evidence:
1. service-worker.js:459-463: every GET from a controlled client, including page modules, wasm, CDN modules, per-LB JSONL, data JSON, suite/texchan bins, and requests from controlled dedicated workers, is dispatched to the SW's JS thread. The handler then returns early for anything outside shards, manifest bins, boot.hba and /scene3d/assets.
2. That same SW thread also handles every intercepted shard: caches.open, match, a 3-way body tee, a full-body arrayBuffer for sha256 (:362-398), and cache.put.
3. The SW path on warm boots was never benched: scripts/perf-worker/coldboot/pw1070/playwright.js:46 forces nosw=1, and coldboot.mjs runs use fresh profiles.
findings.proposal:
In the install handler, when `event.addRoutes` exists (Chrome 123+), register: `fetch-event` routes for /dist/shards/*, /dist/manifest/*.bin, /dist/boot.hba and */scene3d/assets/*, then a final catch-all route with `source:'network'`. Routes are evaluated in registration order. Non-intercepted requests then bypass SW JS dispatch and any SW cold start entirely.
Optional follow-up, verify the semantics first: route shards to `{cacheName}` and let shard_fetch_worker, which already sha-verifies, call `cache.put` itself. That removes the SW tee and second hash from the dominant request class.
findings.expected_gain: Not measured, low confidence. Removes SW dispatch latency and SW-thread queueing (and SW restarts after 30 s idle) for roughly hundreds to 1,000 non-intercepted requests per boot and per landblock crossing. The size depends on SW-thread load during shard bursts.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger searched for addRoutes/static routing/fetch handler/SW dispatch. SW items covered: CAS verify-before-persist, bake gate, SW v3 dormant, the put-after-purge open lead. Nothing about dispatch overhead or routing. Nothing in git log.
findings.verify_how: Orchestrator headless on a loopback (secure) origin with the SW, warm profile. Raise the resource-timing buffer, then compare the `fetchStart - workerStart` gap and total duration for JSONL and module requests with and without routes. Add a worker-side PerformanceObserver in shard_fetch_worker for worker-timeline entries. Node vm test: install registers routes only when addRoutes exists.

verdicts.code_truth: Every citation checks out at HEAD. serve.py:870-885: the revalidating `no-cache` tuple is (.js .mjs .wasm .bin .hba .png .jpg .jpeg .webp .ktx2 .exr). There is no .hbc7, so .hbc7 falls to :887 `no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`. serve.py:576 `BIN_COMPRESS_EXTS = {".wasm", ".bin", ".hba", ".hbc7"}`; :618 is the 96 MB COMPRESS_CACHE. Live `curl -sI` on :8765 for t1024/0x06006D06_color.hbc7 returned `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`, and so did the t128 tier manifest.json. terrain_bc7.js:109 sets DEFAULT_BASE; :491 is a plain fetch. service-worker.js:441-443 makes /scene3d/assets/ SWR, and :483-492 is a background `fetch(event.request)` plus `cache.put` on every hit. terrain_bc7.js:705-706, :831-832 and :1369 all say "immutable HTTP cache". `_releaseArrayMirror` (~:1309) zeroes mipmaps after registering a restore that calls `_rebuildTierMips`, which re-fetches the payloads (`loadTerrainBc7Channel`). The fleet runbook boots the 1070 at http://127.0.0.1:8765 (serve.py through the ssh -R relay) with `?nosw=1` mandatory, so the restore re-downloads over the tunnel. The public route is cloudflared → proxy.cjs:7080 → serve.py, and proxy.cjs:110-113 copies the header through. One error: a high-bandwidth boot fetches t128 then t1024 only. t512 is fetched only when lowBandwidth() reverses the order (terrainBc7TierOrder, :184-187), so t128+t512+t1024 never happens in one boot. Gzip ratio re-measured at 0.971 and 20.5 MB/s on one t1024 file.
verdicts.novelty: New. No ledger hits for hbc7, no-store, SWR or Cache-Control. The only adjacent open lead is 'SWR pairs stale manifest with mixed files', which is about generation mixing, not bandwidth. Git has only 661971a8 (Cache-Control on shards). The 2026-08-03 serve.py fix moved PNG/EXR to no-cache but never covered .hbc7. No url-flag.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None. It adds evidence to two walls: 'Remacri costs are wire (81 vs 20 MB)' and 'Do not release texture CPU copies broadly … only via the rehydrate seam'. The terrain rehydrate seam assumes an HTTP cache that the server's no-store forbids, so today its re-supply path is a full network download.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical. Same bytes, only caching headers and SW refresh behaviour change. Like the existing JS/PNG tier, the mtime-based If-Modified-Since check can false-304 if a file is rewritten within the same second, but these files only change on a re-derive. Dropping gzip (sub-proposal 2) does not touch pixels.
verdicts.gain_realism: Real, but overstated. A warm high-tier boot is t128 (1.4 MB) + t1024 (78 MiB ≈ 81 MB), about 79 MB raw / ~75 MB on the wire, not 97 MB. A low-tier boot is t128+t512, ~21 MB. On SW origins (public https, loopback without nosw) that traffic is a background SWR re-download on every warm boot. On nosw/http origins (the 1070 runbook URL, tailnet http) it is a foreground re-download. Each context loss that restores the terrain arrays re-downloads ~78 MB (both channels), and terrain stays missing until it lands. On the owner's LAN/tailnet link this costs seconds of background transfer per boot; on slow or remote links it is minutes. Fresh-profile benches see nothing. Sub-proposal 2 (serve .hbc7 identity) is a trade, not a clear win: it saves ~4 s of server gzip CPU per t1024 set but adds ~6% (~1.2 MB at low tier, ~15 s at 666 kbps) to first visits. Once step 1 makes bodies cacheable it matters much less. Step 1 alone recovers the wire. Step 3 additionally avoids rewriting ~80 MB into Cache Storage, and a duplicate HTTP-cache copy, on every warm boot.
verdicts.corrected_claim: .hbc7 terrain tiers are served no-store (serve.py:887; .hbc7 is missing from the :870-885 no-cache tuple). Every warm boot therefore re-transfers its tier set: ~75 MB wire at high bandwidth (t128 + t1024; t512 only on low, ~21 MB). On SW origins this happens in the background through the SWR refresh (service-worker.js:483-492); on nosw/http origins, including the 1070 runbook URL, it is in the foreground. Every terrain context-loss restore re-downloads ~78 MB because `_rebuildTierMips` relies on an 'immutable HTTP cache' that no-store forbids (terrain_bc7.js:706/:832/:1369). The fix: add .hbc7 to the no-cache tuple (S effort, pixel-identical), make the SWR refresh conditional (or let the HTTP cache revalidate) and skip `put` on 304, and correct the comments. Dropping gzip for .hbc7 is optional and costs slow-link first visits ~6%.

verdicts.code_truth: Confirmed. http.rs:48-50 makes fetch_bytes FetchPriority::Auto. lib.rs:4569 and :5505 fetch the JSONL directly, and the comment at lib.rs:5101-5108 says `urgent` only routes the Setup resolve. lib.rs:4662-4669 spawns maybe_gate_freeze_hash, which fetches `<lb>.scenery.jsonl.sha256` at Auto (:4725-4727). The dist has 65,026 such sidecars. `freezeHash` is default-ON (only `freezeHash=off` skips it, :13052-13055). maybe_log_sha256 is AWAITED before the first scenery and spawn batches (lib.rs:5118, :5685; SoA :6041, :6180), as a one-shot. shard_fetch_worker.js:545 sends 'low' and 'high' lanes. statics.js:1020 passes `urgent` only for the urgent batch.
verdicts.novelty: New. The ledger has nothing on JSONL priority, the sidecar or the awaited sha logs.
verdicts.wall_conflict: Distinct from interiorStabChunk/walkPace/bakeUrgentReserve, which are wasm permits, not browser priority. Consistent with the round-trip wall.
verdicts.visual_safety: Only partly 'pixel-identical'. Final frames do not change, but demoting non-urgent scenery/spawns JSONL to Low puts ring placement lists behind the low-priority normal-lane shard flood (statics textures etc.). That changes when ring trees and spawns appear and could slow time-to-scenery, so it needs a measured A/B. Demoting or making opt-in the advisory sidecar, and detaching the debug log fetches, changes nothing visible.
verdicts.gain_realism: HTTP/1.1 routes only (LAN, tailnet, the 1070 relay); ≈0 on the h2 public route. The sidecar is 121 high-priority requests per 121-LB ring for a WARN-only check, so making it opt-in or Low is a clean win of a few hundred ms of socket-queue time at most during the fan-out. Detaching the two awaited log fetches saves ~1 RTT on the first scenery and spawn batch, which is ms on loopback. The JSONL demotion gain (~0.25-0.4 s less queueing for urgent interior records) is unproven and could be offset by later ring scenery.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The default-ON E5 freeze-hash sidecar adds one HIGH GET per LB (121 per ring) for an advisory WARN, and two debug sha256 log fetches are awaited before the first scenery and spawn batches. Making the sidecar opt-in or Low, and spawning the log fetches, are clean, invisible wins on HTTP/1.1. Demoting the JSONL layers themselves to Low is a streaming-order change: it needs an A/B of time-to-scenery against urgent-record queue time and is not a free pixel-identical win.

verdicts.code_truth: Confirmed. service-worker.js:459-463: every GET from a controlled client enters the fetch handler and returns early unless isCacheable (shards, boot.hba, manifest/*.bin) or SWR (/scene3d/assets/). The install handler (:87ff) has no addRoutes. Shard hits do the CAS verify/put work on the same SW thread. SW_V3=false (:39), so the route list must follow the same predicate split (packs/index under v3).
verdicts.novelty: New. The ledger and git have nothing on static routing or SW dispatch overhead.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical. Routes reproduce the handler's own early-return set, with a network fallback.
verdicts.gain_realism: Unmeasured, and the finder correctly rates it low confidence. It applies only to SW-controlled secure origins (the public https tunnel, loopback without nosw). The 1070 runbook and bench URLs use ?nosw=1, so the owner's measured route gains nothing. For SW players it removes SW dispatch, and SW-thread queueing behind shard hashing, for several hundred non-intercepted requests per boot (bundled: JSONL ring ~363, data JSON, workers; unbundled: ~430 modules more). Likely sub-ms to a few ms each under shard bursts. The optional shard `{cacheName}` follow-up needs semantics verification, because it would bypass the CAS verify-before-persist.
verdicts.corrected_claim: On SW-controlled origins every non-intercepted GET still dispatches to the SW thread. Registering static routes in install (fetch-event for the cacheable and SWR set, network catch-all), derived from the same predicates, removes that dispatch. The gain is small and unmeasured, and absent on the nosw 1070 route.

refutes.reasons:
I opened every citation and checked the core claim at HEAD.

**The no-store header is real.**
- In scripts/serve.py, the revalidating `no-cache` tuple at :870-885 is .js/.mjs/.wasm/.bin/.hba/.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp/.ktx2/.exr. It has no .hbc7, so .hbc7 falls to the `no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` branch at :887.
- Live probes agree. `curl -sI` on :8765 and on proxy :7080 for t1024/0x06006D06_color.hbc7 returns that header; proxy.cjs:109-114 passes it through unchanged. An If-Modified-Since request already gets `304 0`, so fix (1) is a one-line header change.
- The git history shows no deliberate choice. a5d5961a added .hbc7 to BIN_COMPRESS_EXTS (gzip), and nothing ever put it in the cache tuple. It is an oversight.

**It is on the default path.**
- terrainBc7Enabled defaults ON. terrainT1024Mode returns `auto` when absent, which runs the ladder.
- buildTerrainBc7Atlas (no baseUrl, called from terrain.js:4416) resolves `scene3d/assets/terrain_bc7/t1024`. The static t128 pair comes from the same tree. _fetchPayload (:491) is a plain fetch.
- The pack route (`?packSource`) is OFF by default, and SW_V3=false. No content-addressed or immutable mechanism covers these files.
- service-worker.js:441-443 makes /scene3d/assets/ stale-while-revalidate. On a hit, :483-492 runs a background `fetch(event.request)` plus `cache.put`. Because the origin sends no-store, the HTTP cache never holds a copy, so each refresh is a full-body download.

**Context-loss restore.**
- _releaseArrayMirror is reached by default in _promoteToFullTier → swapOne. It zeroes the mipmaps.
- _rebuildTierMips re-fetches through loadTerrainBc7Channel. It has no in-memory memo; it relies only on the "immutable HTTP cache" that no-store forbids.

**Pixels.** Fix (1) and the SW change deliver the same bytes, so output is pixel-identical.

**What I could not refute.** It is a real, S-effort, pixel-safe fix.

**Where the scale is overstated, beyond what the first verifier caught:**
1. **Context loss happens once per session, not ~7×.** The release is one-shot. The `done` latch and `tex.__hbAfterUpload = null` in _armUploadWatcher (:1259) consume it. The restore callback writes `dst[i].data = src.data` and never re-arms a release. The registry skips entries that have pixels (texture_rehydrate.js). demoteTerrainUnderPressure and promoteTerrainT1024Now have no callers outside terrain_bc7.js and the docs, so promotion happens once. Result: only the FIRST context loss after promotion re-fetches ~78 MB. Later losses find the 88 MiB mirror resident and do not touch the network.
2. **On the bare default URL with the SW active, there is no load-time effect.** The page reads every .hbc7 from Cache Storage immediately. The 78 MB is a background refresh, and the t1024 one starts only after the deferred promotion (scene-ready plus 2 s settle, or the interior hold). The real costs on that path are server uplink, client data, and an ~80 MB Cache Storage rewrite per boot. That is not boot latency.
3. **Warm boot is ~79 MB raw / ~75-77 MB on the wire, not 97.** It is t128 + t1024; t512 loads only on low bandwidth.

**Where the claim is stronger than written:**
- **The owner's real play path pays in the foreground.** MODE P in fleet-runbooks.md uses `http://127.0.0.1:8765/...&nosw=1` with a persistent profile (C:\Temp\cdpwb-wls) over the ssh -R relay. With no-store, every owner boot re-downloads t1024 in the foreground; fix (1) would let that profile's HTTP cache answer with 304s.
- **The nosw restore freezes rendering, it does not just leave terrain missing.** webgl_context_recovery.js parks the whole frame pump during rehydrate, with a 15 s DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS. If the 78 MB re-fetch over the relay misses 15 s (below ~42 Mbps), the pass logs a MISS and the terrain renders BLACK.
refutes.strongest_counterargument:
On the bare default URL, the configuration the task names, the SW is active on a secure origin. Every .hbc7 is served from Cache Storage immediately, so no boot ever waits on these bytes. The re-download is a background SWR refresh that starts only after the deferred t1024 promotion (scene-ready plus settle). By then the content-addressed shards are also served from Cache Storage, so little foreground traffic competes with it.

The context-loss cost is also once per session, not ~7×. The terrain mirror release is one-shot, the restore puts the 88 MiB mirror back permanently, and demote/re-promote has no callers.

So for the default user, the "high / load-time" framing comes down to background bandwidth plus a Cache Storage rewrite per warm boot. The foreground load-time and restore-stall costs appear only on nosw or plain-http origins. Those are the owner's MODE P URL and the dev/bench URLs, and fresh-profile benches see none of it.
refutes.residual_claim:
The .hbc7 terrain tiers are served `no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` because .hbc7 is missing from the revalidating tuple in serve.py (:870-885, falling to :887). This is confirmed live, and proxy.cjs passes it through. It is an oversight: commit a5d5961a only added .hbc7 to gzip.

**Cost by origin:**
- **SW origins (the bare default URL):** every warm boot pays a background SWR re-transfer of t128 + t1024, ~79 MB raw / ~76 MB on the wire (t128 + t512, ~21 MB, on low bandwidth). The page itself reads Cache Storage, so boot latency does not change. The cost is server uplink, client data and an ~80 MB Cache Storage rewrite per boot.
- **nosw / http origins, including the owner's MODE P play URL (`?nosw=1`, persistent profile, ssh -R relay):** t1024 is re-downloaded in the foreground on every boot, after the deferred promotion.
- **Context loss:** only the first loss after the once-per-session promotion re-fetches ~78 MB, because the mirror release is one-shot and the restore leaves it resident. On nosw origins that re-fetch runs while the frame pump is parked, and if it misses the 15 s rehydrate deadline the terrain renders black.

**Fix:**
1. Add .hbc7 to the `no-cache` tuple. Effort S, pixel-identical; the IMS 304 path is already verified (`304 0`).
2. Optionally make the SWR refresh conditional and skip `put` on 304, so warm boots stop rewriting ~80 MB into Cache Storage.
3. Correct the three "immutable HTTP cache" comments (terrain_bc7.js :705, :831, :1369).

Dropping gzip for .hbc7 is an optional trade: it saves ~4 s of server CPU per t1024 set but adds ~3-6% to first-visit bytes.

**Impact:** medium-high. It is high for the owner's nosw play path and the restore stall, and background-only for the default SW path.

None of this is measured live: the laptop is SwiftShader and HD/BC7 only engages with BPTC. The numbers come from the 2026-08-05 1070 census and the T15R 1070 capture, plus arithmetic from the code.

findings.title: Atlas NRA arrays are allocated at the 4x HD diffuse size but hold nearest-neighbour copies of retail-res normal/height maps: 16 identical texels per real one, ~150 MB of heap plus matching VRAM
findings.evidence: Bucket size comes from the member's map: static_atlas.js:1671 `const w = img.width | 0, h = img.height | 0;`. On BPTC hardware (the 1070) `mat.map` is the full-tier BC7 CompressedTexture (bc7_textures.js:2101 `mat.map = tex`). Its image size is the payload size (makeBc7Texture, bc7_textures.js:744-751), i.e. the Remacri x4 upscale. The NRA array is allocated at that same size (static_atlas.js:1334 `buildNraArray(w, h, alloc)`) and packed at it (static_atlas.js:1764 `packNraLayer(ud.nraArray, entry.layer, mat, w, h, ...)`). The sources stay at retail DAT size: the BC7 upgrade swaps only `mat.map`, and normalMap stays the wasm Sobel plane from adapter.js:1207 surfacePixelsToNormalTexture; the height plane and texchan roughness/AO are also DAT-size. _texChannel (static_atlas.js:412-433) stretches each source to w x h with _liftChannel, a nearest-neighbour lift (static_atlas.js:394, 'Nearest-neighbour channel lift'). The code counts this (`stats.nraResampled`, :517) but nothing uses the count. The singleton path samples that same DAT-size normal map bilinearly, so atlased props get blockier 4x4-texel normals and a terraced statPom height field, while the far/mip>=2 look is unchanged (a box filter over a 4x4 block returns the source texel exactly). Per-layer cost is dominated by NRA: `_perLayerBytesFor` bc7 = bc7LevelBytes(w,h) + w*h*4 (:1224), so 4/5 of each layer's bytes. Measured (docs/2026-08-05-1070-black-flicker-and-renderer-oom-handoff.md §12, 1070 Nanto, after statAtlasGrow): NRA arrays 150.9 MB of 863 MB live texture bytes; the arrays are generateMipmaps=true (:366-386), so the GPU holds the same plus 1/3. The statNra validation in url-flags.md ran on SwiftShader, which has no BPTC, so buckets there were RGBA8 at DAT size and the mismatch could not show up.
findings.proposal: New flag `?nraSourceRes` (ship default-on after one batched 1070 look; `=off` escape). (1) In _getOrCreateBucket record `ud.nraW/ud.nraH` = the first member's NRA source size (mat.normalMap.image size, or planeFor(PLANE.NORMAL) size when released). Add that size to the bucket key in _bucketKeyFor (`|n64x64`) so only same-ratio members share a bucket and no member is resampled down. (2) buildNraArray(ud.nraW, ud.nraH, alloc); packNraLayer(..., ud.nraW, ud.nraH); in _growBucketLayers use the NRA stride (nraW*nraH*4) for the NRA prefix copy; _drainNraPending passes p.ud.nraW/H; _perLayerBytesFor/_layerCapacityFor take the NRA size. (3) The shader needs no change: sampleAt is `textureGrad(name, vec3(uv, vLayer), dFdx(vMapUv), dFdy(vMapUv))` (:634-635) in normalized UV, so mip selection follows each array's own size. Apply the same to static_array_pool.js (statArrayMerge) so the twin path does not drift.
findings.expected_gain: Derived from the measured 150.9 MB of NRA (1070, Nanto) and the x4 Remacri statics corpus (2,931 surfaces): roughly 100-140 MB less JS heap and 130-185 MB less VRAM on the same route. The exact figure depends on the x4/x1 bucket mix (read `__atlasStats()` nraResampled vs nraLayersPacked). Side gains: packNraLayer's per-texel loop, each per-layer texSubImage3D, and the whole-array generateMipmap on every feed and every ~10 Hz repack all shrink about 16x for x4 buckets (GPU-process work), and each bucket family fits about 4x more layers in its byte budget (fewer pages, which are +1 draw each, and fewer grow copies).
findings.novelty_check: Searched the ledger for nra, resampl, nearest, NN lift, half-res nra, nra dims. The only hits are the NRA->BC5/BC7 compressed bake (a different mechanism, a bake change, never attempted), statAtlasGrow (allocation count, already shipped), and the raise-ceiling refutation. Git log `rg -i nra` shows only X5, the texture worker and the default-on commits. url-flags.md has no NRA resolution knob.
findings.verify_how: Targeted node test (test_static_atlas_growth.mjs / test_nra_pack_lut.mjs style): a BC7 bucket with w=256 and a 64^2 normalMap must give nraArray.image.width===64 and 64^2*4 bytes per layer; packed bytes must equal the old NN layer sampled at 4x4 block centres. On the 1070, flag A/B on the 4-hop route: `__diag.textures().aliveByOrigin` for the static_atlas NRA row, `__atlasStats()` pages/grows, and a close-up eye check of atlased stone/plank props (smoother normals and relief expected).

findings.title: Every HD texture record fetched through bc7_blocks/xu7_blocks stays in the main wasm shard cache for the whole session, though JS keeps its own budgeted copy (~112 MB measured at one settled spot)
findings.evidence: Default routing: index.html:2652 `bc7mod.initBc7Source({ wasmExports: __hbWasmNs })` passes no fetchImpl/xu7ParsedImpl, so Bc7RecordSource fetches full records through the main-thread wasm (bc7_textures.js:1363-1368 `this._wasm.bc7_blocks(id)`, :1689 `this._wasm.xu7_blocks(id)`). bc7_blocks (lib.rs:12508-12557), bc7_pre_blocks (:12569-12592) and xu7_blocks (:12614-12639) all do `source.prefetch(&[key]).await; source.get_file_by_key(key)`. prefetch puts every body into the namespace-blind shard cache (manifest_source.rs:1095 `cache.insert(task.key, Arc::new(bytes))`). get_file_by_key returns a clone and leaves the entry in place (manifest_source.rs:1237-1253 `return Ok((*bytes).clone())`). The cache never evicts at its default budget (shard_cache.rs:121-123: `budget == usize::MAX (the default)`; the ledger says still usize::MAX on 10-19). JS keeps its own copy in Bc7RecordSource._cache (budget bc7RecordsMB 256 MB) and in the texture mipmaps, so the wasm copy is pure duplication. For xu7 it is the pre-transcode payload, which nothing in wasm reads again. Measured: task-T15R-report.md:41-46, 1070 legacy arm at settle: `bytesFetched 112,191,340` over 321 records, `records.bytes 186,595,544`. All 112 MB of those fetched payloads stay resident in wasm. The 2026-08-05 census split the shard cache at Nanto as main 234 MB / bake worker 73 MB; HD exports run only on main (the bake worker does no compressed-texture work, wall #123), which fits HD records being most of the 161 MB gap. Wasm memory.grow never shrinks, so these bytes also raise the linear-memory high-water.
findings.proposal: Add `ManifestResourceSource::take_file_by_key(key)`. It removes the key from the ShardCache (new `ShardCache::remove`, keeping total_bytes/order in sync) and returns `Arc::try_unwrap(arc).unwrap_or_else(|a| (*a).clone())`, which also saves one memcpy of up to 4 MB per record. Use it in bc7_blocks, bc7_pre_blocks and xu7_blocks behind `?hdRecordRetain` (default `off` = take; `on` = old behaviour). Pack and boot-pack sources are unchanged (consult order stays). Optionally keep a small per-namespace LRU (e.g. 32 MB) instead of zero retention as a middle ground. Add a per-namespace byte tally to publish_shard_cache_diag (`__hbShardCache.byNs`) so the split is attributable. This is not the walled small global budget (#122): DAT records are re-read by every LB build walk, but an HD record has exactly one reader (Bc7RecordSource, single-flight per rsId through _inflightP) that keeps its own budgeted copy, so take-on-read cannot cause walk refetch churn. A re-ask after JS eviction becomes a Service Worker Cache Storage hit plus worker sha verify instead of a wasm hit; the re-transcode already happens on that path today.
findings.expected_gain: At least 112 MB of main-thread wasm linear memory at a single settled location on the 1070 (equal to the measured bytesFetched). Derived ~150-200 MB on the six-town route: JS-side BC7 at Nanto was 297 MB naive, and xu7 is about 59% of BC7. An interior like Town Network fetched 151 xu7 records (~200 MB) that would no longer accumulate. One fewer full-record memcpy per HD fetch.
findings.novelty_check: The ledger treats the shard cache as a 'DAT working set' (walls #121 and #122; open leads 'shard record cache unbounded', 'census of main/worker overlap', 'Rust store budgets'). None of them identify HD texture namespaces being held twice in wasm and JS, and none propose namespace-scoped take-on-read. The ST5 lane-T path (xu7_cas_info, lib.rs:12742) sends xu7 around wasm only under the opt-in ?texCompressedOnly; the default arm still goes through wasm and retains. Git log has no shard-cache/no-retain/take commit, and url-flags.md has no such flag (shardBudgetMB is global).
findings.verify_how: Native unit test in holtburger-resource-http (orchestrator runs cargo): insert, take, assert absent, total_bytes decremented, a second take misses, and a prefetch round's protection still holds. On the 1070: `await __diag.wasmMem()` shardRecords for main at spawn-settle, A/B `?hdRecordRetain=on|off`. Expect the drop to match `__bc7Stats().bytesFetched`, `__bc7Stats()` errors to stay 0, and no re-fetch storm (count re-asks).

findings.title: Far-ring patch render targets each keep an unused 512^2 depth renderbuffer (~1 MiB each, 25-49 live), and the per-LB bake arrays stay alive after baking
findings.evidence: far_terrain.js:885-917 allocates `patch.rt = new THREE.WebGLRenderTarget(texels * PATCH_LB, texels * PATCH_LB, { depthBuffer: true, ... generateMipmaps: true })`. Defaults are texels 128 and radius 8 (far_terrain_flags.js:85-96), so 512x512, and farRing is default on (:72-81). With no depthTexture, three creates a DEPTH_COMPONENT24 renderbuffer at setup (three.module.js setupDepthRenderbuffer ~12930-12945), about 4 B/px on D3D11, kept for the RT's life. The bake draws one LB heightfield mesh per tile with an ortho camera pointing straight down (far_terrain.js:762-774 rig: the scene holds only root+cam+mesh; :950-1004 per-tile draw). A top-down heightfield never overlaps itself, so the depth test changes no pixel. Patches retire only past Chebyshev radius+PATCH_LB = 12 (:1350-1357), so 25 to 49 patches are live. After the bake, finishPatch disposes only `d.geom` (:1600-1605). The lbData arrays (positions, indices, codes, mergeData, heights, acNormals, acLightNormals; :1548-1551) live until disposePatch (:1625-1628), although buildPatchGeometry has already copied them into the merged patch geometry (:1581).
findings.proposal: Use `depthBuffer: false` on patch.rt (the per-tile `renderer.clear(true, true, false)` then clears color only). If a future overlay needs depth, share ONE 512^2 DepthTexture across all patch RTs instead. In finishPatch, after buildPatchGeometry, keep only the lbData keys (farLbKeys bookkeeping) and null the typed arrays.
findings.expected_gain: 25-49 MiB less VRAM (1 MiB per live patch; derived from patch count x 512^2 x 4 B), about 2-4.5 MB less JS heap (~5.7 KB per LB x 16 LBs x live patches), and no 16 per-tile depth clears per patch bake.
findings.novelty_check: The ledger's far-terrain items are the RADIUS POLICY fix, farLbKeys pruning, farBakeCompileAsync, an undisposed bake material clone (open), the far paint decline and the fog-silhouette look. None covers the patch depth attachment or lbData retention. Git log and url-flags (farTexels/farRadius/farDepthBias) have nothing either.
findings.verify_how: Laptop SwiftShader: readPixels of a baked patch RT with depthBuffer true vs false must be byte-identical (`__farTerrainState()` exposes the patches). Count GL renderbuffers via `__diag` before/after. The 1070 needs no eye test.

findings.title: Liveness-sweep despawns (maintPrune, default on) skip the per-guid bridge prune that the code claims every exit path reaches
findings.evidence: lib.rs:39555-39634 PerGuidBridgeIndexes::prune_guid documents 'this is the ONE place a guid-keyed per-entity cache is dropped. Both lifecycle entry points reach it — prune_on_delete (ObjectDelete / InventoryRemoveObject) and prune_on_guid_reuse'. It clears latest_object_icons, latest_appraisals (JSON strings), identify_meta_index, physics_script_table_index, entity_enchantments_index, projectile_index and the thread_locals DEFAULT_SCRIPT/UI_EFFECTS/RADAR_BLIP_COLOR/PROJECTILE_*/MOTION_*_STAMPS/REMOTE_AIRBORNE_STATE. There is a third exit. Liveness sweeps an entity 25 s after it leaves visibility (crates/holtburger-world/src/state/liveness.rs:322-371 deadlines, :493-507 sweep_entity, which emits EntityDespawned), and with unifiedTick and maintPrune both default on (lib.rs:679-684, :1577-1593) movement.rs:1613-1657 only does `js_spawned_guids.remove` plus a KIND_REMOVE push, with no prune_guid and no wielder_index strip. Vanilla ACE never sends DeleteObject for objects that go out of range: RemoveTrackedObject (Player_Tracking.cs:94-106) is only called from pickups and the teleport visibility fix, which is disabled by default (:240-271). So every dynamic-GUID creature or item seen and then walked away from keeps its ObjectCreate-time entries (lib.rs:39114-39134) until a GUID reuse happens to collide.
findings.proposal: In the maintPrune loop (movement.rs:1614), for every swept guid (not only those in js_spawned_guids), call `maintain_bridge_indexes_on_delete(guid, &wielder_index, &per_guid)`, which strips the wielder and calls prune_on_delete. Thread the Rc maps into that command context the same way the message handler already receives them (session/messages/mod.rs:1316-1325). Count sweeps on a new BRIDGE_INDEX_SWEEP_PRUNES next to the delete/reuse counters, and update the 'ONE place' doc to name the sweep.
findings.expected_gain: Small: roughly 50-150 B of wasm heap per swept dynamic object (more for appraised ones, whose JSON can be KB), so about a MB per several thousand creatures over a long hunting session. bridgeIndexSizes() stops growing. Stale per-guid reads for swept guids go away.
findings.novelty_check: The ledger has maintPrune default-on (JS ghost rigs), LEAK-01 (the bridge index prune on delete/reuse), and 'per-guid maps' listed as a swept bug class. None of them covers the liveness-sweep exit, which became default-on (NETSYNC-4, 2026-10-07) after the F1 list merge (2026-08-03). No matching git commit or flag.

Live (laptop is fine): `__sessionHandle.bridgeIndexSizes()` before and after walking ~300 m from a spawn cluster and waiting 30 s; with the fix, latestObjectIcons/physicsScriptTable/radar counts drop back.

verdicts.code_truth: Every citation checks out at HEAD. static_atlas.js:1671 `const w = img.width | 0, h = img.height | 0;` takes img from `mat.map.image` (:1601-1603). The bucket is built at those dims: :1334 `buildNraArray(w, h, alloc)`, :1496 (grow) and :1764 `packNraLayer(ud.nraArray, entry.layer, mat, w, h, _atlasStats)`. bc7_textures.js buildAndSwap (~:2094-2101) assigns only `mat.map = tex` via makeBc7Texture (:744-751, image dims = parsed.width/height = full tier). It never touches normalMap. The worker-NRA attach that does replace normalMap (materials.js:6677/_attachWorkerNra :6691) lives only in _upgradeCompressedFull, the ?texCompressedOnly ST5 arm, which is off by default. On the default path normal and height textures come from the wasm DAT decode at sp.width/sp.height (materials.js:5466-5474), the same dims as the RGBA8 albedo. ?statTexOverride, the only path that could feed HD pixels to wasm, is `=== "on"` opt-in (tex_overrides.js:38). _liftChannel (:394-410) is nearest-neighbour. Its comment (:389-393) assumes the normalMap always matches the albedo, which stops being true once mat.map becomes the x4 BC7 full tier. _perLayerBytesFor (:1221-1225) charges w*h*4 for NRA on BC7 buckets. The shader samples NRA with `textureGrad(name, vec3(uv, vLayer), _statUvGx, _statUvGy)` in normalized UV, with derivatives dFdx/dFdy(vMapUv) shared with the diffuse lookup. No textureSize appears anywhere and the POM steps are in UV space, so a smaller NRA array needs no shader change. nraResampled is only counted and logged (:517, :1875).
verdicts.novelty: New. The ledger has the NRA->BC5/BC7 bake (open), the statAtlasGrow allocation fix (shipped), the raise-ceiling refutation and the LUT pack speedup. None of them notes that the NRA array is sized from the HD diffuse while its sources are DAT-res. The 08-06 array-merge design doc cites _liftChannel as an intended resampler for 'nra channels whose bake size differs', again without seeing the x4 mismatch. Git log for nra shows only X5, ST4 and the default-on commits. url-flags.md has statNra but no resolution knob.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None. This is not a texFreeCpu-style CPU release (wall #120): the arrays stay complete, just at their true resolution. It is not bucket-merge arithmetic (#108) and not a draw-count claim (#107/#137). It brushes #130 (global pools mandatory) only through the proposed bucket-key split, which adds a bucket only when same-HD-dims members have different source dims.
verdicts.visual_safety: Not pixel-identical, but the change moves toward singleton parity. Up close, atlased props currently get NN-blocky 4x4 normal texels and a terraced statPom height field, while their singleton twins sample the same DAT-res normal map bilinearly. Mip>=2 is unchanged only for exact pow2 x4 ratios. The finder correctly flags one batched 1070 eye check (default-off first). Design caveats: (a) texchan roughness/AO carry their own dims in the sidecar header (suite_assets.js decodeTexchanBytes). Town Network's 290 sidecars average ~340 KB at 5 B/px, roughly 260², so near DAT res but not guaranteed equal to the normal plane. The NRA size should be the max of the member's plane dims, or roughness/AO get NN-downsampled. (b) Members with no normal or height (flat NRA) need a defined key. (c) pool_material.js:206/349/456 is a third packNraLayer/buildNraArray twin besides static_array_pool.js.
verdicts.gain_realism: The derivation holds. In the 08-05 census, BC7 atlas diffuse was 125.7 MB against 551 MB NRA (25 of 29 NRA arrays belonged to BC7 buckets), so about 90% of NRA bytes sit in f7 buckets where NRA = 4x diffuse. Applied to the post-grow 150.9 MB, that is ~137 MB in x4 buckets, which would drop to ~9 MB: about 125-130 MB less heap and ~170 MB less VRAM with the 4/3 mip chain, at Nanto on the 1070. That is consistent with the finder's 100-140 / 130-185 MB. No steady-state fps gain should be claimed. The GPU-process work per feed and repack (texSubImage3D plus whole-array generateMipmap) shrinks ~16x for x4 buckets, but those are streaming events, not per frame. Real secondary value: less VRAM pressure (about 7 context losses per session at ultra) and less heap toward the ~2.8 GB renderer OOM.
verdicts.corrected_claim: On BPTC hardware the default arm sizes each statics-atlas NRA array (and its CPU mirror) from the x4 BC7 full-tier diffuse, but fills it with nearest-neighbour lifts of DAT-res normal/height (and near-DAT texchan) planes. Sizing NRA at its sources' native dims (max over the member's planes, keyed into the bucket) saves ~125 MB heap and ~170 MB VRAM at Nanto (derived from the 08-05 census) and restores bilinear (singleton-parity) close-range normals and relief. It needs one 1070 eye check, and the same change in static_array_pool.js and pool_material.js.

verdicts.code_truth: Verified. index.html:2652 `bc7mod.initBc7Source({ wasmExports: __hbWasmNs })` passes no fetchImpl. bc7_textures.js _fetchHbc7Bytes (~:1363-1368) calls `this._wasm.bc7_blocks(id)`, and the xu7 lane (~:1686-1690) calls `this._wasm.xu7_blocks(id)` and counts `_stats.bytesFetched += b.length`. lib.rs bc7_blocks (:12508), bc7_pre_blocks (:12569) and xu7_blocks (:12614) each do `source.prefetch(&[key]).await; source.get_file_by_key(key)`. manifest_source.rs:1095 `cache.insert(task.key, Arc::new(bytes))`. get_file_by_key (:1237-1253) returns `(*bytes).clone()` and leaves the entry in place. shard_cache.rs:120-123 says budget usize::MAX is the default and 'can never evict' (order index None). The three HD namespaces are referenced in lib.rs only by these exports and xu7_cas_info (ST5 opt-in), so nothing in wasm re-reads the bodies. The shardFetchWorker (default on) moves the fetch and sha off-thread, but bodies still land in the main ShardCache through the same step-E insert.
verdicts.novelty: New. The ledger's shard-cache items are all a GLOBAL budget: shardBudgetMB deferred, 24 MB thrash wall, an owed ABAB, the N:M grammar, and a main/worker overlap census. None identifies HD texture namespaces held twice (wasm cache plus JS Bc7RecordSource._cache and texture mips) or proposes namespace-scoped take-on-read. No take/remove API exists in holtburger-resource-http. No git commit or url flag (shardBudgetMB is global).
verdicts.wall_conflict: Brushes #121/#122 (cache converges at ~307 MB; a 24 MB budget thrashes). The finder's distinction holds: those walls concern DAT records re-read by build walks, while HD records have one single-flight JS reader that keeps its own budgeted copy. Nothing in this proposal touches DAT residency.
verdicts.visual_safety: Final pixels are identical. One timing trade the finder underplays: after a JS bc7RecordsMB eviction (541 evictions on the 08-05 route), a re-ask today is an instant wasm hit. After the change it becomes an SW Cache Storage read plus a shard-worker sha of up to 4 MB plus re-insert, admitted through the paced TexUpgradeQueue. HD re-sharpening on re-entry could lag slightly. The finder's optional small per-namespace LRU covers this.
verdicts.gain_realism: Plausible. The T15R 1070 capture (task-T15R-report.md:41-46) shows bytesFetched 112,191,340 over 321 records at settle. The 08-05 census independently corroborates it: main shardRecords 245 MB over 5,914 entries (41 KB average) against the worker's 76 MB over 3,078 (25 KB average). Main's surplus of large entries matches ~100+ MB of HD payloads living only on main. memory.grow never shrinks, so the win is a ~110-200 MB lower main-wasm linear-memory high-water from boot, not a release mid-session. That is renderer-process RAM, not JS heap or VRAM, so it does not move fps and only modestly helps OOM headroom. The saved memcpy (Arc::try_unwrap) is minor.
verdicts.corrected_claim: On the default arm every HD texture payload (tex-bc7 / tex-bc7-pre / tex-xu7) fetched through the main wasm stays in the never-evicting ShardCache for the session, duplicating the JS-side budgeted copy. Taking the entry out on read (or a small per-namespace LRU) avoids ~110 MB (1070, one settled spot) to ~200 MB (route) of main-wasm linear-memory growth. Cost: a re-ask after JS eviction becomes an SW-cache fetch instead of a wasm hit.

verdicts.code_truth: far_terrain.js:887-913 creates `patch.rt = new THREE.WebGLRenderTarget(texels*PATCH_LB, ..., { depthBuffer: true, stencilBuffer: false, generateMipmaps: true, ... })`. PATCH_LB=4 (:89), farTexels defaults to 128 (far_terrain_flags.js) giving 512², and farRing defaults on. three r184 setupRenderBufferStorage / getInternalDepthFormat allocate a DEPTH_COMPONENT24 renderbuffer when there is no depthTexture (three.module.js:11246-11275, :12670-12700). The bake scene holds root, an ortho camera pointing straight down and one mesh (:752-779). Each tile draws a single 81-vertex heightfield, the 9x9 grid from the per-LB decode (:1494-1532), with FrontSide, so no pixel is covered twice and the depth test cannot decide anything. Retirement keepR = radius + PATCH_LB = 12 (:1349-1357). finishPatch disposes only d.geom (:1602-1605). lbData keeps positions, indices, codes, mergeData, heights, acNormals and acLightNormals until disposePatch (:1625-1628). No re-bake path can reuse them, because d.geom is nulled and bumpFarCompositeEpoch disposes and re-fetches whole patches (:1797-1804).

verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical. A single-valued heightfield drawn top-down gives no overlapping fragments. Without a depth attachment, GL/ANGLE treats the depth test as always passing. The three r184 program key does not depend on the render target's depth attachment (only global log/reversed-depth flags), so bakeProgramReady / farBakeCompileAsync do not fork.
verdicts.gain_realism: Derived from code: 1 MiB per live patch (512² x 4 B; D24 maps to D24S8 on D3D11), times 25-49 live patches, gives 25-49 MiB VRAM. lbData is about 5.7 KB per LB x 16 x 25-49 patches, so 2.3-4.5 MB of JS heap. refutes.reasons:
I could not refute it. Every link checks out at HEAD, and the one claim the earlier verifier only estimated now has data behind it.

(a) Citations. static_atlas.js:1671 takes w/h from mat.map.image. On the 1070, mat.map is the BC7 full tier, and bc7Enabled() is default-on behind the BPTC probe. :1334 builds the NRA array at those dims and :1764 packs it at them. bc7_textures.js buildAndSwap only reassigns mat.map. The only code that replaces normalMap (materials.js _attachWorkerNra) sits under ?texCompressedOnly, an exact-match opt-in that is off. On the default path normal and height come from the wasm decode at sp.width/sp.height (materials.js ~5466-5474). _liftChannel is nearest-neighbour, and its comment assumes normalMap and albedo share dims, which stopped being true once the BC7 swap landed. The NRA arrays are built with generateMipmaps=true; the singleton normal map is bilinear with mipmaps and anisotropy.

(b) Full tier really is x4 of DAT size. The bc7_textures.js clip-alpha note gives a DAT 128x128 surface a 512x512 full tier (152,256 = 16 x 9,516). The PAGE-RESAMPLE ledger entry says "TEXREF declared DAT dims while full tier is 4x upscale".

(c) Texchan roughness/AO are DAT size too. I read the headers of all 5,475 served sidecars in ~/hb-serve/dist/current/suite: mostly 128², 256², 64², 512² (288 files), and only 8 at 1024². So every NRA source plane is DAT size.

(d) Byte split, new data. docs/RESULTS-atlas-occupancy-2026-08-05.json rows sorted by capacity (BC7 vs RGBA8 is decided by the cap formula): of the 123 MB of occupied NRA, 119.25 MB (97%) sits in f7 (BC7) buckets. That includes 2048x2048 at 32 MB for 2 layers, which is DAT 512 lifted 4x. The earlier verifier assumed ~90%, so the derived saving is about 0.97 x 150.9 x 15/16, roughly 137 MB of CPU copy and about 180 MB of VRAM with the 4/3 mip chain. That is at or just above the top of the claimed 100-140 / 130-185 MB range. aliveByOrigin counts CPU bytes, which confirms the heap side.

(e) No existing mechanism. No NRA-resolution flag appears in url-flags.md. The worker NRA is ST5 opt-in. pool_class_key and the drawPools resample are opt-in. Commits since August touched the NRA path only with byte-identical LUT and column-map speedups.

(f) No shader change needed. Sampling is textureGrad in normalized UV with dFdx/dFdy(vMapUv). Nothing calls textureSize, and the POM steps are in UV space. Mip levels >= 2 of the current array equal the native levels for exact power-of-two x4 ratios, so only the near field changes. Side gain: smaller per-layer pack loops, texSubImage3D calls and whole-array generateMipmap work. That pack loop was measured at 345 ms of one frame on a 1070 teleport before the LUT fix.
refutes.strongest_counterargument:
The look change near the camera is real, and calling it an improvement is an assumption until someone sees it. Since 2026-08-05 the owner has looked at statPom relief on the 1070 only in its current form: a 4x nearest-neighbour seam-height field with vertical groove walls 4+ HD texels wide, which give hard parallax and sun-shadow edges. Bilinear sampling at native resolution makes grooves V-shaped and softer, so POM depth and self-shadow may read weaker even though the result matches the singleton path. So the change cannot ship default-on without that 1070 look, as the finding itself says.

The gain also rests on the 08-05 Nanto census, which has not been repeated. Since then statAtlasPages and texUpgradeQueue went default-on (10-04 and 10-09). The queue grants full-tier BC7 only in visibility and distance order, and the atlas holds pending members out, so today's atlas could hold fewer or smaller x4 layers than the 151 MB baseline. Bucket-key details are also unresolved: members with no normal or height plane, and texchan dims that differ per surface (rare: 8 of 5,475 sidecars are 1024²). Only static_atlas.js matters on the default URL. The static_array_pool.js and pool_material.js twins are opt-in.
refutes.residual_claim: On BPTC hardware with the default flags, every f7 statics-atlas NRA array and its CPU copy are allocated at the x4 BC7 full-tier size. They are filled with nearest-neighbour lifts of planes that are all DAT size: the wasm normal, the seam height, and the texchan roughness/AO (all 5,475 served sidecars are DAT size). The 08-05 occupancy data puts 97% of occupied NRA bytes in f7 buckets. Sizing NRA at the member's native plane dims (the max over its planes, added to the bucket key) would save about 125-137 MB of renderer heap and about 170-180 MB of VRAM, scaled from the 150.9 MB post-grow Nanto census, which is stale and owes a re-measure under texUpgradeQueue. It would also cut NRA pack, upload and generateMipmap work about 16x for x4 buckets, and no shader change is needed. Pixels change only in the near field, where nearest-neighbour blocky normals and a terraced POM height field become bilinear, matching the singleton path. Ship it flagged; it goes default-on only after a batched 1070 eye check of statPom relief.
