Also clean: terrainLast phase plumbing (both comparators get _phaseOf; every depthTest:false material is transparent; grit streaks are transparent and lifted; terrain has no discard); depthBandSort math vs three's reversed projection; freezeWorldRoots gating; canvasDepth; cloudResScale; the orbAnimSync and minimap HUD trims (no bypassing writers); the water-flow shader (no depth use); particlesOverHaze under reversed.

Deliberately skipped: rynth, the Rust crates, the film code, the non-render parts of 6c51237b. Walls that shaped the search: draws × µs does not predict ms (so no draw-arithmetic claims), the SwiftShader limits (every GPU claim routed to a 1070 arm), the eye-test gates (every order change marked needs-eyetest), wall 162 (punch writes gl_FragDepth), wall 112 (splitting buckets spatially adds draws, so finding 3 does not split), lead #86 (finding 4 is an advance of it). The reversed-Z port itself is unusually thorough; the only real reversed bug I found is the upstream three PCF bias. The higher-value item is that terrainLast is gated away in most town views.

findings.title: terrainLast is suppressed in most town views: any kept doorway or window aperture switches it off
findings.area: scene3d/atmosphere_pipeline.js terrainLast gate; scene3d/cells.js tickPortalPunch; scene3d/portal_clip.js
findings.evidence: atmosphere_pipeline.js:2542: `_terrainLastNow = terrainLastOn && !(portalPunchPass && portalPunchPass.hasApertures)`. portal_punch.js:448-450: hasApertures is true whenever _apertureCount > 0. cells.js:4055-4073 then :4129: tickPortalPunch hands every kept aperture to setApertures(punchFlat, punchRect). clipAperturesForPunch drops only near-plane/degenerate, oversized, or fully terrain-hidden apertures; sidedness is off by default (cells.js:310-330). Live counts from the default arm (docs/reengineering/impl/task-PORTAL-BLEED-report.md:101-112, Holtburg): the 7 controlled orbit poses kept 8, 3, 9, 20, 31, 36 and 4 apertures; only the uncontrolled follow camera kept 0. So in town views with buildings on screen, the terrain still draws first. Under punchRetail the phase tags (index.js:1759-1760: worldRoot 2, terrainGroup 0; punch group 1 at atmosphere_pipeline.js:1473) make the punch erase only TERRAIN depth. It is needed only where terrain would sit in front of interior surfaces seen through the aperture: sunken or below-grade rooms, or terrain rising inside the footprint. terrainRayBlocked already samples the terrain height at each aperture (portal_clip.js:440 `hTarget = sampleHeight(bx, by)`) through a memoised sampler (_punchLosCache). url-flags.md:301 and fps-review.md:99 assume aperture-free frames are common; neither measured it.
findings.proposal: Step 1 (S): add `?terrainLast=force` (ignore apertures) and a counter `window.__terrainLast.stats()` = {frames, active, suppressedByApertures}, maintained in pipeline.render() at atmosphere_pipeline.js:2542. This measures the suppression rate and the upside, and shows where terrain-first is really needed (e.g. the Yaraq blacksmith sunken shop) before building anything. Step 2 (M): classify apertures. In clipAperturesForPunch, add a per-aperture `intrudes` bit: sample terrain on a small grid (e.g. 3 across × 4 deep, up to ~16-24 m) on the far side of the aperture plane from the camera, using the same sampleHeight and the same _punchLosCache memo key, plus the existing hTarget. intrudes = max(h) > the aperture's lowest vertex z + 0.05 m (within the floor-bias tie band). tickPortalPunch publishes pass.terrainFirstNeeded = any kept aperture intrudes. The gate becomes `_terrainLastNow = terrainLastOn && !(portalPunchPass?.hasApertures && portalPunchPass.terrainFirstNeeded !== false)`. A static alternative: compute per EnvCell in wasm once per landblock (max LB height over the cell AABB footprint vs the cell's min z) and append the bit to the aperture stream. Ship behind `?terrainLastApertures=classify` (default off until the eye test). Why it is safe for non-intruding apertures: with terrain moved last, the phase-1 punch stamps into a still-cleared depth buffer (the clear value, a no-op), interior surfaces at or above grade win the later terrain draw by depth, and terrain drawn last also occludes a doorway partly behind a mound correctly (the Bug 7 class) and gives terrain seen through two windows real depth instead of sky depth.
findings.expected_gain: Makes terrainLast's own benefit, so far unmeasured, available in the fill-bound town views where it is now switched off. Derived bound: terrain is one BatchedMesh at 6.1 ms GPU at ultra in the 2026-10-17 census. Assuming buildings, statics, entities and grass cover 20-40% of the terrain's rasterised pixels in a town view, early-Z would skip about 1.2-2.5 ms of GPU per town frame (the covered fraction is an assumption). This only becomes fps where the GPU is the binding stage; the fps review says towns at ultra are fill-bound.
findings.novelty_check: rg terrainLast / hasApertures / below-grade over all three ledgers and the slices: only shipped and eye-check-owed entries (ledger-compact 638, 951; ledger-open 233, 461), nothing on the suppression rate or the gate design. fps-review.md:99 lists 'town with and without a door in view' as an eye check only. url-flags terrainLast row (:301) assumes 'no aperture in view'. git log: no commit touches terrainLast after 217ba89a. Brushes wall 162 (the punch writes gl_FragDepth / a depthFunc flip rejects everywhere); this proposal keeps the Always punch and changes only when terrain draws relative to it.
findings.verify_how: Node: extend tests/terrain_last.test.mjs so the gate honours terrainFirstNeeded, and add a portal_clip unit test for the intrudes bit on the real-DAT Yaraq sunken shop vs a flat Holtburg cottage (fixtures as in test_terrain_water_flow). 1070 arm at Holtburg and Linvak, ultra, hbbench --uncapped + GPU census world-pass ms + __terrainLast.stats(): default vs =force vs =off, fresh profile per arm. Eye test: Yaraq blacksmith and a sloped-plot cottage doorway under force and under classify.

findings.title: ?shadows=on under the new reversed-Z default: three r184's PCF chunk adds shadowBias with the wrong sign, so thin and double-sided casters shadow their own sunlit faces
findings.area: scene3d/shader_logdepth.js installReversedZ; three ShaderChunk shadowmap_pars_fragment; scene3d/lighting.js sun shadow
findings.evidence: node_modules/three/src/renderers/shaders/ShaderChunk/shadowmap_pars_fragment.glsl.js:117-125: the PCF getShadow(sampler2DShadow) does `shadowCoord.z += shadowBias;` with NO USE_REVERSED_DEPTH_BUFFER branch. The VSM branch (:159-165), the BASIC branch (:226-232) and the point-light PCF branch (~:285) all flip to `-= shadowBias` under reversed. WebGLShadowMap.js:263 switches the PCF compare to GreaterEqual under reversed, and :477 renders BACK faces of FrontSide casters (DoubleSide: both faces). lighting.js:233-241 sun shadow: ortho far 2400 m, bias -0.0005, normalBias 0.05. Under reversed the bias therefore moves the reference about 1.2 m of shadow depth AWAY from the light while the compare is GreaterEqual. Any caster thinner than about 1.15 m along the light (rigs, posts, fences) and every DoubleSide caster fails its own compare on the lit face, so the sun term goes to zero. index.js:1595 `?shadows=on` enables exactly this three-chunk path; the CSM custom receivers (materials.js:1373-1396, terrain.js:2154, particle_fx.js:670) are already flipped correctly, and the CSM cascade lights have intensity 0, so ?csm=on is unaffected. No project code patches this chunk (rg shadowmap_pars_fragment/shadowBias in scene3d: 0 hits); tests/reversed_z.test.mjs does not cover it.
findings.proposal: In shader_logdepth.js installReversedZ, next to the existing packing-chunk rewrite (item 2), add `conventionalPcfShadowChunk(src)`. Locate the `float getShadow( sampler2DShadow shadowMap` function only, then replace its single `shadowCoord.z += shadowBias;` with `#ifdef USE_REVERSED_DEPTH_BUFFER shadowCoord.z -= shadowBias; #else shadowCoord.z += shadowBias; #endif`, and its `frustumTest = inFrustum && shadowCoord.z <= 1.0` with a reversed twin `shadowCoord.z >= 0.0`. Leave the VSM and BASIC blocks alone (they already branch; a global replace would double-wrap them). Return a note and change nothing if the anchor count is not exactly 1 (three drift). Record res.pcfShadowFix in __depthMode. The log arm strips back to the original bytes via stripReversedZBranches.
findings.expected_gain: Correctness: sun-lit faces of rigs, thin props and double-sided statics stop rendering as shadowed under ?shadows=on with the default reversed-Z. No cost (a compile-time branch). Pixel-identical on ?reversedZ=off and on every default-URL frame.
findings.novelty_check: rg shadowBias / PCF / 'shadows=on' / 'reversed.*shadow' over the ledgers: only RENDER-5 (requestShadowRaster) and the csm-default decision; the reversedZ eye-check list names 'csm=on shadows' only. three's chunk has no reversed branch for PCF (read in place). The reversed_z test and the shader_logdepth header items 1-8 list no shadow-bias handling. git log -i shadow: nothing after 4bfde09e touches three's chunk.
findings.verify_how: Node: a unit test for the chunk patcher against the real r184 ShaderChunk (anchor found once, VSM/BASIC untouched, strip-to-original equals the stock chunk). GPU smoke on SwiftShader (2D depth shadow maps render there): ?shadows=on, a 0.3 m-thick box and a DoubleSide quad on a plane, sun at 45 degrees. The lit-face luminance under the reversed default must match ?reversedZ=off (today it reads as shadowed).

findings.title: particleAlphaRetail's alpha buckets are ordered by a stale per-bucket sort key, not by where their particles are
findings.evidence: d817f9c3 made alpha particles blend with no depth write: particle_manager.js:797 and :1966 `mat.depthWrite = !retail`, and :2982 alpha buckets get renderOrder -1. Among alpha buckets the visible result now depends only on draw order. three r184 takes an InstancedMesh's transparent sort key from `object.boundingSphere.center` (WebGLRenderer.js:1884-1897), computed only while it is null (InstancedMesh.js:109, :160 computeBoundingSphere), i.e. once, from that frame's instances. particle_manager never sets or clears im.boundingSphere (rg boundingSphere in scene3d/particles: only particle_fx_kids.js:332 and a geometry read at :2375). Buckets are rewritten every tick (reset → append → finalize, :3096) and _growBucket (:862) mints a fresh InstancedMesh. Each alpha bucket's key is therefore its first-render instance cloud (a town-wide centre for gfxobj-keyed shared buckets, a stale cast point for spell buckets) and never follows the live particles. The documented trade-off at :767 ('draw in creation order, not back to front') is this mechanism. _sortBucketBackToFront (:818-840) already reads every instance translation and camera distance each tick, for per-manager buckets (:3128) and shared buckets (:739).
findings.proposal: In _sortBucketBackToFront, accumulate the instance translation sum while filling _sortKey (3 adds per instance, same loop). After the sort, set `im.boundingSphere ??= new THREE.Sphere()`, centre = mean translation (im-local, the same space as the instance matrices), radius = sqrt(max _sortKey) (unused for culling: frustumCulled is false). Apply only to alpha buckets; additive buckets are order-independent. Ride the particleAlphaRetail escape or a `?particleBucketKey=off` escape. Do NOT split buckets spatially (wall 112: splitting adds draws).
findings.expected_gain: Visual: overlapping alpha buckets (chimney or brazier smoke vs fountain mist, waterfall sheets of different falls, spell smoke vs ambient smoke) draw far-to-near between buckets instead of in a fixed arbitrary order that is wrong for half of all camera headings. Inside a bucket the existing per-instance sort is unchanged. Limit: a bucket spanning a whole town still gets one centroid. Cost: 0 draws and about 3 float adds per alpha particle per tick (derived from code).
findings.novelty_check: rg 'creation order' / 'bucket.*(sort|order)' / boundingSphere over the ledgers: only the particleSharedAlpha and particleAlphaRetail shipped rows (ledger-compact 475, 916), which state the trade-off without a fix. ledger-open 160 (water eye tests incl. particleAlphaRetail layering) is the eye test, not a mechanism. git log: no commit after d817f9c3 touches the bucket key.
findings.verify_how: Node (like test_particle_inst_alpha.mjs, real three renderer over fake GL): two alpha buckets with instances at 10 m and 40 m, camera moved to the far side. After finalize, the render-list transparent order must put the 40 m bucket first in both camera positions (today it is fixed). 1070 eye test: overlapping chimney plumes at Holtburg 0x1000fbf and a twin-fall waterfall view, orbiting 360 degrees.

findings.title: buildingMatBatch buckets qualify for batchedRuns as they stand: a one-line opt-in plus a live sizing counter
findings.evidence: Ledger-open lead (perf-oct) 'Non-opted BatchedMeshes still pay ANGLE per-range emulation (buildingMatBatch, terrain batch, other sorted buckets)' was marked never attempted and unverified. Verified against the batchedRuns requirements (batched_runs.js:358: sortObjects === false, _multiDrawCount > 1, opted in, three's batching chunks). buildings.js:341 draws through batchedMaterialFor(mat), so three's batching_pars_vertex/batching_vertex chunks are already the hbBatchSlot-patched ones. Geometry is deduped per bucket and instanced per placement (:331-337 gidOf, :362-368 addGeometry once then addInstance; header :291-292). :383 sortObjects=false, opaque members only. Statics opt in at static_batch_x.js:2388 and static_atlas.js:1346; buildings.js never calls markBatchedRuns. 78e89aa5: Linvak 126 building draws became 11 counted calls, but ANGLE D3D11 still loops ~126 ranges (each a full draw + uncached gl_DrawID + whole vertex-UBO upload, fps-review finding 1). Also checked statics.js consolidateStaticSingletons (:2627): it calls addGeometry per member, so it has no repeated ranges and gets no run gain; it should not be opted in.
findings.proposal: Import markBatchedRuns in buildings.js and call `markBatchedRuns(bm)` right after :383, under the existing ?batchedRuns flag (no new flag needed; `__batchedRuns.off` stays the live A/B seam). Before the 1070 run, read `__buildingBatchStats()` per town: (batched − uniqueGeoms) is the upper bound on ANGLE ranges removed for buildings.
findings.expected_gain: CrGpuMain (79% busy) loses (instances − unique geometries) ANGLE range emulations per building bucket per pass. Upper bound at Linvak: about 115 ranges/frame (126 − 11) if every placement repeats a model; the real figure is batched − uniqueGeoms from the live counter (derived, unmeasured). Pixel-identical: the same (range, instance) pairs, reordered only inside an opaque, depth-tested bucket.
findings.novelty_check: Advance of ledger-open 'Non-opted BatchedMeshes still pay ANGLE per-range emulation (buildingMatBatch…)': that entry is code-derived and unverified for eligibility. This adds the proof that buildingMatBatch meets every batchedRuns precondition (file:line above), the exact one-line site, the sizing counter that already exists, and the negative result for statics.js consolidateStaticSingletons. Not walled: wall 89/108 (statArrayMerge 0.0 ms) concerns bucket merging; this removes ANGLE sub-draws on the GPU-process thread (wall 83 says main-thread A/Bs cannot see it).
findings.verify_how: Node: extend tests/building_mat_batch.test.mjs with the batched_runs fake-GL path (a bucket with 6 placements of 2 geometries issues 2 instanced runs, the same per-draw uniforms and samplers, colours and matrices bit-identical). GPU smoke: batched_runs_smoke.mjs style, building bucket pixel-identical to =off. 1070: __diag.render.subDraws vs issuedSubDraws at Linvak/Holtburg plus gpu_thread_split.py CrGpuMain WebGL ms, __batchedRuns.off toggled in-session (ABAB).

findings.title: Direct-to-canvas frames under reversed-Z lose most of their distance precision on the 24-bit canvas depth (about 1,800× worse at 1.5 km than the log buffer)
findings.evidence: canvas_depth.js:72-76: screenTarget() returns null (draw to the canvas) whenever the canvas has a depth buffer, which is the default (?canvasDepth on). index.js:3099 makes the direct path draw the world to the default framebuffer. This path covers the pre-bake window (~8 s on the 1070), the atmosphere-failure fallback (the whole session) and ?wireframe=1. The canvas depth is 24-bit fixed point; three only allocates 32F for FloatType depth (WebGLTextures getInternalDepthFormat :254-290). With reversed-Z on a fixed-point buffer, precision is conventional: about z²·2^-24/near = 6 mm at 100 m, 15 cm at 500 m, 1.3 m at 1.5 km. The log buffer this replaced gave about (1+z)·5e-7 = 0.8 mm at 1.5 km. The far-ring push (far_terrain.js:438-442, a relative 8.5e-6, i.e. 1.3 cm at 1.5 km) falls far below that quantum, so the near/far-ring overlap and distant coplanar surfaces z-fight in these frames. url-flags.md:539 says the default framebuffer gets 'no precision gain'; it is in fact a regression against the log buffer.
findings.proposal: When `renderer.state.buffers.depth.getReversed()` is true and not wireframe, have the world direct path use the float-depth offscreen target the canvasDepth arm already builds: a `screenTarget(renderer, { forceFloatDepth: true })` used only at index.js:3099 (leave the portal tunnel on the canvas: tiny scene), then presentScreenTarget as the =off arm does. Fix the url-flags reversedZ 'Known gaps' text to say 'precision regression vs log' for these frames.
findings.expected_gain: Visual: no far-ring seam or distant coplanar z-fighting in the boot window and for the whole of a pipeline-failure session. Cost: one full-screen present per direct-path frame only; composer frames are untouched (derived from code).
findings.novelty_check: rg '24-bit|DEPTH_COMPONENT|float depth|default framebuffer' over the ledgers: no entry. url-flags reversedZ row (:539) lists the default framebuffer as 'no precision gain', which understates it. The canvasDepth arm (ee1456a2) builds the float-depth target only for =off. git log: no later change.
findings.verify_how: Node: a canvas_depth test that screenTarget redirects under a reversed renderer when asked, and not under log or wireframe. GPU smoke (fps_arms_smoke style, SwiftShader, reversed default): render the direct path with two coplanar quads 1 m apart at 1.2 km; the depth-tested winner is stable with the redirect and flickers or interleaves without it.

verdicts.code_truth: The citations check out. atmosphere_pipeline.js:2542 reads `_terrainLastNow = terrainLastOn && !(portalPunchPass && portalPunchPass.hasApertures);`. portal_punch.js:448-450 has `get hasApertures() { return !this._errored && this._apertureCount > 0 && this._apertureMesh != null; }`. cells.js tickPortalPunch (3917-4135) passes every kept aperture to `pass.setApertures(punchFlat, punchRect)` (~4129). PUNCH_SIDEDNESS_MODE defaults to "off" (cells.js:310-330). Phase tags are at index.js:1759-1760 (worldRoot 2, terrainGroup 0) and atmosphere_pipeline.js:1473 (punch 1). punchRetail is default-on (index.js:6287, `!== "off"`). Untagged scene objects also get phase 0 (_punchPhase, :776-790). portal_clip.js:440 does `hTarget = sampleHeight(bx, by)`. The PORTAL-BLEED report table (lines 101-112) matches the quoted kept counts. That same table also shows that the one gameplay-like camera ('follow') kept 0 of 36. The floor-vs-terrain tie the proposal relies on is real: applyFloorDepthBias (materials.js:800-830) pulls floors by -2e-4 under reversed-Z as well, so coplanar floors beat terrain whatever the draw order.
verdicts.novelty: New as a design. The ledgers carry terrainLast only as shipped (compact 638, 951) and as eye-check/arm owed (open 233, 461). Nothing covers the suppression rate, a counter, or aperture classification. git log has no later terrainLast commit, and url-flags has no such flag.
verdicts.wall_conflict: No settled wall is contradicted. It brushes wall 162 (punch / gl_FragDepth): the proposal keeps the Always punch and only moves terrain after it. Walls 97/105/141 (check boundedness before GPU work) apply to the gain: it turns into fps only where the GPU is the binding stage, which the finder concedes.
verdicts.visual_safety: Step 1 (counter plus `=force` arm) is safe as a diagnostic. Step 2's main classifier has a real flaw. It flags a doorway only when terrain on the far side rises above the aperture's lowest vertex. That misses interiors that drop below grade behind an at-grade threshold: cellars, stairs going down, sunken floors. Looking down through such a door, the terrain surface at grade inside the footprint is nearer than the descending interior surfaces. With terrain drawn last it would paint grass over the stairwell, which is exactly what the punch exists to prevent. The finder's 'static alternative' is the right shape: per EnvCell, cell min z against the max terrain height over the cell footprint. It must be applied to every cell of the building reachable through the aperture, not only the cell that owns it. Correctly flagged needs-eyetest, default off.
verdicts.gain_realism: Unmeasured on two axes. (1) Frequency: the only data point is controlled orbit poses. The follow camera, the common gameplay view, kept 0 apertures, so terrainLast may already be active in most gameplay frames and the classifier's upside could be small. (2) Per-frame saving: terrain is 6.1 ms GPU at ultra. Feature-off A/Bs (ledger 615) show that time is fragment-heavy, so early-Z can help. The 20-40% covered fraction is an assumption, and the saving is fps only in GPU-bound frames. Corrected estimate: 0-2.5 ms GPU in town frames that have apertures, times an unknown share of frames. Step 1's counter should decide whether Step 2 is worth building.
verdicts.corrected_claim: terrainLast is switched off on any frame where the doorway punch keeps an aperture. Under punchRetail that order is needed only when terrain would sit in front of interior surfaces seen through an aperture. How often town frames are suppressed has not been measured: the controlled orbit poses kept 3-36 apertures, but the follow camera kept 0. Cheap first step: a `?terrainLast=force` arm and a `__terrainLast.stats()` suppression counter, to measure the rate and the upside on the 1070. If that justifies it, classify per building (any reachable cell whose min z lies below the terrain max over its footprint means terrain-first is needed), not by terrain-vs-threshold height, and ship default-off behind an eye test.

verdicts.code_truth: node_modules/three shadowmap_pars_fragment.glsl.js:115-125: the SHADOWMAP_TYPE_PCF `getShadow(sampler2DShadow ...)` does `shadowCoord.z += shadowBias;` with no USE_REVERSED_DEPTH_BUFFER branch. VSM (:159-167), BASIC (:226-234) and point PCF (:285-295) all use `-= shadowBias` under reversed. WebGLShadowMap.js:200-201 marks the shadow camera reversed, :263 sets the compare to GreaterEqual under reversed, and :277 rebuilds the projection. LightShadow.js:216-223 keeps z in [0,1] with identity Z for reversed. WebGLLights.js:290/344/386 passes shadow.bias without negation. lighting.js:226-241: near 0.1, far = sceneSize*4 = 2400, bias -0.0005, normalBias 0.05, so under reversed the reference moves ~1.2 m away from the light. index.js:1595-1598: `?shadows=on` without csm selects PCFShadowMap with the single sun shadow. rg finds no patch of this chunk in scene3d. The shader_logdepth.js header (:153-154) even claims 'three's own shadow chunks shift their bias', which is false for 2D PCF.
verdicts.novelty: New. The ledgers mention ?shadows=on only through RENDER-5, the csm:false preset decision and the 'csm=on shadows' eye check. Nothing in git log or url-flags covers the PCF bias sign.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None. Wall 71 (shadows checkbox removed) and wall 125 explain why this path is URL-only. They do not make the bug acceptable.
verdicts.visual_safety: The fix is compile-time and scoped to the PCF getShadow body. It is pixel-identical on the default URL (no shadow maps) and on ?reversedZ=off (the branch strips out). Under ?shadows=on it is a strict improvement. Most building and static materials are DoubleSide, so their lit faces fail the compare by ~1.15 m, and the effect is probably close to world-wide self-shadowing, not just thin props. The frustumTest twin (`>= 0.0`) changes only fragments outside the shadow far plane. It is harmless but optional.
verdicts.gain_realism: No fps gain is claimed. It is a correctness fix for an opt-in debug/look path that no preset uses.
verdicts.corrected_claim: three r184's 2D PCF getShadow adds shadowBias without the reversed-depth sign flip its VSM, BASIC and point branches have. With reversed-Z on by default, `?shadows=on` (single sun shadow, bias -0.0005 over a 2400 m ortho range) pushes the receiver ~1.2 m away from the light against a GreaterEqual compare. Lit faces of DoubleSide casters and of casters thinner than ~1.15 m therefore read as shadowed. A guarded chunk patch in installReversedZ (anchor count exactly 1, PCF body only) fixes it at zero cost.

verdicts.code_truth: particle_manager.js:797 and :1966 have `mat.depthWrite = !retail`, and :2982 sets alpha buckets to renderOrder -1. three's WebGLRenderer.js:1883-1897 keys an InstancedMesh on `object.boundingSphere.center`, computing it only when null. InstancedMesh.js:109 initialises it to null, and computeBoundingSphere (:160-185) unions the current instances. particle_manager never sets or clears im.boundingSphere (rg: only particle_fx_kids.js:332 and a geometry read at :2375). _growBucket (:862) mints a fresh InstancedMesh. _sortBucketBackToFront (:818-840) already walks every instance translation. reversePainterSortStable sorts groupOrder, then renderOrder, then z, then id. Under reversed-Z the push hook in shader_logdepth.js (_fixReversedSortKeys, :423-462) negates z so the order is right. The centroid is therefore the first-render instance cloud and is never refreshed. The finder overstates one part: the key is projected through the CURRENT camera every frame (`applyMatrix4(matrixWorld).applyMatrix4(_projScreenMatrix)`), so bucket order does follow the camera. Only the centre position is stale, not a 'fixed order'. The in-code comment's 'creation order' claim is also not accurate in general.
verdicts.novelty: New. Ledger rows 475/916 and the :767 comment state the trade-off with a wrong mechanism ('creation order') and no fix. Open 415 is only the eye test. Nothing in git log or url-flags.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None. It does not split buckets (wall 112) and adds no per-bucket instanced attribute (wall 187; boundingSphere is an object property).
verdicts.visual_safety: It changes draw order between alpha buckets, so pixels change. Correctly flagged needs-eyetest. Downside: two large overlapping buckets can swap order abruptly when their live centroids cross in depth (popping), where today the stale centre is at least stable. Town-wide gfxobj-keyed shared buckets still get one arbitrary centroid either way.
verdicts.gain_realism: Zero draws and ~3 adds per alpha instance per tick: the cost claim is right. The visual benefit is narrower than claimed. For static, compact, single-site buckets the stale first-render centre is already about correct. The fix matters for buckets whose membership or positions change after first render: town-wide shared buckets as emitters stream or cull, moving spell or missile emitters, and buckets first drawn with count 0 (centre at the local origin).
verdicts.corrected_claim: Each alpha particle bucket's transparent sort key is the bounding-sphere centre three computed once at its first render (or after _growBucket), and it is never refreshed. Between-bucket order is still evaluated against the live camera each frame, but from a stale centre. That is wrong for buckets whose emitters move or whose membership changes. Refreshing im.boundingSphere.center to the mean instance translation inside _sortBucketBackToFront (alpha buckets only, behind an escape) costs nothing measurable. It should improve overlap order for dynamic buckets but can introduce order pops, so it needs the 1070 eye test.

verdicts.code_truth: buildings.js:341 builds the bucket with `batchedMaterialFor(mat)`. :331-337 and :362-368 dedupe geometry per bucket (addGeometry once, addInstance per placement). :383 has `bm.sortObjects = false`. buildingMatBatch is default-on (:181-195). markBatchedRuns is called only from static_batch_x.js:2388 and static_atlas.js:1346. batched_runs.js:150-164 patches THREE.ShaderChunk globally (batching_pars_vertex, batching_vertex, color_vertex), so any stock-batching material, including the buildings' mirrored variants, already compiles the hbBatchSlot path. The wrapper gate (:426) is `!ctl.off && _chunksPatched && sortObjects === false && _multiDrawCount > 1 && _eligible.has(object)`, and it steps aside by itself when no range repeats. rg finds no building-side shader reading gl_DrawID; only terrain_batch.js:222 does, and terrain is not proposed. statics.js consolidateStaticSingletons (:2627) calls addGeometry per member (+42), so no repeats, as claimed.
verdicts.novelty: A valid advance of ledger-open 232 ('never attempted', code-derived). It supplies the eligibility proof and the one-line site. It also contradicts ledger-compact 629's label 'Not batchedRuns-eligible': I found no blocker beyond the missing markBatchedRuns call. The finder did not cite that label.
verdicts.wall_conflict: Not walled. Walls 89/107/108 concern main-thread draw and merge arithmetic. Walls 82/83/206 explain why the gain sits on CrGpuMain and needs gpu_thread_split.py to see.
verdicts.visual_safety: Effectively pixel-identical: the same (range, instance) pairs, reordered inside one opaque, depth-tested bucket. The only theoretical difference is exact-coplanar ties between different geometries of the same material in one bucket. Under GreaterEqual the later draw wins a tie, so the winner could flip. That case is vanishingly rare for building shells.
verdicts.gain_realism: The '~115 ranges at Linvak' bound assumes each of the 11 buckets holds a single distinct geometry. Buckets are per (landblock, material), and ranges repeat only when the same model part recurs within one landblock with that material (identical cottages in one LB). The realistic saving is likely tens of ANGLE sub-draws per frame, against thousands of BatchedMesh sub-draws (5,838 at Holtburg in July): roughly 1-2% of CrGpuMain range work, probably below the 8.33 ms grid. Cost is near zero (no-repeat buckets take noGain).
verdicts.corrected_claim: buildingMatBatch buckets meet every batchedRuns precondition: stock batching chunks patched globally, sortObjects false, per-placement instancing of shared geometry. Adding `markBatchedRuns(bm)` after buildings.js:383 is a safe, effectively pixel-identical opt-in. The gain is (instances in view - distinct geometries in view) per landblock-material bucket. That is likely tens of ANGLE ranges per frame, not ~115, and should be sized live from __buildingBatchStats / __batchedRuns.frame() before claiming fps.

verdicts.code_truth: canvas_depth.js:72-76: screenTarget returns null when the canvas has depth, the default (resolveCanvasDepth returns depth:true unless =off). index.js:3099-3100 sends the direct path to the canvas, and :3242 presents only when redirected. The camera is near 0.1, far 5000 (index.js:1813). Chrome's default framebuffer depth is 24-bit fixed. With reversed-Z on fixed point, Δs ≈ s²·2^-24/near: ~6 mm at 100 m, 15 cm at 500 m, 1.34 m at 1.5 km. The old log buffer gave Δs ≈ (1+s)·ln(1+far)·2^-24 ≈ 0.8 mm at 1.5 km. The far-ring push (far_terrain.js:438-442, `gl_Position.z *= exp2(-uFarDepthBias*log2(far+1))`) is a small relative shift, far below a 1.3 m quantum. The arithmetic is right.
verdicts.novelty: Partly known. url-flags.md:539 already lists 'the default framebuffer (?wireframe=1, pre-composer boot frames) get no precision gain' as a reversedZ known gap. The finder adds that this is a regression against the log buffer, not merely 'no gain', and proposes reusing canvas_depth's float-depth stand-in for it. Both of those are new. The same regression applies to the packed 24-bit depth-stencil of ?punchOcclusion=on / ?portalStencil=on, which the finder did not mention.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None. Wall 150 (a default-off gate's allocation can cost the default path) is respected: the target is allocated only on direct-path frames.
verdicts.visual_safety: Not strictly pixel-identical. Redirecting through the HalfFloat stand-in makes those frames blend in linear space with a present encode, as the canvasDepth=off arm already does, instead of sRGB blending on the canvas. That arguably brings them in line with composer frames, an improvement, but it is a look change for boot frames. Excluding wireframe is correct.
verdicts.gain_realism: Visual only. It affects the ~8 s pre-composer window on the 1070 and whole sessions where the atmosphere pipeline fails. Whether distant near/far-ring overlap is even on screen in that window is unverified. Cost is one full-screen present per direct-path frame. Low impact.
verdicts.corrected_claim: With reversed-Z on by default, frames drawn straight to the canvas (the pre-composer boot window, a pipeline-failure fallback) use the canvas's 24-bit fixed-point depth. That is ~1.3 m depth resolution at 1.5 km against ~0.8 mm under the old log buffer: a precision regression the url-flags 'no precision gain' note understates. Routing the non-wireframe direct path through canvas_depth's existing float-depth stand-in when the renderer is reversed fixes it, at the cost of one present per such frame and linear rather than sRGB blending in those frames.

findings.title: Outdoor collider populates keep staging collision after an eviction; the 6c51237b purge only catches products staged before it
findings.evidence:
How eviction works now: enqueue_clear_landblock_collision (lib.rs:22126-22132) bumps the epoch, calls purge_pending_env_cell_products and purge_pending_populate_products, then queues the clear. The purge (lib.rs:22143-22165) drops only what is already in the BUILDING_*/STATIC_*/SCENERY_COLLIDER piles. LANDBLOCK_COLLISION_PARTS_PENDING is not in that list.

The per-build guard LandblockBuildEpoch (lib.rs:22199-22233) is used once, by fetch_env_cells_in_landblock (lib.rs:27170, plus lb_live checks after every await). The three outdoor populates never take it, and they push after their awaits:
- populate_building_aabbs_for_landblock_impl (lib.rs:22501) awaits at 22524/22594/22649/22777, then pushes BUILDING_ORIGIN (22622), BSP (22732, 22811), AABB (22839) and PHYSICS (22864).
- populate_statics_aabbs_for_landblock_impl awaits at 23016/23047/23080/23166, then pushes STATIC_BSP (23125, 23197) and STATIC_AABB (23228).
- populate_scenery_colliders_for_landblock_impl awaits at 23526/23557, then pushes SCENERY_COLLIDER (23616).
- The export wrapper (22929-22940) pushes note_landblock_collision_part after the impl resolves, with no liveness check.

On the JS side, landblock_stream.js:650-718 checks notEvicted() only between stages (before and after each wasm call), never inside one.

The TickMovement drain clears first and then inserts (movement.rs:853-871 clear, then 890/919/938 inserts, parts at 1103). Its own comment says these tables are "all append-only, so evict+re-enter must REPLACE rather than append".

The test does not cover this case: tests/collider_populate_evict.test.mjs:28-31 (P7) pins only products "a populate staged BEFORE the eviction", and P2-P6 stub the wasm call as a JS promise.
findings.proposal: In lib.rs, give each of the three populate impls `let hold = LandblockBuildEpoch::begin(landblock_high);` at entry. Wrap every `*_PENDING.with(|pile| …push…)` in `if hold.live()`, the same idiom as fetch_env_cells' queue_cell / lb_live. Return the liveness to the wrapper, or re-check `landblock_evict_epoch`, so note_landblock_collision_part is pushed only while live. Add LANDBLOCK_COLLISION_PARTS_PENDING to purge_pending_populate_products. No URL flag needed: this is a robustness fix of the same kind as STREAM-TERRAIN-3, which shipped without one.
findings.expected_gain: No fps change on the normal path. In the race case, the append-only building AABB/BSP/physics, static AABB/BSP and scenery-collider lists for that landblock stop doubling after a re-entry, so per-transition collision work there stops being up to 2x. Orphaned colliders no longer outlive the eviction. A stale STATICS part mark can no longer open the spawnz settle gate before the re-entry's static floors have drained (scene.rs:3789-3795, 7546), which would drop dock/porch creatures through the floor. Basis: derived from code. Trigger: an LRU eviction while a ring populate is suspended on a DAT prefetch, which is typical right after a teleport or portal hop (the at-cap reclaim churn noted at index.js:6926-6936).
findings.novelty_check: The ledger-compact STREAM-TERRAIN-3 row says "purge_pending_populate_products; collider populate re-checks eviction after every await". That is the JS stage checks plus a before-eviction purge, and 6c51237b's own comment says the purge "drops what it already staged". Nothing gates what an in-flight wasm populate stages after the eviction. Nothing in ledger-open/walls; `rg populate` hits only the shipped row and an unrelated BatchWalkEnd lead. `git log | rg -i 'populate|LandblockBuildEpoch'` shows no later fix. No URL flag covers it.
findings.verify_how: Native test (cfg(any(wasm32,test)), like landblock_evict_epoch_tests): run a populate impl against a MockSource whose prefetch is a manually completed future, bump_landblock_evict_epoch while it is suspended, complete the future, and assert that no pile holds an entry for that landblock and no collision part is queued. Run the negative control against HEAD. Extend collider_populate_evict P7 with a source pin that each populate impl calls LandblockBuildEpoch::begin. The orchestrator then rebuilds wasm once.

findings.title: H2 particle chain walker has no post-await liveness check, so a same-guid respawn mid-walk can destroy the new rig's emitter and leak sound timers
findings.evidence:
_attachParticleChainForEntity (entities.js:15422) awaits fetchPhysicsScript (15436), _ensureWorldParticleManager (15457), import('three'), and fetchParticleEmitter for each CreateParticle entry (15735). There is no liveness check after any of these.

After the await, it calls ownerRegistry.addEmitter(guid, …, {parent: rig, emitterId: createParticleEmitterInstanceId}) at 15856-15870.

What remove() does (14036-14066): destroyAllForOwner(g), which deletes the owner record (owner_registry.js:503-521); it clears only the timers already in _soundTimeoutsForGuid; and it deletes _particleChainsAttached, so the respawned rig walks the chain again. The respawn can be T9 _respawnForLod (16699-16740) or a re-sent CreateObject (spawn path, ~4546).

What the old walk then does when it resumes:
- ownerRegistry.addEmitter captures the epoch at call time (owner_registry.js:276), so this fresh call passes. With a nonzero instance handle that the new rig's walk already registered, the replace branch (owner_registry.js:247-262) destroys the NEW rig's emitter. The replacement is parented to the disposed, detached old root.
- Sound/SoundTable/Scale timers created before the await sit only in the walk's local timeoutIds until the merge at 15909-15921. remove() cannot cancel them. They fire behind `.has(guid)` (15606, 15621), which passes for the respawned guid, and call _fireHook on the disposed inst.

The sibling functions were given identity checks in b20cdc37: _attachVfxParticlesForEntity has live() at 15288, and _fireCreateParticleHook has its check at 19797.
findings.proposal: In _attachParticleChainForEntity, define `const live = () => { const cur = this.entityMap.get(guid >>> 0); return !!cur && !cur._disposed && cur.root === rig; };` and check it after every await: 15436, 15457, the three import, and each fetchParticleEmitter. When it fails, clearTimeout every id in timeoutIds, return a {ok:false, reason:'respawned'} descriptor, and do not merge into _soundTimeoutsForGuid. Change the two timer guards at 15606/15621 from `.has(guid)` to `this.entityMap.get(guid >>> 0)?.root === rig`. No flag needed: this is the same identity rule (ledger wall #48) applied to a missed site.
findings.expected_gain: Correctness only. It closes a race that can remove a lifestone, portal or aura emitter from a freshly respawned rig and play duplicate hook sounds. Basis: derived from code. Frequency is low: the respawn has to land while a cold record fetch holds the walk suspended, mostly shortly after a spawn or across an LOD band edge.
findings.novelty_check: The ledger-compact ENTITIES-3/4 row says "All 18 post-await .has() sites in entities.js converted incl _fireCreateParticleHook…". This walker had no `.has()` check at all, so it was not among the 18. Ledger row 471 (chain-walker Sound timers self-remove) fixed timer growth, not liveness. Wall #48 states the rule; it does not cover this site. `rg 'chain walk|attachParticleChain'` finds nothing open, and git log has no later fix.
findings.verify_how: Node test in the style of same_guid_respawn.test.mjs, with fake wasm whose fetchParticleEmitter resolves on demand. Spawn a rig with physicsScriptDid, then remove and respawn the same guid while the walk is suspended. Let the new walk land first, then resolve the old fetch. Assert that the new rig's handle emitter still exists in ownerRegistry, that no emitter is parented to the old root, and that no timer from the old walk fires. The negative control on HEAD must fail.

verdicts.code_truth: Every citation checks out at HEAD. enqueue_clear_landblock_collision (lib.rs:22126-22132) calls bump_landblock_evict_epoch, purge_pending_env_cell_products, purge_pending_populate_products, then pushes LANDBLOCK_CLEAR_PENDING. purge_pending_populate_products (22143-22165) retains only BUILDING_AABB, BUILDING_ORIGIN, BUILDING_BSP, BUILDING_PORTALS, LANDBLOCK_RESTRICTIONS, BUILDING_PHYSICS, STATIC_AABB, STATIC_BSP and SCENERY_COLLIDER. LANDBLOCK_COLLISION_PARTS_PENDING (22950) is not in that list. LandblockBuildEpoch::begin is called only in tests (22278-22305) and in fetch_env_cells (27170, `let lb_live = || evict_hold.live()`). None of the three outdoor populate impls use it. Building impl: it awaits the LandblockInfo prefetch, then pushes BUILDING_PORTALS and RESTRICTIONS. It awaits the Setup prefetch. Then, for each building, it pushes BUILDING_ORIGIN and awaits a per-model prefetch or ensure_walk_prefetched_keyed. Its BSP/AABB/PHYSICS pushes are interleaved with those awaits. Statics impl: it awaits per stab inside the loop (23080, 23166), and the STATIC_BSP/STATIC_AABB pushes (23125/23197/23228) are interleaved. Scenery impl: its single push (23616) comes after the awaits at 23526/23557. The building wrapper (22929-22940) and statics wrapper (23266-23278) call note_landblock_collision_part on Ok without checking liveness. The drains (lib.rs:21446, 22333, 22357, 22391) insert with no residency filter. TickMovement (movement.rs:853-871) clears first, then inserts, then marks parts last (1103). clear_landblocks_collision (scene.rs:5341-5454) drops the parts marks, but only for products already present when it runs. terrain_heights is never removed anywhere, so after a re-entry, landblock_collision_ready (scene.rs:3789-3795) depends only on the parts marks. On the JS side, populateOne (landblock_stream.js:649-718) checks notEvicted() only between wasm calls. P7 in tests/collider_populate_evict.test.mjs:28-31 pins only products staged before the eviction.
verdicts.novelty: New. The ledger rows (ledger-compact:442, recent-diff-covered:32) cover STREAM-TERRAIN-3's EnvCell epoch, the before-eviction purge, and the JS re-check after every await. Nothing covers what an in-flight wasm populate stages after the eviction. ledger-open:198 ('populate AABB marks collision part only on Ok') is a different lead. git log has nothing after 6c51237b that touches it. No URL flag covers it.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None. It applies walls #50/#51 (re-check the generation after every await in bake/attach) to three Rust sites that the STREAM-TERRAIN-3 fix left out. It also respects wall #127: EnvCell timing is untouched, and only the outdoor populates change.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical. Only wasm collision piles and the parts marks change. The fix makes behaviour match the intended contract (no collision for an evicted landblock until a re-entry populates it again).
verdicts.gain_realism: No fps effect, as the finder says. It is a correctness fix only, and narrower than 'medium'. (a) Trigger: an LRU eviction must land while a ring populate is suspended on a cold DAT prefetch. Typical cases are a teleport or portal hop soon after arriving, or the stale-centre at-cap reclaim noted at index.js:6926-6936. Cached prefetches probably resolve without yielding, so the window exists only on a cold fetch. (b) Result: orphan colliders stay in the evicted landblock. That is harmless while the player is away. On re-entry, only the post-eviction subset is duplicated, and that lasts only until the next eviction of that landblock clears it all. The collision cost increase is negligible. (c) The real visible risk is the remoteSettle gate, which is default ON (url-flags.md:1865). A stale BUILDINGS or STATICS mark arrives with only partial orphan geometry: the products staged before the eviction were purged, and the note is still pushed on Ok. A narrower variant also exists: a note pushed before the eviction but not yet drained is never purged. It is then applied after the clear, giving a mark with zero geometry. Either way, a re-entered landblock can report collision_ready before its floors drain, and a floating spawn can settle below a missing porch or dock floor. Both cases are rare.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The three outdoor collider populates (populate_building_aabbs/statics_aabbs/scenery_colliders_for_landblock_impl) do not hold LandblockBuildEpoch, and they push to their pending piles after awaits. Their export wrappers push note_landblock_collision_part on Ok with no liveness check, and purge_pending_populate_products does not purge LANDBLOCK_COLLISION_PARTS_PENDING. So a populate suspended on a cold prefetch when its landblock is evicted stages orphan colliders and a parts mark after the purge. Consequences: orphan colliders in the evicted landblock; a duplicated post-eviction subset after re-entry, cleared at that landblock's next eviction; and a remoteSettle gate (default ON) that can open on a re-entered landblock whose floors are incomplete. Fix: begin a LandblockBuildEpoch in each impl, gate every pile push (BUILDING_PORTALS/RESTRICTIONS and enqueue_outdoor_overlap_bake included) on hold.live(), have the wrappers note the part only while live, and add LANDBLOCK_COLLISION_PARTS_PENDING to the purge. Correctness only, rare trigger, no fps change.

verdicts.code_truth: The gap is real, but the mechanism cited is mostly off the default path. _attachParticleChainForEntity (entities.js:15422) awaits fetchPhysicsScript (15433) and _ensureWorldParticleManager (15457) with no liveness check. Then, when SCRIPT_QUEUE_ON, it returns this._queuePhysicsScript(...) at 15466-15467. SCRIPT_QUEUE_ON (entities.js:2309-2319) is coded !== 'off', so it is default ON (url-flags.md:1103). The import('three'), the hook loop, the SoundTable/Scale timers with the `.has(guid)` guards (15606/15621), the Sound timers, fetchParticleEmitter (15735) and the ownerRegistry.addEmitter call (15852-15870) therefore run only with ?scriptQueue=off. On that legacy path the finder's description is accurate. owner_registry.js reads the epoch at call time (`const epochAtCall = this._epoch(ownerKey)`), and its replace branch destroys or supersedes an existing scoped handle. remove() (14036-14066) calls destroyAllForOwner, cancels only the bucketed timers, clears _scriptManagersForGuid and deletes _particleChainsAttached. The timers are merged only at 15909-15921. On the default path the consequence is different. A stale walk that resumes after a same-guid respawn calls _queuePhysicsScript (16072) with the old rig. That re-points the new owner's ScriptManager executor and enqueues a duplicate copy of the script, or creates the ScriptManager first and the new walk then adds a second copy. _executeScriptHook (16150) resolves inst via entityMap.get(gKey), so the duplicate hooks fire on the live new inst. The stale `rig` is only threaded through CallPES. If the entity was removed with no respawn, the stale walk creates an orphan ScriptManager for a dead guid. Its hooks are dropped by `if (!inst) return`, but the manager stays in the map until that guid is removed again.
verdicts.novelty: New site. ledger-compact:458 (ENTITIES-3/4: all 18 post-await .has() sites converted) did not include it, because the walker had no .has() check after fetchPhysicsScript. ledger-compact:471 (timer self-remove) and ledger-compact:238 (anim-hooks-3, the CallPES timer same-instance guard) are different sites. Nothing in ledger-open or the walls covers it, and git log shows no later fix.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None. It is wall #48 (post-await liveness = identity) applied to a missed site.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical on the normal path. In the race it removes duplicate emitters and sounds (or, on the legacy path, a wrongly destroyed emitter), so it can only improve the look. Adding a live() check before _queuePhysicsScript does not change the non-race schedule.
verdicts.gain_realism: Correctness only, and rare. A remove plus same-guid respawn has to land inside a cold fetchPhysicsScript window, which is typically tens to hundreds of ms on first sight. Sources are an LOD band-edge respawn (thrash already fixed in 9665230d) or a re-sent CreateObject. On the default path the visible effect of a hit is a doubled script: anonymous (handle 0) emitters doubled, persistent nonzero-handle emitters replaced or restarted, hook sounds doubled. The new-rig-emitter destruction and the uncancellable-timer leak the finder describes need ?scriptQueue=off.
verdicts.corrected_claim: _attachParticleChainForEntity has no identity liveness check after its awaits. On the default scriptQueue path, a walk suspended on fetchPhysicsScript or _ensureWorldParticleManager across a remove plus same-guid respawn calls _queuePhysicsScript with the stale rig. That enqueues a duplicate copy of the script on the respawned guid's ScriptManager (doubled anonymous emitters and hook sounds, restarted handle emitters) and re-points its executor at the disposed rig. On a plain remove it leaves an orphan ScriptManager for a dead guid. The addEmitter replace and pre-merge timer leaks the finder describes are real only on the legacy ?scriptQueue=off path. Fix: an identity live() check (entityMap.get(guid)?.root === rig && !_disposed) right after fetchPhysicsScript and after _ensureWorldParticleManager, before _queuePhysicsScript. On the legacy path also check after each fetchParticleEmitter and clear the local timeoutIds on failure.

findings.title: The soft frame-cap pacer misses its target on common refresh rates: a 60 cap gives 37.5 fps at 75 Hz, 50 at 100 Hz, 72 at 144 Hz and 55 at 165 Hz
findings.evidence: index.js:519-523: softCapDelayMs = pacerDelayMs - 4 ms, always measured from the last frame's start. index.js:2673 schedules with setTimeout and then rAF. The comment at :506-515 claims 'Waking early keeps a cap at or below the refresh rate exact'. tests/frame_cap.test.mjs:326-342 checks only 60 Hz and accepts 55-73 fps for a 60 cap at 144 Hz. The probe (scratchpad softcap_sim.mjs) runs the test's own vsync model (work 6 ms, slop 1 ms) and gets, for caps 60 / 30: 75 Hz 37.5 / 25; 100 Hz 50 / 25; 120 Hz 60 / 30; 144 Hz 72 / 28.8; 165 Hz 55 / 27.5. findings.proposal: Replace the relative sleep with a timeline gate for runtime caps. Request rAF every vsync; in tick, when `_frameCapSoft` is set and `ts < capDue - halfRefresh`, re-request and return before any work; otherwise set `capDue = Math.max(capDue + _frameIntervalMs, ts - _frameIntervalMs)`. Estimate halfRefresh from a running minimum of rAF deltas. In the same model this gives 60.0 / 30.0 on every rate from 60 to 240 Hz, removes the setTimeout-jitter misses, and leaves the exact ?targetFps pacer untouched.

findings.title: An Items-tab item that leaves the pack wedges the bot on Buffing and re-casts at its dead guid about once a second (TargetNotAcquired is classed transient)
findings.area: rynth/buff_loop.js B7 layer bookkeeping + rynth/vt/index.js projectItemBuffs
findings.evidence: vt/index.js:823-866 projectItemBuffs resolves each Items-tab entry to a guid once (`items.resolveGuid(e)` at :840; combat/items.js:282-293 checks inventory only at that moment). It re-projects only when bot.buff, the spellbook, the spell table or an items/buffs/profile setting changes (:1086-1090, :953-975), never on an inventory change, so the B7 list keeps the guid of an item that was dropped, sold, traded or lost on death. ACE answers a targeted cast at an unknown guid with an immediate UseDone(TargetNotAcquired) (ACE Player_Magic.cs:135-140, GetTargetCategory). buff_loop.js:347 maps 0x042c to 'transient'. :708-709 attaches the kind-13 refusal to _itemPending; :2245-2262 hands it to _holdRefusedItem, which for 'transient' (:1561-1562) only sets `_backoffUntil = now + TRANSIENT_BACKOFF_MS` (1000 ms, :322) and never sets _itemHeldUntil. _itemDue (:1486-1493) ignores the backoff, so the item stays due. a58df981 made status (:1617-1625) count due item enchants as missing buffs, so kernel._buffNeeded() (kernel.js:219-226; 'blocked' is never set for transient) stays true. _auxLadder returns 'Buffing' before any beforeIdle slot (kernel.js ladder `if (ctx.buffNeeded) return "Buffing"`), which starves Navigate, ReadScrolls, Salvage and Doors. After each 1 s backoff (:2143) the cast loop (:2297-2318) sends CastSpell(staleGuid) again. Before a58df981 the same stale entry was only tried during self-buff passes and never held the kernel.
findings.proposal: (a) In _holdRefusedItem, give an item cast whose target is not our own guid an item-specific hold on 0x042c: `if (cls === "transient" && !p.worn && (r.code & 0xffff) === 0x042c) this._itemHeldUntil.set(key, now + PLACE_PARK_MS)`. A worn cast at our own guid stays transient (teleporting). (b) Also in _itemPass, filter non-worn entries whose itemGuid is missing from `_inventoryRows()`; the rows are already read at 1 Hz by _wornArmor. (c) In vt/index.js oneHz, re-project when the inventory signature (set of resolved guids) changes. Any one of these breaks the wedge; (b) also covers items whose cast fails in other ways.
findings.expected_gain: Derived from code. Without the fix the route stalls indefinitely and about one CastTargetedSpell per second goes to ACE for as long as the stale item stays due. That starts within the recast window (about 25 min) of its last enchant, or immediately after a Force Buff. Likely triggers: death item loss, selling at a vendor waypoint, handing gear to a mule. With the fix: at most one refused cast, then a 60 s hold or the entry is dropped.

Ledger-compact:119-122 cover other buff fixes (B5/B8, valve, skill cap). git log shows nothing after a58df981. The display.js header (:1-3, :17-22) says 'made live with RynthAi's defaults — all ON … works with no bot and with the panel closed'. rynth/vt/README.md:276 says 'Page-level: it also applies on a ?botVt=off page'. docs/rynth-integration/STATUS.md:29-33 lists 'the 60 / 30 fps limit and the steep-ground tint start ON' as owner decisions taken one by one. Dropping the session fallback is not: it removes the red steep-ground tint (passability_overlay.js, opacity 0x60/255) that every player sees today, a visible change the owner chose deliberately, so it needs an owner call rather than the finder's 'pixel-identical'. On the owner's 120 Hz panel the cap only matters where frames would land on the 8.33 ms grid (light wilderness, small dungeons); there it holds 60 instead of up to 120. Derived from code, not measured: once a58df981's display controller installs, every Playwright-driven 1070 bench is held at 60 fps with vsync, or about 73 fps in hbbench's uncapped mode (vsync off, the soft pacer wakes at I-4 ms plus slop). Whether a player who never runs the bot should get them is an owner call, not a bug. Use the safe fix: raise the background minimum and FRAME_CAP_MIN_FPS to 10, or widen the clamp only for soft runtime caps. Do not use the global max(0.1, 1.25*interval) clamp, which also changes ?targetFps<10 pages and pushes 0.2-0.25 s steps into integrators that were never run that large. Low impact, non-default setting only.

The comment at :506-515 claims 'Waking early keeps a cap at or below the refresh rate exact' and allows only 'up to one refresh fast'. vt/README.md:276 repeats the claim. tests/frame_cap.test.mjs:326-342 checks 60 Hz and accepts 55-73 for 60 fps at 144 Hz, nothing else. A 60 cap gives 37.5 fps (or 75) at 75 Hz, 50 at 100 Hz, 72 at 144 Hz and 55 at 165 Hz, contradicting the comment at :506-515. A timeline gate (rAF every vsync, render when ts >= due - half a refresh, due = max(due+I, ts-I)) makes it exact on every rate. No effect on the owner's 120 Hz panel.

coverage_notes:
I read ledger-walls.txt and both decomp-gaps slices in full, then read the retail function bodies for each candidate, not just greps. Retail functions read: CObjectMaint (UseTime with its 1 Hz visible list, the destruction queue, DeleteObject), LScape (draw, draw_check_blocks, calc_draw_order, get_block_order, get_block_orient far-block LOD, grab_visible_cells, update_loadpoint, add_ambient_sounds, SetDetailTexturing), CPhysics::UseTime, CPhysicsObj (update_object, UpdateObjectInternal, UpdatePositionInternal, UpdateViewerDistance, ShouldDrawParticles, animate_static_object, update_position, set_hidden, leave_visibility, the attack/check_attack chain, get_object_info FREE_ROTATE, process_fp_hook), ParticleEmitter (UpdateParticles, ShouldEmitParticle, InitEnd degrade distance), GfxObjDegradeInfo (get_degrade, get_max_degrade_distance), Render (SetDegradeLevelInternal, minimize_object_lighting, set_zfar, GetFogAdjustment), SoundManager (PlaySoundInternal, GetAttenuation, the 16-voice ring), SmartBox (set_viewer viewer light, UseTime, ProcessNetBlobs, HandleRenderOption, HandleDeleteObject), CellManager, GraphicsResource/SceneTool resource purge, RenderDeviceD3D (DrawBuilding, DrawEnvCell, DrawMeshInternal), ClientCombatSystem (UseTime, TrackTarget, UpdateTargetTracking), CommandInterpreter (mouse look, StopDrift, ApplyCurrentMovement), CameraSet map/look-down modes, gmRadarUI::UseTime, InterpolationManager, MoveToManager::CheckProgressMade, GameSky.

I also listed every retail Class::method name that holtburger never cites, about 1,000 of them, and triaged the render and gameplay classes in that list.

Most leads turned out to be already ported, usually with acclient.c line citations. Already done: the viewer light (?viewerLight), retail ambient gather, particle degrade distance including the penultimate-band quirk (particleDegrade), the TargetManager voyeur, PS_Hidden/UnHide, placement frames, retail sound attenuation and voices, the 40 Hz radar, building/environment detail textures (envDetailTex), far-terrain simplify, chess, BlipPlayer, the light pool's dynamic priority, and the 96 m activity gate (physupd-3, already in the ledger).

For the render tricks the dimension is close to exhausted. Retail draws landblocks back to front, its far-block LOD (2 triangles per block beyond ring 4) has no value on a 1070, and degrade ladders, portal culling and render-state sorting are all already ported or ledgered.

The one real gap is a cadence misread. Retail ticks the whole physics world, including every ParticleManager, at most once per 1/30 s (CPhysics::UseTime, MIN_QUANTUM). Holtburger's retailQuantum port says there is 'no 30 Hz gate on the direct path' and missed that outer gate. So every rule retail counts per tick runs once per render frame in holtburger. Findings 1-3 come from this. I ran a read-only Python census of client_portal.dat's 2,051 emitters to measure it (script: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-wbterminal/98168d1d-a7fa-4057-8cdb-22b89664f038/scratchpad/agent-scratch/emitter_census.py).

Findings 4 (GPU idle purge, low confidence) and 5 (an advance on an open lead) are smaller.

Skipped on purpose: UI-only classes (gm*/UIElement), net transport, rynth, and anything needing a 1070 or browser.

Walls that shaped the search: #41 (physics quantum constants / 1/30 gate, DECISIONS-A1-O5; each finding says how it differs), #120 (texture CPU copies), #6 (deg_mul pinned), #8 (IsInView), #193 (the particle sorting radius is not a cull sphere), #105/#141 (the frame is CPU-bound).

findings.title: Particle emission rate follows render fps; retail caps it at one emit per 30 Hz world tick
findings.evidence:
RETAIL: CPhysics::UseTime (acclient.c:311335) runs every object update, the static-animating loop and UpdateTexVelocity only when `quantum >= MIN_QUANTUM_93` (:311352). MIN_QUANTUM_93 = 1/30 (:783717). The other ParticleManager::UpdateParticles call sites are gated the same way: animate_static_object (:321170, MIN_QUANTUM_97) and update_position (:321678); UpdateObjectInternal (:322881) and UpdateChild only run from inside the UseTime gate. ParticleEmitter::UpdateParticles emits at most ONE particle per call (`if (ShouldEmitParticle) EmitParticle` :331230; the degraded path's RecordParticleEmission :331161). So above 30 fps retail emits ≤30 particles/s per emitter, quantised to whole ticks.

HOLTBURGER: ParticleEmitter.updateParticles also emits ≤1 per call (scene3d/particles/particle_emitter.js:531-536; the predicate `currentTime()-lastEmitTime > birthrate` is in particle_emitter_info.js:387-393). But it is called once per rAF: the static manager through tickFrame (particle_manager.js:2516-2526, driven by statics.js:6523-6535 _spLoop) and the world manager through entities.js:18062-18068. play_effect_vfx.js:1961-1975 even budgets 'a frame per particle'. The retailQuantum row (url-flags.md:1403) says physics steps 'every frame — no 30 Hz gate on the direct path', missing the outer CPhysics::UseTime gate.

DAT CENSUS (client_portal.dat, my read-only script): 1,849 BirthratePerSec and 202 BirthratePerMeter emitters; 186 per-second emitters have birthrate < 1/30 s. Modelling tick-quantised emission (emit when elapsed > birthrate, checked each tick), holtburger at 120 fps emits a median 1.14x retail's rate (p90 1.33x, max 4.0x), and 1,187 emitters run >10% faster. Steady live-particle sum is +14% at 120 fps and +7% at 50-60 fps. Worst cases: 0x32000451 98 vs 42 live; 0x320008c1/0x320007c7/0x32000553 48 vs 18; 0x320008ee 125 vs 75. 71 fast emitters with a totalParticles budget finish 1.7-4x sooner than authored.

OWNER-VISIBLE: this is the likely cause of the open lead 'Flaming weapons leave a metres-long trail of big fire puffs when running fast' (docs/HANDOFF-1070-session-2026-10-11.md:65-66, called 'retail-like physics'). Retail's tick would cap that trail at ≤30 puffs/s.
findings.proposal:
Add a manager-level retail world-tick clock and gate only EMISSION on it; particle motion keeps updating every frame. In ParticleManager._tickLatched (particle_manager.js ~2527), compute `const worldTick = now - this._lastWorldTick >= 1/30; if (worldTick) this._lastWorldTick = now;` under the existing time latch, then pass it to emitter.updateParticles(worldTick). In particle_emitter.js:532, emit only `if (emitAllowed && this.shouldEmitParticle())`; the culled/virtual-emission path does the same. Births land on tick boundaries as in retail. Positions are analytic in lifetime (particle.js:477-490), so per-frame motion stays smooth and exact.

New flag `?particleEmitTick=retail|nominal|off`, default `off` = byte-identical. `nominal` is an alternative for the owner: emit floor(elapsed/birthrate) particles per frame with sub-frame birth times, giving fps-independent density at the authored rate. Also update oneShotFiniteBackstopSec (play_effect_vfx.js:1970) to charge max(birthrate, 1/30) per particle when the flag is on.

Matches retail for every per-second and per-metre emitter. Fixes the owner's flaming-weapon trail. Perf (derived from the census, not measured): about 12% fewer live particles across emitters at 120 fps and about 7% at 50 fps, and 57-62% fewer for the fastest continuous emitters. Particle simulation, instance append/upload and alpha/additive fill all fall by the same proportion for those effects.

This proposal leaves integration alone and applies the retail tick only to the per-call emission count; the census and the retailQuantum misread are new evidence. git log: b2a55a17 fixed only the per-metre predicate; no commit touches emission cadence. url-flags.md has no particleEmitTick/emitTick/emitHz reader. particleClock=loop|sim (url-flags.md:554) unifies the clock source, not the cadence.

findings.title: Step far particle emitters at retail's 30 Hz world tick (retail stepped every particle at ≤30 Hz)
findings.evidence:
RETAIL: every ParticleManager::UpdateParticles call site sits behind the 1/30 s world-tick gate (CPhysics::UseTime acclient.c:311352; animate_static_object :321170; update_position :321678). Retail particles therefore move at ≤30 Hz at any frame rate.

HOLTBURGER: _tickLatched runs `emitter.updateParticles()` for every live, unculled emitter on every tick (particle_manager.js:2727), and ticks once per rAF (tickFrame :2516-2526; world manager entities.js:18068). The cost is known to be significant. Removing one duplicate static tick saved ~0.75 ms/frame (ledger: particleTickOnce, 49130dd3). The comment at particle_manager.js ~2712-2718 cites a 1070 profile where the static tick took 302 ms (82.6 ms of it _setPartsVisible) over the probe window. rp6TravelReach raised Linvak drizzle from ~40% to 76% live, and that perf check is still owed. Particle positions are analytic in lifetime (particle.js:477-490: lifetime += elapsed, or = elapsed), so skipping an update and sampling later gives exactly the position retail would show. The only existing far-band stride is ?entitySmoothStride (entities.js:2950-2975), and it covers entity easing only.
findings.proposal: Under `?particleFarTick=on` (default off): in _tickLatched, emitters whose sorting-sphere centre is farther than FAR_M from the camera skip updateParticles() on frames where the manager's retail world tick (the same clock as decomp-gaps-1) did not fire. They still _appendInstances() their held slot transforms, so nothing vanishes. FAR_M defaults to 40 m: retail's particle-object full-detail band is 25 m (Render::particle_distance at deg_mul 1, acclient.c:379812-379815) and holtburger's near smoothing band is 40 m. The RP6 cull, cell gate and degrade cull are unchanged. The near field (local player, spells cast on you, anything inside 40 m) keeps per-frame stepping. Optional follow-up: let held emitters skip the append copy by reusing their previous instance range.
findings.expected_gain: Derived, not measured: in towns at ~50 fps, retail ticks every 2nd frame, so far emitters run about half as many updateParticles calls; at 120 Hz about a quarter. Taking the measured ~0.75 ms/frame static tick and assuming 60-80% of live emitters are beyond 40 m in towns, that is roughly 0.2-0.4 ms/frame of renderer main-thread time at 50 fps, which helps the 98%-busy main thread. More on drizzle-heavy Linvak.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger rg for stride, Hz, half-rate, every other frame, quantum, particle tick: the hits are entitySmoothStride (entities only), particleTickOnce (duplicate driver), orbAnimSync (HUD), and wall #41 (physics integration constants, not particle sampling). Wall #165 ('particles stay unpooled') is unrelated. git log has no particle cadence or stride commit. url-flags.md has no particleFarTick or far-particle rate reader.

Positions at tick frames equal the flag-off arm. 1070: Linvak Tukal and Holtburg at ultra, renderer main-thread busy % and fps A/B against =off with fresh profiles, plus an eye check on distant fountains and drizzle for visible stepping.

findings.title: InterpolationManager's 5-tick progress window is counted per render frame, so stalled remotes blip ~4x sooner at 120 fps
findings.evidence:
RETAIL: InterpolationManager::adjust_offset (acclient.c:389178) increments frame_counter once per call. It judges progress only after 5 calls (`if (v14 < 5)` :389244, progress_made/progress_quantum/max_speed ≥ 0.3); a failed window does ++node_fail_counter and NodeCompleted(0) (:389271-389273), and UseTime blips with SetPositionSimple once node_fail_counter > 3 (:389302). It is reached once per world tick (CPhysics::UseTime gate :311352, MIN_QUANTUM 1/30 :783717 → update_object → UpdatePositionInternal → PositionManager::adjust_offset), so the window is ≥5/30 s ≈ 167 ms.

HOLTBURGER: position_manager.rs:76-78 `PROGRESS_WINDOW_FRAMES: i32 = 5`, incremented per step at :437-462, with the blip rule `node_fail_counter > 3` at :332-342. force_position_interp.rs:74 and :277-307 copy the same window for the local force-position interp. Steps run once per render frame: retailQuantum (url-flags.md:1403) integrates dt ≤ 0.2 'as ONE direct quantum ... every frame', and scene.rs:2187-2190 says 'one window advance ... per frame'. At 120 Hz a window is 41.7 ms (4x shorter than retail); at the 50 fps town rate 100 ms (1.6x). A remote that a transition blocks (wall, door, other body) reaches the 4-failure blip after ~0.17 s instead of ~0.67 s, and each short window is a noisier progress sample.
findings.proposal: Count the window in retail ticks, not render frames. Keep progress_quantum += quantum per step, but close the window when `frame_counter >= 5 && progress_quantum >= 5.0/30.0` (or accumulate quantum into a tick counter that advances by 1 per 1/30 s). This reproduces retail exactly at ≥30 fps and stays 5 frames below 30 fps. Apply it in both position_manager.rs (remote queue) and force_position_interp.rs (local force-position). Gate it on a Rust const plus a `?interpTickWindow=on` flag (default off) so the browser default stays byte-identical until a live check.
findings.expected_gain: Fidelity: blocked remotes, and the local player after a force-position, get retail's ~0.67 s before a snap at any frame rate, instead of a frame-rate-dependent 0.17-0.4 s. Remote snapping stops changing with fps. No perf effect.
findings.novelty_check: Ledger rg for interpolat* plus window/frame_counter/progress: no hits. The covered remote-motion items D1-D10, moveto-1..6 and the motion-remote rounds cover catch-up speed, gates and sticky, not window length in wall time. Wall #41 covers quantum constants for integration; this change keeps integration per frame and only fixes a counter that retail measures in ticks. git log has no interpolation-window commit.
findings.verify_how: Rust unit test (orchestrator runs cargo): feed adjust_offset_core 1/120 s quanta against a target the transition never closes, and assert the wall time to node_fail_counter > 3 is ~0.67 s with the fix and ~0.17 s without; at 1/30 s quanta both match. Live: a creature pushed into a doorway on the 1070, comparing snap timing with =off.

findings.title: Retail GPU-resource age purge (unused >120 s, purged when VRAM is low, restored on use) as a context-loss mitigation
findings.evidence:
RETAIL: SceneTool::PurgeOldGraphicsResources (acclient.c:123095) runs every 5 s. If RenderDeviceD3D::IsAvailableVideoMemoryLow, it calls GraphicsResource::PurgeOldResources(120.0) (:131192). That purges every resource that is not already lost, is marked thrashable, was not used this frame (m_FrameUsed != m_nFrameStamp) and is older than 120 s (m_TimeUsed), and marks it lost. AutoRestore re-creates it on next use (RestoreLostResources, around :131180).

HOLTBURGER: no recency-based GPU purge exists. webgl_context_recovery.js:3-7 records the context being revoked 'under VRAM/driver pressure (observed 7× on 1070 with quality=ultra + cloud RTs + CSM + lensFlare + POM during vendor open / paperdoll wield / motion bursts)'. The memory levers that exist work on the CPU side: matBudgetMB is a CPU-byte LRU that 'only disposes entries that were never handed out' (static_batch_x.js:2049; materials.js:2864-3011), and texture_release.js frees CPU copies (default-off). A texture uploaded once stays in VRAM until its owning landblock evicts or its cache entry dies. rg for lastDrawn/lastUsedFrame/idleSince/thrash in materials.js, static_atlas.js, landblock_lru.js and the texture modules finds no GPU-recency tracking. three r184 already behaves like retail AutoRestore: texture.dispose() frees the GL texture and keeps image.data, and the next draw re-uploads.
findings.proposal:
`?texIdlePurge=on` (default off). Every 5 s (the retail cadence), consider only non-atlas textures with CPU data still present: material-cache singletons, building per-material batches, EnvCell and entity textures, never DataArrayTexture atlas pages, which wall #120 rules out. Purge (texture.dispose(), keep image.data) those whose last-use frame is older than 120 s. WebGL has no VRAM query, so trigger on 'a context loss has already happened this session' (from __webglContextRecoveryHistory) OR an uploaded-byte estimate above a preset budget.

Track last use coarsely, through passes that already walk visible things: stamp a frame number on each material from the static-batch cull walk, cells.js render set and entity visibility, instead of a per-draw hook (wall #133). Keep it off texRehydrate's path, since nothing is released from CPU.
findings.expected_gain: Unmeasured. The aim is fewer of the ~7 context losses per ultra session on the 1070, each of which pauses rendering and re-uploads every texture from CPU, so a loss is the worst hitch class. Cost: a one-time re-upload when a purged texture is drawn again (one texture at a time instead of everything at once).
findings.novelty_check: Ledger rg for vram, context loss, purge, thrash, idle texture, LRU: the hits are CPU-side only (texFreeCpu, matBudgetMB, shard budgets, 'context-loss frequency soak' still open, 'GTX 1060 3GB → ultra' risk). git log rg for purge/vram/context loss: 28c64fae frees GPU memory when the animation cache evicts (entities only); nothing does age-based GPU purging. Wall #120 bans releasing CPU copies; this keeps them. Walls #121/#164 concern the JS heap, not VRAM.
findings.verify_how: First run the owed __webglContextRecoveryHistory soak on the 1070 (six-town route at ultra plus vendor/paperdoll opens) to confirm losses track uploaded texture bytes. Then interleave fresh-profile arms with ?texIdlePurge=on vs off, counting losses per hour, renderer.info.memory.textures and re-upload hitches. Node: a fake-WebGL test that a purged texture re-uploads from image.data on next render.

findings.title: Gate tier-1 PlayScript cues (flash, shockwave, decal) with the retail particle degrade distance and cell visibility
findings.evidence:
Open lead (reviews 2026-10-18 §8): '_fireTier1Cue fires flash/shockwave/decal at ANY distance (no range gate)', marked unverified. I verified it: play_effect_vfx.js:3674-3687 resolves the placement and calls fireFxCue/fireFxShowcaseCue with no distance or cell test. fx_cues.js:103-145 spawns the flash, shockwave and decal unconditionally. spawnFxShockwave (fx_distort.js:77-86) and spawnFxFlash (fx_lights.js:282-293) only evict the oldest item at their caps (FLASH_MAX 10, SHOCK_MAX), so far cues can evict near ones.

findings.novelty_check: This advances the ledger-open item 'play_effect_vfx _fireTier1Cue fires flash/shockwave/decal at ANY distance (no range gate) | WHY-OPEN: Unverified reviewer lead'. verdicts.code_truth:
Retail citations hold. CPhysics::UseTime (acclient.c:311335) runs the update_object loop, the static-animating loop and UpdateTexVelocity only when `quantum >= MIN_QUANTUM_93` (:311352), and MIN_QUANTUM_93 = 1/30 (:783717). animate_static_object (:321150) and update_position (:321658) each gate on MIN_QUANTUM_97 = 1/30 (:784229). UpdateObjectInternal (:322719) is reached only through update_object (:323081), which only the UseTime loop calls (:311375). ParticleEmitter::UpdateParticles (:331097) emits at most once per call (:331230; degraded path :331161). ParticleEmitterInfo::ShouldEmitParticle (:324500) tests the strict `cur_time - last_emit_time > birthrate`.

Holtburger matches the description. particle_emitter.js:532-536 emits once per updateParticles. particle_emitter_info.js:387-393 has the same predicate. particle_manager.js tickFrame (2516-2526) calls _tickLatched, which calls updateParticles (~2727) once per rAF, driven by statics.js:6523-6535 _spLoop. I re-ran the census with my own interval model, (floor(b/T)+1)*T. It reproduces the finder's 120 fps figures exactly: 1,849 per-second and 202 per-metre emitters, 186 below 1/30, median 1.143x, p90 1.333x, max 4.0x, and 1,187 emitters more than 10% fast.

(a) 0x32000451 at 120 fps is 84 vs 42 live, not 98; 98 is the nominal 70/s rate.

(c) The flaming-weapon main flame 0x3200026E has birthrate 0.0833, maxP 12 and a 1 s life. Holtburger emits 10.9/s at 120 fps vs retail 10/s (1.09x), and 10 vs 8.3/s at 50 fps.
