Retail holds as cited. InterpolationManager::adjust_offset (acclient.c:389178) does `frame_counter+1` and `progress_quantum += quantum` on every call, and judges progress only once `v14 >= 5` (:389244). A failure (progress/quantum/max_speed < 0.3) does ++node_fail_counter and NodeCompleted(0) (:389271-389273). NodeCompleted (:388882) resets frame_counter and progress_quantum. UseTime (:389278) recovers once node_fail_counter > 3.

Holtburger mirrors it: position_manager.rs:78 sets `PROGRESS_WINDOW_FRAMES: i32 = 5`, step_queue increments per call (~436-440), and use_time (339-341) recovers on `node_fail_counter > 3 || (queue empty && node_fail_counter > 0)`. force_position_interp.rs:76 has the same constant, and ~277-307 returns Failed and calls stop().

The per-frame claim is verified through the driver. simulation.rs:206-218 makes one slice per frame for dt <= 0.2 under retailQuantum, then calls world.step_remote_objects(slice) (:273), then step_remote_inner, then step_remote (scene.rs:7254). scene.rs:2187-2188 also says 'one window advance ... per frame'. So the window is 5 render frames.

Two corrections:
(a) At 50 fps retail ticks every 2nd frame (T = 40 ms), so retail's window is ~200 ms vs holtburger's 100 ms: 2x, not 1.6x. At 120 fps it is ~167-208 ms vs 42 ms, about 4x.
(b) With one queued node, the first failed window empties the queue and use_time blips at once. So the usual snap lag is one window (42 ms at 120 fps), not four.
verdicts.novelty: No hit in ledger-compact, ledger-open or the walls for interpolation window, frame_counter or progress. No git commit. It is a concrete instance of the umbrella A1 §3 row 8 / A1-O5 (c3) 'frame-rate-dependent tick counts' divergence, but the interp window was never enumerated, and the fix needs no global gate.
verdicts.wall_conflict: Wall #41 (A1-O5) covers the quantum constants of movement integration. This change keeps per-frame integration and only makes a counter that retail measures in ticks count wall time, so it does not contradict the wall.
verdicts.visual_safety: Needs-eyetest, correctly flagged and default-off. Blocked remotes, and the local player after a force-position, would snap later, at retail timing. Default stays byte-identical.
verdicts.gain_realism: Fidelity only, no perf effect, as claimed. Behavior in the blocked or slow-progress case stops depending on fps. Effort is small, but it needs a wasm rebuild plus flag plumbing through lib.rs.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The remote InterpolationManager window (position_manager.rs:78) and the force-position window (force_position_interp.rs:76) count 5 render frames, because remote and local steps run once per frame (simulation.rs:206-273). Retail counted 5 calls of adjust_offset, which run once per >=1/30 s world tick. The window, and so the time before a stalled node fails, is therefore ~42 ms vs ~167-208 ms at 120 fps (4x) and 100 ms vs ~200 ms at 50 fps (2x). Single-node queues blip right after the first failed window. Closing the window at `frame_counter >= 5 && progress_quantum >= 5/30` (or sharing a 1/30 tick clock) reproduces retail at >=30 fps.

verdicts.code_truth:
Retail holds as cited. SceneTool::PurgeOldGraphicsResources (acclient.c:123095) runs every 5 s; if IsAvailableVideoMemoryLow, it calls PurgeOldResources(120.0) (:123103). PurgeOldResources (:131192) purges resources that are not lost, are thrashable, were not used this frame and are older than 120 s, then marks them lost. RestoreLostResources (:131171) brings back AutoRestore resources.

Holtburger: the webgl_context_recovery.js:3-7 quote is accurate, but the '7x' was observed with quality=ultra plus CSM, lensFlare and POM. CSM is now off in every preset, and the context-loss frequency soak after the atlas-grow fix (ledger-open 292) has never run, so the current loss rate is unknown. static_batch_x.js:2046-2050 and materials.js:2864ff confirm that matBudgetMB never disposes handed-out cache materials. That is a real route-length VRAM retainer and a sensible purge target. rg finds no lastUsed or idleSince recency tracking.

Two omissions in the finding:
(a) A GPU-only dispose that keeps image.data already exists for paletted textures: palBudgetMB evictions dispose the GPU handle while image.data stays alive (materials.js:3452-3455). The new part is only the age trigger.
(b) bc7_textures.js:599 (texCompressedOnly full tier) and texture_release.js:145 (texFreeCpu) null the CPU data. A purge of those textures would re-upload empty levels. Both are default-off, and the finder's 'CPU data still present' filter excludes them, but the filter is load-bearing.
verdicts.novelty: New as an age-triggered GPU purge. Adjacent open VRAM items exist: ledger-open 287 (geometry dispose refcount), 300 (decode-admission budgets as a VRAM lever), 164 (GTX 1060 3GB sent to ultra) and 292 (the soak). Git log has nothing age-based (28c64fae only covers animation-cache entities).
verdicts.wall_conflict: Respects wall #120, since CPU copies are kept. It must stay off the texFreeCpu and texCompressedOnly released population, as noted. Walls #121 and #164 are about the heap, not VRAM, so no conflict.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical in principle: three r184 re-uploads from image.data before the draw that needs it. The risks are a re-upload or mipmap-regeneration hitch on the first frame a purged texture returns, and broken textures if the CPU-data filter ever lets a released texture through.
verdicts.gain_realism: Unknown, and the premise is unproven. WebGL exposes no VRAM query, so the trigger is a heuristic. On Windows/ANGLE, losses commonly come from GPU-process resets rather than plain VRAM overcommit (WDDM pages VRAM). The one cited loss rate predates CSM-off and the atlas fix. Until the soak in ledger-open 292 shows losses tracking uploaded texture bytes, the expected gain is unestimable.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Retail purges thrashable GPU resources unused for more than 120 s when VRAM is low and restores them on use. Holtburger keeps every handed-out cache-material texture uploaded for the whole session (matBudgetMB never disposes handed-out entries). It already does a GPU-only dispose with CPU data kept, but only for paletted textures under a byte budget (palBudgetMB). An age-triggered dispose-and-keep-data purge of non-atlas textures with CPU data present is a plausible VRAM lever, but whether it would reduce context losses is unproven. Run the owed context-loss soak first (ledger-open 292).

verdicts.code_truth:
Confirmed: _fireTier1Cue (play_effect_vfx.js:3674-3687, called at :3600) resolves the placement and calls fireFxCue and fireFxShowcaseCue with no distance or cell test. fireFxCue (fx_cues.js:103-145) spawns the flash, shockwave and decal unconditionally. spawnFxFlash evicts the oldest flash at FLASH_MAX = 10 (fx_lights.js:203, 291-295), and spawnFxShockwave evicts at SHOCK_MAX (fx_distort.js:77-86). The retail threshold is correct: CPhysicsPart::GetMaxDegradeDistance defaults to 100 m (acclient.c:314372-314381), and ShouldDrawParticles is at :317184.

The visual claim is overstated. A flash only registers into the light pool within REGISTER_RADIUS = 48 m (fx_lights.js:204). collectFxDistortSources fades rings with `k *= 1 - clamp((depth-60)/60)`, which reaches zero at 120 m depth (fx_distort.js:152-153). So beyond ~100 m the flash already lights nothing and the ring is nearly or fully faded; only the decal is a visible 'lone' element.

The cell half is weak on retail grounds: wall #8 says CObjCell::IsInView returns 1 for EnvCells (only CLandCell overrides it, :354835), so retail does not hide interior particles by cell.
verdicts.novelty: Advance on ledger-open 154 ('_fireTier1Cue fires flash/shockwave/decal at ANY distance | WHY-OPEN: Unverified reviewer lead; far cues compete for 10-flash/8-shockwave caps'). The cap-competition point is already in the lead. The finder adds the code verification and a threshold. No fxCueRange flag exists.

verdicts.visual_safety: Within range it is pixel-identical. Beyond range, skipping the flash past 48 m plus its range, and the ring past 120 m, is pixel-identical today, because neither shows. Only skipping the decal changes pixels: an improvement or neutral, but owner-visible.
verdicts.gain_realism: Small. The cost of far cues is mainly slot competition: FLASH_MAX 10, SHOCK_MAX and FX_DECAL_MAX transient eviction in big fights or town spell spam, plus far decal draws. The CPU/draw saving is negligible, as the finder also says.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Verified: _fireTier1Cue and fireFxCue have no range or cell gate. Far flashes, however, already light nothing beyond 48 m (REGISTER_RADIUS), and rings fade to zero by 120 m (fx_distort.js:152-153). The real effects are far cues taking flash, ring and decal cap slots from near ones (already named in ledger-open 154) and far decals. A pixel-identical gate needs no 100 m retail figure: skip the flash beyond 48 m plus its range, skip the ring beyond 120 m, and skip the decal beyond ~100 m (degrade distance) behind ?fxCueRange. The EnvCell gate is a holtburger choice, not retail (wall #8).

findings.title: ClipMap cutouts get dark edges and darken at distance: clip texels decode to black RGB, and the opaque ClipMap path has no blend to hide it
findings.evidence:
WHAT THE DECODE WRITES:
- crates/holtburger-dat/src/file_type/texture.rs:391-394 and :426-429 emit RGBA(0,0,0,0) for paletted ClipMap texels with idx<8. Retail does the same: acclient.c:365907 ImgTex::CopyIntoData writes DWORD 0.
- bc7_textures.js:2270-2274 records that one real grass key has 9,516 of 16,384 texels at alpha 0, all with black RGB.

HOW THE GPU THEN TREATS THEM:
- adapter.js:1136-1184 surfacePixelsToTexture uploads this straight-alpha RGBA8 with generateMipmaps=true and LinearMipmapLinear, so the GPU averages the black texels into every mip.
- static_atlas.js:335-353 buildDiffuseArray copies the same img.data into the atlas arrays, also with generateMipmaps.

WHY RETAIL HAD NO DARK EDGE:
- materials.js:2424-2446 documents retail's ClipMap state: alpha test >= ref, then BLEND ONE/INVSRCALPHA, i.e. premultiplied 'over'.
- With black clip texels, retail's filtered edge texel (a*C, a) blends to a*C + (1-a)*dst, which is a correct soft edge.

WHAT HOLTBURGER DOES INSTEAD:
- materials.js:2611-2627: since ?clipMapOpaque the surface stays opaque with blending dropped ('Blending is deliberately NOT set').
- So the surviving edge or mip fragment writes a*C with nothing behind it.
- Paletted refs are 100/255, so an edge fragment can carry up to 61% black; DDS refs are 200/255, up to 22% black.
- The census at materials.js:2449-2451: 721 ClipMap surfaces, 518 of them paletted.

WHERE THIS PATH IS ON SCREEN:
- The recoloured-entity decode always uses it (lib.rs:17725-17726, to_rgba8_clipmap).
- Static surfaces use it before their HD upgrade and beyond texUpgradeFullM.
- Low-bandwidth sessions use it always.

THE SERVED BC7 LANES:
- bc7_textures.js:2284-2286: the texfix-fringe re-encode of the xu7 corpus (2026-08-09) was never re-ingested into the served dist.
- The tex-bc7 lane those clip rows fall back to was encoded 07-31, before that repair.
- So the BC7 lanes very likely carry the same black-under-clip RGB.
findings.proposal:
RUST CHANGE (holtburger-dat):
- Add `dilate_clip_rgb(rgba: &mut [u8], w, h)`: a multi-source BFS, or push-pull, from the texels with a>0 into the a==0 texels.
- It writes only RGB and leaves alpha untouched. It wraps at the edges, because most AC textures repeat.
- Call it at the end of `to_rgba8_impl` when `clipmap && paletted`.
- Call it from the surface decode in lib.rs:14944 and :17726 for every pure-ClipMap surface: surface_type&0x4 set and not Translucent (0x10) or Alpha (0x100), to keep the blended 0x14 arm retail-exact.

WHAT IT FIXES:
- Texels with a>0 stay byte-identical, so the interior and the cutout silhouette do not change.
- Only bilinear edge samples and the GPU-generated mips change: they now average real foliage or creature colour instead of black.
- The atlas arrays inherit the fix automatically.

FLAG: `?clipDilate` (DEFAULT ON per the owner's validated-gate rule; `=off` escape) as a wasm-side boolean, or an export arg checked once.

BAKE SIDE (orchestrator): re-ingest the already-repaired xu7 corpus, and re-encode tex-bc7/tex-bc7-pre clip rows with the same push-pull, so the HD lanes match.
findings.expected_gain: Removes a dark rim around every pure-ClipMap cutout (up to 61% darkening on paletted, 22% on DDS; derived from the alpha refs) and the progressive darkening of foliage and clip creature parts at distance (mip texels at 50% coverage currently show 0.5*C). No fps cost: a single O(texels) pass in wasm per surface decode, run in the bake worker.
findings.novelty_check:
- Ledger: rg 'fring|halo|dilat|premult|clipmap' finds only texfix-fringe (ledger-compact:822), which repaired the Remacri CORPUS offline. The runtime retail-resolution RGBA8 decode and the GPU mips are untouched.
- bc7_textures.js:2284-2286 itself says the repaired xu7 corpus was never re-ingested; that is not in the ledger either.
- git log 'fringe|dilat|clipmap' shows the ClipMap ref/blend/opaque work (244a0fde, f712c13f, 494b1aea) and the corpus repair (b03bf204); none of them touches decode RGB.
- url-flags: no clipDilate.
- Walls 117/144 respected: alpha, ref and pass are unchanged.
findings.verify_how:
- Rust unit test (orchestrator runs a targeted `cargo test -p holtburger-dat dilate`): every a>0 texel byte-identical; no a==0 texel keeps RGB 0 when an opaque texel exists.
- Node probe on real data: decode 0x0600385A, box-filter to mip 2, and compare the mean RGB of texels that pass 100/255 before and after; the 'before' should show roughly a*C darkening.
- 1070 eye test: Holtburg tree line at 30-150 m and a paletted clip doll/Virindi, with ?clipDilate=off vs default.

findings.title: Alpha-to-coverage for opaque ClipMap surfaces when the world target is MSAA (soft cutout edges close to retail's blended edge, no sort cost)
findings.evidence:
TODAY:
- index.js:868-879: msaaSampleCount() defaults to 2.
- atmosphere_pipeline.js:1186-1220: ?msaaWorldOnly is on by default, so samples live on the world target that every scene pass draws into.
- materials.js:2611-2627: pure ClipMap surfaces are opaque alpha-test (ref 0.392/0.784) with blending dropped. Their edges are per-pixel hard cuts that MSAA cannot smooth, because every sample gets the same discard.
- Retail softened that same edge with ONE/INVSRCALPHA (materials.js:2436-2441).

WHAT THREE r184 PROVIDES:
- The A2C variant: three.module.js:305 (`diffuseColor.a = smoothstep(alphaTest, alphaTest + fwidth(a), a)`, discarding only below the ref, so the silhouette never grows), :10415-10417 (SAMPLE_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE) and :7585 (program bit).

CAVEATS FOUND IN CODE:
- three.module.js:7634: A2C materials lose the OPAQUE define, so fractional alpha reaches the HDR buffer, and the canvas is alpha:true + premultiplied (shader_logdepth.js:256-262; three.module.js:16308-16309 always requests alpha:true). ssao_marker.js:5-9 records that an alpha below 1 shows the page through the canvas. So A2C needs visuals-3 first.
- three.module.js:9518: the shadow pass substitutes alphaTest 0.5 for A2C materials. This only matters with ?csm=on.
- static_array_pool.js:347-352 rejects alphaToCoverage.
- static_atlas.js:534-575: _stateKeyOf/_applyStateKey do not carry it.
findings.proposal:
COMPUTE A2C IN ONE PLACE:
- A2C = (alphaTest > 0 && transparent === false && sessionMsaaSamples > 0 && clipA2CEnabled()).
- Apply it in applyClipMapRenderState (materials.js:2611 branch; it already covers entities.js:6810 and materials.js:2178).
- Apply it in static_atlas._applyStateKey, derived from the key's existing transparent/alphaTest fields, so the key does not change and buckets do not fragment.
- Apply it in static_array_pool replication, replacing the reject at :348 with the same derivation.
- static_batch_x value-keying already enumerates the property.

RULES:
- Never set it on transparent materials; that keeps 0x14 Translucent+ClipMap untouched (wall 117).
- Never set it when msaa=0.

FLAG: `?clipA2C` (default OFF until the 1070 eye test, then ON), with visuals-3 as a hard prerequisite.
findings.expected_gain: Visual: foliage, fence, wrought-iron and hair cutout edges go from 1-bit stair-steps to 2-level (msaa 2) or 4-level (msaa 4) coverage. Edge shimmer in motion drops, and the look moves toward retail's blended edge. fps: about neutral, assumed. A2C is free in hardware, fwidth is a few ALU, and the pass, sort and draw count do not change (one-time program variant per ClipMap material).
findings.novelty_check:
- Ledger and walls: rg 'alpha.?to.?coverage|A2C|coverage' returns no A2C item.
- url-flags.md:827 mentions alphaToCoverage only as a merge-key property inside statBatchValueKey.
- git log 'coverage|alphaToCoverage': nothing relevant.
- Brushes walls 117/144 (ClipMap is structural): this keeps the existing clipMapOpaque predicate and adds no new class.
findings.verify_how:
- Node tests: the A2C derivation (only opaque alphaTest>0, only with msaa>0); static_atlas/static_array_pool replicate it without changing the state key; clipMapOpaque tests unchanged.
- 1070 eye test: tree canopies and fences at 10-60 m, msaa 2 and 4, with ?clipA2C=on/off. Also check NVIDIA's A2C dither pattern is acceptable.
- hbbench --uncapped pair to confirm the cost is about 0.

findings.title: Create the WebGL context opaque (alpha:false) so nothing can show the page through the canvas; this also unblocks A2C
findings.evidence:
THE CONTEXT IS TRANSLUCENT TODAY:
- three.module.js:16308-16309: three r184 always creates its context with `alpha: true`.
- shader_logdepth.js:249-262: holtburger's probe copies that (alpha:true, premultipliedAlpha:true) so it creates the very context three gets back.
- three.module.js:16044-16050: three accepts a pre-made context and then reads `_alpha` from its attributes, so an opaque context is supported.

THE HAZARD IS REAL:
- ssao_marker.js:5-9: the grass writes alpha 0 as an AO marker, and 'an unrestored 0 would show the page through the grass'. ssao.js:295-297 restores it.
- index.html:149: the page body has no dark background outside agent-mode (only `html.agent-mode body` is #000 at :457), so any alpha below 1 leaks page colour into the frame.
- Any fractional-alpha writer, such as A2C (visuals-2) or a future effect, re-opens that class.

NO RELIANCE FOUND: rg found no code that relies on canvas transparency. The clear is 0x101418 at alpha 1 (index.js:1463).
findings.proposal:
- In shader_logdepth.js threeContextAttributes, set alpha:false.
- Always create the context through probeClipControl/getContext before `new THREE.WebGLRenderer` (today the probe only runs when reversedZ is requested), or pass it as `context:` explicitly. three then takes `_alpha=false` and clears with alpha 1.
- Flag: `?canvasAlpha=on` as the escape back to alpha:true. Default: opaque.
- Keep the SSAO alpha restore as belt-and-braces.
findings.expected_gain: Pixel-identical wherever the final alpha is 1 today, and a fix wherever it is not. The whole 'page shows through' bug class goes away, and visuals-2 becomes safe. A small GPU-process bonus is possible: Chrome can treat the full-viewport canvas layer as opaque, with no blend and no drawing of the page background under it. That is assumed, not measured; expect it well under 0.2 ms, since CrGpuMain is mostly WebGL decode and HUD raster.
findings.novelty_check:
- Ledger and walls: rg 'alpha: ?false|opaque canvas|canvas alpha|context attribute' returns nothing.
- git log: nothing.
- url-flags: no canvasAlpha or opaqueCanvas.
- Related but distinct: canvasDepth (depth attribute only) and canvasMsaa (antialias attribute).
findings.verify_how:
- Node test: threeContextAttributes().alpha === false, and the probe runs unconditionally.
- GPU smoke page: gl.getContextAttributes().alpha === false, and a readPixels of the canvas after a frame returns alpha 255 everywhere. Then force SSAO_GRASS_MARKER without the composite and confirm no page bleed.
- 1070: a gpu_thread_split.py A/B can look for a compositor delta (optional).

findings.title: Speech bubbles are drawn in the world pass, so clouds, layered haze, SSAO and ground decals are applied using the depth behind them, and late particles draw over them
findings.evidence:
THE BUBBLE MATERIAL:
- speech_bubble.js:20-21: bubbles have been always-on since 2026-06-10 (eye-tested then, before cloudsMainPass and particlesOverClouds existed).
- speech_bubble.js:138-147: SpriteMaterial with depthTest:false, depthWrite:false, toneMapped:false. toneMapped is inert inside the composer, because tone mapping is a post effect over the whole buffer.

WHAT HAPPENS TO IT IN THE POST CHAIN:
- Because it writes no depth, every depth-driven post effect treats a bubble pixel as whatever lies behind it.
- atmosphere_pipeline.js:1848-1879 split chain (clouds at high/ultra): cloudsMain + aerialPerspective composite clouds over sky-depth pixels. This is exactly the bug particles_over_clouds.js:7-18 documents and fixed for particles ('clouds are over particle effect').
- Layered haze (layered_haze.js:11-21, default 0.4, depth-based) hazes the bubble by the distance of the hills behind it.
- The ssaoComposite and fxDecals effects in the same chain decode the same background depth.

ORDERING AND REACH:
- Late particles (ParticlesOverCloudsPass, atmosphere_pipeline.js:676-720) are drawn after the world pass, so smoke or a portal swirl BEHIND an NPC now paints over its bubble.
- The fix mechanism already exists: collectLateFx (particles_over_clouds.js:211-238) accepts unlit materials, and SpriteMaterial passes materialNeedsLights. play_effect_vfx.js:624, fx_ribbons.js:405 and fx_showcase.js:498 register this way. speech_bubble.js does not.

NO MIPMAPS:
- speech_bubble.js:133-135 sets LinearFilter with generateMipmaps=false, at 128 px/m (:31).
- At the ~53.6 deg retail FOV and 1080p, a bubble at 20-40 m is minified about 2.4-4.8x (derived: 128 / (1069/d)), so the text crawls with no mips.
findings.proposal:
- In speech_bubble.js keep a module Set of live bubble sprites (add in showSpeechBubbleOnEntity, delete in disposeBubble).
- Register them: `registerLateFxSource(out => { for (const s of _live) out.push(s); })`. Import from the zero-dependency particles_over_clouds.js.
- The late pass then draws bubbles after clouds, aerial perspective and haze, sorted after particles by renderOrder 11. It uses the same Fog object, and its depthTest:false is unaffected.
- Also set texture.generateMipmaps = true and minFilter = LinearMipmapLinearFilter; WebGL2 mips NPOT canvases.
- The same registration can cover the opt-in sprite nameplates (nameplate_sprite.js).
- Flag: `?bubbleLate` (default ON; `=off` escape).
findings.expected_gain: Bubbles against the sky stop being overpainted by volumetric cloud at high/ultra. Bubbles against distant hills stop getting the hills' haze (up to about 17% wash at 1 km; derived from LAYER_HAZE_DEFAULTS) and stop picking up AO or decals. Smoke and portal particles stop covering the text, and distant text stops shimmering. CPU: one tiny extra push per live bubble per frame (usually 0-3).
findings.novelty_check:
- Ledger: rg 'speech|bubble|nameplate' finds only HearRangedSpeech range, nameplate batching and the nameplate VRAM leak; no post-chain or late-pass item.
- SKY-1 and particlesOverClouds (ledger-compact) fixed particles only. This is the same mechanism on a different, always-on object.
- git log 'speech|bubble': only e6fcface (the feature).
- url-flags: speechBubbles row only.
findings.verify_how:
- Node test: with a bubble shown, collectLateFx(out, scene, mask) contains the sprite, and after disposal it does not.
- SwiftShader cannot show clouds (wall 101). A headless screenshot can still show a particle emitter behind an NPC no longer covering its bubble.
- 1070 eye test: an NPC speaking against a cloudy sky at high, with ?bubbleLate=off vs default.

findings.title: Toksvig-style specular anti-aliasing for glossy normal-mapped materials (metal category: roughness 0.3, metalness 0.9)
findings.evidence:
WHY SPARKLE IS LIKELY:
- materials.js:514-533: the Metal category gets roughness 0.3, metalness 0.9 and normalScale 0.6.
- quality.js:110/309/423/527: normalMaps is on in every preset.
- normal_gen.rs:69-105: normal maps are a high-frequency Sobel of luminance.
- adapter.js:1186-1240: they are uploaded as mipmapped RGBA8 (generateMipmaps true), so the GPU averages them and the filtered vector shortens wherever normals diverge.
- three.module.js:443 normal_fragment_maps immediately does `normalize(tbn * mapN)`, which throws that variance away.
- three.module.js:399: lights_physical adds geometryRoughness from the non-perturbed normal only.
- Result: glossy metal (armour, weapons on per-entity MeshStandard materials) keeps a tight lobe on minified normal maps. That is the classic specular-sparkle setup, which MSAA does not touch.

WHY THE CHUNK PATCH WORKS:
- roughnessFactor is declared earlier in the same program (three.module.js:473), so it can be adjusted inside the normal chunk.

CAVEAT: atlas statics use packed RG normals with reconstructed z (static_atlas.js:790-794), which discards the length information, and the atlas drops metalness. So this mainly reaches entities and non-atlas statics.
findings.proposal:
- Install once, like installRadialFog/installLightLoops: patch ShaderChunk.normal_fragment_maps in the USE_NORMALMAP_TANGENTSPACE branch, guarded by `#ifdef STANDARD`.
- Keep the raw filtered texel `vec3 hbRaw = texture2D(normalMap, vNormalMapUv).xyz*2.0-1.0`.
- `float hbLen = clamp(length(hbRaw), 1e-3, 1.0)`.
- `roughnessFactor = sqrt(clamp(roughnessFactor*roughnessFactor + (1.0-hbLen)/hbLen, 0.0, 1.0))`.
- Then the stock normalize path continues unchanged.
- Flag: `?specAA` (default OFF until the eye test). The off-form leaves the chunk byte-identical.
findings.expected_gain: Less specular crawl and sparkle on armoured characters and metal props at 10-40 m in sun, with the camera moving. It changes only minified, divergent normal-map texels, so near-field surfaces are about identical. fps: a few ALU per lit fragment, about neutral. One program-key change at first compile only. Assumed, not measured.

findings.title: Far composite ring stores linear albedo in 8-bit UNorm; storing it as SRGB8_ALPHA8 gives about 3x finer dark-tone precision at the same memory
findings.evidence:
- far_terrain.js:887-913: the patch RT is created without `type`, so it is UnsignedByte, with colorSpace NoColorSpace and mipmapped.
- terrain.js:4060: the bake writes `modulated`, the linear albedo, since the atlas is SRGB-decoded (terrain.js:4542).
- far_terrain.js:507: the far shader reads `texture(uComposite).rgb` as linear albedo, and then applies the same Gouraud, paint light and lighting as the near ring.
- three.module.js:7584: render-target programs output linear, with no shader encode.
- three.module.js:11226: an RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE target with an sRGB colour space allocates SRGB8_ALPHA8, which the hardware encodes on write, decodes on sample and mip-filters in linear.
- Precision (derived): linear 8-bit at albedo 0.03 has about 6.5% relative step; sRGB storage gives about 1.9%.
findings.proposal:
- Pass `colorSpace: THREE.SRGBColorSpace` in the patch RT options (far_terrain.js:907-913).
- Nothing else changes. uComposite is the only consumer (far_terrain.js:1077), the far shader already treats samples as linear, and SRGB8_ALPHA8 is colour-renderable and filterable, so generateMipmap is legal (ANGLE maps it to R8G8B8A8_UNORM_SRGB).
- Flag: `?farCompositeSrgb` (default ON, `=off` escape).
findings.expected_gain: Less quantisation and blotching in dark far-ring albedo (forest floor, volcanic, dusk) and a closer colour match at the near/far handoff. Memory and fps are unchanged. Small, because the inner far ring at about 1.05-1.25 km is only lightly fogged and texture noise dithers most of it.
findings.novelty_check:
- Ledger: rg 'srgb|banding|quantiz|8-bit' finds nothing for the far composite.
- git log 'srgb|colorspace': only eb687115 (light colours).
- Far-ring open leads (FARCRIT-3, mountain fog silhouettes) are different.
findings.verify_how:
- Node test: the patch RT texture colorSpace is SRGB.
- glcensus or a GPU smoke page (test_far_bake_shared_textures_gpu.html pattern): internal format SRGB8_ALPHA8 with 10 mip levels and no GL errors after a bake.
- 1070 snap pair of a dusk far-ring vista, ?farCompositeSrgb=off vs default.

verdicts.code_truth:
Every citation holds at HEAD.
- texture.rs:391-394 (P8) and :426-429 (Index16): for `clipmap && idx < 8` the decoder pushes `[0,0,0,0]`.
- lib.rs:14944 and :17725-17726: both compute `clipmap = (surface_type & 0x4) != 0` and pass it into the decode.
- adapter.js:1136-1184 surfacePixelsToTexture: SRGBColorSpace, LinearMipmapLinear, generateMipmaps=true.
- static_atlas.js:340-356 buildDiffuseArray copies img.data into the array, also with generateMipmaps.
- materials.js:2424-2451: retail ONE/INVSRCALPHA blend, refs 100/255 and 200/255, census 721/518.
- materials.js:2611-2627: the clipMapOpaque branch sets transparent=false, depthWrite=true and no blend.
- bc7_textures.js:2262-2286: the reed key has 9,516 of 16,384 texels at alpha 0, and the xu7 corpus was never re-ingested.
- So the dark-rim mechanism is real. In the opaque path a bilinear edge sample is (t*C, t), passes at t>=0.392 and outputs t*C with no blend behind it. GPU mips average the black clip texels in the same way.

The proposal's safety claim is WRONG as written. The finder wants the dilation at the end of to_rgba8_impl, but lib.rs:14967-14991 feeds that same `pixels` buffer to three other consumers:
- compute_stats (surface_classify.rs:131-170): a plain unweighted mean, std-dev and hue over every texel, alpha ignored. For the reed, 58% of its texels are black, so filling them moves luminance, saturation and hue, and can flip the surface category. The category sets roughness, metalness and normalScale for the whole material (materials.js:4987-4992).
- normal_and_height_pixels: the Sobel normals and POM heights at edge texels change.
- So 'texels with a>0 stay byte-identical, interior unchanged' does not hold for shading.
verdicts.novelty:
New for the runtime retail-resolution RGBA8 decode and its GPU mips.
- texfix-fringe (ledger-compact:822, b03bf204) repaired only the offline Remacri corpus.
- git log and url-flags have nothing on runtime dilation; the only alpha-weighted code is rgba_pixel_mean at lib.rs:7427, which is unrelated.
- The BAKE half is NOT new. texfix-fringe-2026-08-09.md 'Propagation debts' #1-#2 already records that the dist full tier and the packs need a re-bake against the repaired ingest, and bc7_textures.js:2284-2286 says the same. The ledger lacks it, but the debt is documented.
verdicts.wall_conflict:
- Walls 117/144: alpha, ref and pass are unchanged, so the structural rule is respected only if the dilation runs AFTER compute_stats and the normal/height derivation (or those read the undilated buffer). As written it changes material category, roughness and normals, which is a look change that needs an eye test.
- Wall 101: SwiftShader cannot judge the result.
verdicts.visual_safety:
- With the reorder (dilate only the albedo buffer handed to JS, after stats/normals/heights), it is an improvement: the silhouette is identical and edge and mip samples become C instead of t*C.
- Hidden regressions in the proposal as written: category flips (roughness 0.3-0.95, metalness 0/0.9) and changed Sobel edge relief.
- Escape-path regression: under ?clipMapOpaque=off the retail ONE/INVSRCALPHA blend needs black (premultiplied-equivalent) clip RGB. Dilated RGB would add C + (1-t)*dst, an over-bright halo. The dilation must be gated on the opaque path.
verdicts.gain_realism:
Visual only, and narrower than claimed on the owner's ultra/1070 setup:
- Within 32 m, static foliage is replaced by the xu7/tex-bc7 HD lanes. Beyond 32 m the in-view tex-bc7-pre record takes over (tex_upgrade_queue.js:22-35). Both lanes have baked RGB and mips that a runtime fix cannot touch.
- Runtime reach: the recoloured-entity path (always), statics before their upgrade lands, ?bandwidth=low, and ?texBc7=off.
- The '61% darker' figure is in linear light; perceptually about a third darker at the edge.
- Cost: a negligible O(texels) pass. The entity recolour decode most likely runs on the main thread, not the bake worker (not checked here).
verdicts.corrected_claim:
Paletted ClipMap texels decode to RGBA 0, so on the default opaque ClipMap path (clipMapOpaque, no blend) bilinear edge samples and GPU mips render t*C. That is a dark rim (up to 61% in linear light at the 100/255 ref) and darkening at distance, which retail hid with ONE/INVSRCALPHA.

A runtime RGB dilation of a==0 texels fixes the RGBA8 path (entities, statics before their upgrade, low bandwidth) only if:
- it is applied after compute_stats and normal_and_height_pixels (or to a copy handed to JS), so category, roughness and normals stay identical;
- it is gated to the opaque path, so the ?clipMapOpaque=off retail-blend escape keeps black clip RGB.

The HD-lane half is the already-recorded texfix propagation debt (re-ingest xu7, re-encode tex-bc7/-pre clip rows with dilated RGB and mips).

verdicts.code_truth:
Citations are accurate.
- three.module.js:16308-16309 (src WebGLRenderer.js:369) hard-codes `alpha: true` in the context request. The constructor `alpha` param (default false) only sets the default clear alpha: WebGLBackground :1316 `clearAlpha = alpha === true ? 0 : 1`.
- :16044-16050 reads `_alpha` from a pre-made context.
- shader_logdepth.js:256-266 threeContextAttributes copies alpha:true and premultipliedAlpha:true.
- index.js:1463 setClearColor(0x101418, 1).
- ssao_marker.js:5-9 and ssao.js:291-296 restore the grass marker alpha.
- index.html:149: body has no dark background outside agent-mode.

No present-day leak was found. I checked the blend factors used in scene3d (ibl_environment.js, fx_decal_effect.js and static_array_pool.js only replicate them). Under the clear alpha of 1, nothing in the world pass lowers destination alpha, and postprocessing 6.39.1 and the takram passes take the `alpha` init flag without branching on it.

Minor correction: the probe already runs by default, because reversedZ is ON (index.js:1243-1247), so 'always run the probe' only matters for =off.

The three docs describe `alpha` only as the default clear alpha (https://threejs.org/docs/pages/WebGLRenderer.html). Upstream's reason for hard-coding alpha:true in the context is not stated in the source.
verdicts.novelty: New. Nothing in the ledgers, git log or url-flags for canvas alpha, opaque canvas or context alpha. The related flags canvasDepth and canvasMsaa cover other attributes.
verdicts.wall_conflict:
- Wall 101 / perf walls 83/86: the compositor or GPU-process 'bonus' is unmeasured and can only be measured on the 1070 with gpu_thread_split.py.
- It also departs from a deliberate upstream three choice: alpha:true is always requested regardless of the param.
verdicts.visual_safety: Pixel-identical today, since every frame already ends at alpha 1. It only changes pixels where alpha would otherwise be below 1, which is a fix. The only other alpha:true renderers are the paperdoll and dye viewports, which are separate canvases and renderers and are unaffected.
verdicts.gain_realism:
- Today it is a defensive fix: no current writer leaks alpha below 1 to the canvas.
- The claimed CrGpuMain or compositor saving is speculative, and its sign on Chrome/ANGLE-D3D11 is unknown. three upstream deliberately requests alpha:true regardless of the param, so an alpha:false context is a less-travelled path.
- Expect about 0 ms, unproven.
- Its main value is as one way to unblock visuals-2; a final-pass alpha=1 write is a cheaper, zero-platform-risk alternative.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Creating the main context with alpha:false would make page-bleed through the canvas impossible and is pixel-identical today. But no current leak exists: SSAO restores the grass marker, the clear alpha is 1, and the blend modes in use keep destination alpha at 1. The performance effect on ANGLE/D3D11 is unknown in sign and needs a 1070 gpu_thread_split A/B. For the A2C prerequisite, forcing alpha=1 in the final post pass is the lower-risk option.

verdicts.wall_conflict:
- Extends wall 62 / SKY-1 (depthWrite:false objects vs depth-based post) to an object that fix missed.

verdicts.visual_safety:
An improvement:
- Bubbles stop being covered by volumetric cloud when the sky is behind them (the split chain at high/ultra); an opaque cloud currently replaces the bubble pixel outright.
- They no longer take the haze, AO or decals of the geometry behind them.
- Late particles no longer cover them, given the renderOrder fix.
- Exposure, bloom and tone mapping still apply, since the late pass is still pre-tone-map HDR, so brightness is unchanged.
- Mipmapping a canvas with an opaque-ish black backdrop is safe; distant text becomes stable rather than crawling.
verdicts.gain_realism: A visual-only correctness fix for an always-on HUD-in-world element. CPU cost is negligible: 0-3 extra pushes per frame and one mip generation per utterance.
verdicts.corrected_claim:
Speech-bubble sprites (depthTest/depthWrite off, always-on) are drawn in the world pass. So on the split chain at high/ultra, cloud + aerial perspective composite over them wherever sky is behind, and layered haze, SSAO and fxDecals shade them by the depth behind them. Late-pass particles and bursts paint over them, and their un-mipmapped canvas text aliases at 20-40 m.

The fix: register live bubbles with registerLateFxSource (the existing particles_over_clouds mechanism), use renderOrder above 950 so bursts (play_effect_vfx.js:676) do not overpaint them, and enable mipmaps on the bubble texture.

verdicts.corrected_claim: The far composite RT stores linear albedo in RGBA8 UNorm. Tagging it SRGBColorSpace makes three allocate SRGB8_ALPHA8, which gives about 3.4x finer dark-tone steps at the same memory, with no shader or program-key change.
